teile.einleitung: Martina Hingis is a former Swiss tennis player and one of Switzerland’s most successful sportswomen. At just 16 she became world number 1. She won five Grand Slam tournaments in singles and many titles in doubles.
wichtigste: Martina Hingis was born in 1980 in Košice in what was then Czechoslovakia.
She grew up in Trübbach in the canton of St Gallen.
Her mother, Melanie Molitor, was her coach.
In 1997, at 16, she became world number 1.
She won five Grand Slam tournaments in singles.
In 2016 she won silver in the doubles at the Olympic Games in Rio.
In 2017 she ended her career as number 1 in doubles.

abschnitte.text: Martina Hingis was born on 30 September 1980 in **Košice**, which is now in Slovakia. Her mother named her after the famous tennis player Martina Navratilova. As a child she moved with her mother to Switzerland, to **Trübbach** in the St Gallen Rhine valley. Even as a small child she played tennis almost every day.

Hingis was a real **child prodigy**. At twelve she won the junior girls’ tournament in Paris. In March 1997, at 16, she became the youngest world **number 1**. Her game was not especially powerful, but very clever and precise.

The four **Grand Slam tournaments** are the most important tournaments in tennis. In 1997 Hingis won the Australian Open, Wimbledon and the US Open. In 1998 and 1999 she won in Australia again. The only one she never managed to win in singles was the tournament in Paris.

Hingis was also one of the best in **doubles** and mixed doubles. She returned to the tour several times after injuries and won many more doubles titles. In 2016 in Rio she won silver in the doubles with Timea Bacsinszky. In 2017 she ended her career for good.

Martina Hingis made tennis very popular in Switzerland, even before Roger Federer. In 2013 she was inducted into the **International Tennis Hall of Fame**. This hall of fame honours the best players in history. Many young Swiss players see her as a role model.

begriffe.erklaerung: The four most important tennis tournaments: Melbourne, Paris, Wimbledon and New York.
A list that shows who is playing best at the moment.
A match with two players on each side of the net.
A child who can do something exceptionally well at a very young age.

gewusst: At 16 Martina Hingis won the Wimbledon singles, making her one of the youngest winners.
Martina Hingis was named after Martina Navratilova, one of the best tennis players of all time.

teile.einleitung: Something is fair when everyone has the same chances and keeps to the rules. Fairness is important in games, in sport and wherever people do things together.
wichtigste: Fair means: the same rules and the same chances for everyone.
In a fair race everyone starts at the same time.
Fair behaviour in sport is called **fair play**.
Rolling dice gives everyone the same chance.
A foul is a breach of the rules of the game.
Fair winners stay friendly.

abschnitte.text: In a **race** everyone should set off at the same time. Anyone who starts too early gains an **unfair advantage**. That is not fair on the others. That is why there is a starting signal, for example ‘Ready, steady, go!’. That way everyone has the same chance of winning.

Sometimes you have to decide who goes first in a game. You can do this fairly, for example by **rolling a die**. When you roll a die, every child has the same chance. You can also toss a coin or say a counting-out rhyme. What matters is that nobody is favoured.

In sport, fair behaviour is called **fair play**. It means keeping to the rules and respecting your opponent. A **foul** is a breach of the rules, for example tripping someone up. There is a penalty for it, such as a free kick or a yellow card. The **referee** makes sure that everyone plays fairly.

Fair does not always mean that everyone does exactly the same thing. If a child cannot run because of a **plaster cast**, they can take on another job, for example timing or keeping score. That way they can still **join in**. It is fair when everyone can take part.

Whoever wins is happy. But a **fair winner** stays friendly and does not laugh at anyone. Whoever loses may be disappointed. A **good loser** still congratulates the winner. After a game people often shake hands. That way the fun lasts for everyone.

gewusst: In football there is the yellow card as a warning and the red card for sending a player off.
At many sporting events there is a special prize for especially fair behaviour.

teile.einleitung: People are different: they speak different languages and have different skin colours, abilities and ideas. This diversity makes living together exciting. What matters is that everyone belongs and nobody is left out.
wichtigste: All people are of equal worth, whatever they look like.
In Switzerland many families speak another language at home.
Because people are different, we can learn a lot from each other.
If you do not let someone join in just because they are different, you are excluding them.
If someone is deliberately picked on again and again, it is called bullying.
A prejudice is a fixed opinion about others before you know them.

abschnitte.text: No person is exactly like another. Some are tall, others small; some have light skin, others dark. **Skin colour** says nothing about what a person is like. All people are of **equal worth**. Different people have different ideas and abilities. That way we can **learn a lot from each other**.

Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. On top of that there are many other languages that families speak at home. If a child speaks another language at home, that is **completely normal**. Being able to speak several languages is a **treasure**. Perhaps a child in your class can teach you a few words in their language.

Some children use a **wheelchair**, cannot hear or see well, or need more time to learn. With a bit of imagination you can find games in which **everyone can join in**. For example, you can throw a ball instead of running, or choose a board game. Nobody should be left out. If you belong, you feel at ease and can show what you can do.

If someone is not allowed to join in just because they are different, this is called **exclusion**. It hurts and is unfair, because every child wants to belong. If someone is deliberately picked on or left out over a long time, that is **bullying**. Then you must tell adults, for example the teacher. Exclusion often starts with a **prejudice**: a fixed opinion about a group without knowing the people. Usually such a judgement is not true.

gewusst: Switzerland has four national languages, and in many school classes even more languages are spoken.
There are sports such as wheelchair basketball in which people with and without disabilities can play together.

teile.einleitung: Yann Sommer is a Swiss football goalkeeper. He played for Borussia Mönchengladbach for a long time and later moved to Inter Milan. He became famous at Euro 2021, when he saved Kylian Mbappé’s penalty against France.
wichtigste: Yann Sommer was born on 17 December 1988 in Morges in the canton of Vaud.
He plays as a goalkeeper.
His career began at FC Basel.
From 2014 to 2023 he played for Borussia Mönchengladbach in Germany.
At Euro 2021 he saved Kylian Mbappé’s shot in the penalty shootout against France.
After Euro 2024 he retired from the national team.

abschnitte.text: Yann Sommer was born in **Morges** on Lake Geneva and grew up in the Basel area. He speaks German and French. Even as a child he wanted to be in goal. He is rather small for a goalkeeper, but he makes up for it with speed and good reflexes.

Sommer played his first professional matches at **FC Basel** and became Swiss champion with the club several times. In 2014 he moved to **Borussia Mönchengladbach** in the German Bundesliga. There he was the number 1 in goal for almost nine years. At the beginning of 2023 he moved to Bayern Munich and became German champion there.

In the summer of 2023 Sommer went to **Inter Milan** in Italy. In his very first season he became Italian champion with Inter. He was one of the best goalkeepers in the league. In the Italian Serie A he is seen as a very reliable last line of defence.

At **Euro 2021** Switzerland played world champions France in the round of 16 in Bucharest. The match ended 3:3 after extra time and went to a **penalty shootout**. Yann Sommer saved the last penalty from superstar Kylian Mbappé. That put Switzerland into the quarter-finals of a big tournament for the first time in many decades.

Besides football, Yann Sommer likes playing the **guitar** and singing. He also enjoys cooking and has written about it. He played almost 100 international matches for the Swiss national team. After Euro 2024 in Germany he retired from the national team.

begriffe.erklaerung: The only player who may play the ball with their hands in their own penalty area.
A shot at goal from eleven metres (German “Elfmeter”; in Switzerland also “Penalty”).
A way of deciding a match in which both teams take turns to shoot penalties.
When a goalkeeper stops a shot.

gewusst: At about 1.83 metres, Yann Sommer is rather small for a professional goalkeeper.
The victory over France in 2021 put Switzerland into the quarter-finals of a big tournament for the first time since 1954.

teile.einleitung: Marco Odermatt is a Swiss ski racer from the canton of Nidwalden and one of the most successful skiers of all time. From 2022 to 2026 he won the overall World Cup five times in a row. He is fast in almost every discipline, from the giant slalom to the downhill.
wichtigste: Marco Odermatt was born in 1997 and comes from Buochs in the canton of Nidwalden.
He races giant slalom, super-G and downhill.
In 2022 he became Olympic giant slalom champion in Beijing.
From 2022 to 2026 he won the overall World Cup every year, five times in a row.
He has become world champion several times, including in downhill and giant slalom.
In the 2022/23 season he collected more World Cup points than any racer before him.
He is very popular with fans because of his cheerful manner.

abschnitte.text: Marco Odermatt was born on 8 October 1997 and grew up in **Buochs** on Lake Lucerne. Buochs is in the canton of **Nidwalden**, not far from Lucerne. He was on skis even as a small child. Early on he raced his first races against other children at the ski club.

In 2018 Odermatt competed at the **Junior World Championships** in Davos. There he won five gold medals, a huge achievement. Soon afterwards he was already finishing near the front in the World Cup. In 2019 he celebrated his first World Cup victory, in the super-G at Beaver Creek in the USA.

The **overall World Cup** is the ranking across all disciplines and the whole season. Odermatt won it for the first time in 2022 and then every year until 2026. In the 2022/23 season he reached 2042 points, which is a record. He also won many small **crystal globes** in giant slalom, super-G and downhill.

At the 2022 Olympic Games in **Beijing**, Odermatt won gold in the giant slalom. At the 2023 World Championships in France he became world champion in the downhill and the giant slalom. In 2025 in Saalbach in Austria he also won the title in the super-G. So he has collected big titles in all his disciplines.

Odermatt skis very aggressively, but still cleanly and safely. He often finds a fast **line** and is good at making up for mistakes. Off the slopes he comes across as relaxed, down to earth and funny. Many children in Switzerland affectionately call him “Odi”.

begriffe.erklaerung: The ranking of the best skier across all the races of a winter.
A glass trophy for the winners of a World Cup ranking.
A discipline with many gates and wide turns.
The path a skier chooses between the gates.

gewusst: With 2042 points in one season, Marco Odermatt set a record previously held by Hermann Maier.
Marco Odermatt won five gold medals at a single Junior World Championships.

teile.einleitung: Values and norms shape how people live together. Values say what is important to us; norms say how we should behave. Ethics thinks about whether these values and rules are well justified.
wichtigste: A value is something people think is important, for example honesty.
A social norm is a rule for behaviour in a group.
Legal norms are laws that the state makes and enforces.
Keeping or breaking a norm is followed by a sanction, such as praise or blame.
The word “ethics” comes from Ancient Greek.
Ethics is thinking about morality.
Norms can change over time and from country to country.

abschnitte.text: A **value** is something that people think is important and worth striving for. Examples are **honesty**, friendship, justice, freedom or health. If you keep a promise, you show the value of **reliability**. Others can rely on people like that, and that builds trust. Values are rather general; they do not yet say exactly what to do in a situation.

A **norm** is a concrete rule of behaviour that says what is expected in a community. “You say hello when you meet someone” is a social norm. Norms often come from values: from the value of honesty follows the norm “You shall not lie”. Customs and traditions are based on habit. **Legal norms**, on the other hand, are laws laid down by the state; in Switzerland, for example, by parliament or by the people at the ballot box.

How does a group react when someone keeps or breaks a norm? This reaction is called a **sanction**. Sanctions can be **positive**, such as praise or a reward. They can also be **negative**, such as blame, exclusion or a fine. With legal norms the sanctions are laid down exactly, for example a fine for speeding. Sanctions make sure that norms are kept.

The word **ethics** comes from the Ancient Greek word **“ethos”**, which means habit, custom or character. The philosopher **Aristotle** made ethics a subject of its own. **Morality** means the values and rules by which people actually live. **Ethics** is the field of study that thinks about this morality and asks how it can be justified.

Sometimes two important values are in conflict. This is called a **value conflict**. Should you honestly tell a friend that their drawing has gone wrong, or keep quiet out of consideration? You have to weigh them up, because you cannot do full justice to both values. Also: norms **change**. What used to be seen as rude can be normal today, and in other countries some different rules apply.

gewusst: In Switzerland the people can directly help decide which legal norms apply, through initiatives and referendums.
Aristotle wrote a “Nicomachean Ethics”, which is probably named after his son Nicomachus.

teile.einleitung: The Golden Rule is one of the oldest and best-known principles of morality. It says: treat others as you would like to be treated yourself. It is found in many cultures and religions of the world.
wichtigste: The Golden Rule asks you to treat others as you would like to be treated yourself.
In German it is known as a rhyme: ‘Was du nicht willst, dass man dir tu, das füg auch keinem andern zu’ (what you do not want done to you, do not do to anyone else).
At its heart is a change of perspective: you put yourself in the other person's position.
Confucius was already teaching a form of the rule in China around 500 BC.
In the Bible it appears in the Sermon on the Mount in the Gospel of Matthew.
It appears in all the great world religions.
Kant's categorical imperative is often compared with it.

abschnitte.text: The Golden Rule is a rule of **reciprocity**. Before you act, you ask yourself: how would I feel if someone did this to me? This **change of perspective** is at its heart. There is a negative form, which says what you should not do, and a positive form, which calls on you to do good. The well-known German rhyme belongs to the negative form.

The Chinese thinker **Confucius** said, in essence: what you do not wish for yourself, do not do to others. Similar sayings are also found in **Judaism**, **Christianity**, **Islam**, **Hinduism** and **Buddhism**. In Judaism, for example, a saying of the scholar Hillel is well known: what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbour. Because so many cultures know it, the Golden Rule is regarded as a principle shared by all humanity.

In the **Gospel of Matthew** (chapter 7, verse 12) Jesus says that you should do to others as you would like to be treated yourself. This passage belongs to the **Sermon on the Mount**, a long speech with important teachings. There is a similar passage in the Gospel of Luke. Here the rule is put positively: it calls on you to actively do good yourself.

The **principle of retaliation** says: tit for tat. Like is answered with like, including bad with bad. The Golden Rule goes further: you should take the first good step yourself, without waiting for the other person. With the **categorical imperative**, the philosopher **Immanuel Kant** developed a principle that is often compared with it. But Kant himself distinguished it from the Golden Rule.

The Golden Rule can be applied everywhere. If you show a new child round the school, you are doing what you would want in that situation yourself. When sharing, listening or comforting, too, the question helps: how would I like to be treated? This makes living together in the family, the class and the community friendlier.

gewusst: The Golden Rule is so old that nobody knows exactly who first put it into words.
Almost identical sayings arose in cultures that knew nothing of each other at the time, for example in China and in the Middle East.

teile.einleitung: Wendy Holdener is a Swiss ski racer from the canton of Schwyz. Her strengths are the slalom and the combined. At the 2018 and 2022 Olympic Games she won five medals altogether.
wichtigste: Wendy Holdener was born on 12 May 1993 and comes from Unteriberg in the canton of Schwyz.
She is strongest in the slalom and the combined.
In 2018 in Pyeongchang she won gold in the team event, silver in the slalom and bronze in the combined.
In 2022 in Beijing she won silver in the combined and bronze in the slalom.
Together that makes five Olympic medals.
In 2017 in St Moritz she became world champion in the combined.

abschnitte.text: Wendy Holdener comes from **Unteriberg** in the canton of Schwyz. She grew up in the area around the Sihlsee lake and the Hoch-Ybrig ski resort. She was racing even as a child. For many years she has been one of the best slalom skiers in the world.

At the 2018 Olympic Games in **Pyeongchang** in South Korea, Holdener won three medals. She won silver in the slalom and bronze in the combined. With the Swiss team she won gold in the **team event**. That was her greatest success so far at the Olympic Games.
Four years later, in 2022 in **Beijing**, Holdener was successful again. She won silver in the combined. In the slalom she won bronze. That brought her to five Olympic medals in total.

In 2017, at the home World Championships in **St Moritz**, Holdener became world champion in the combined. In slalom she was on the podium very often without winning. Only in November 2022 in Killington in the USA did she celebrate her first World Cup slalom victory. She shared this win with the Swede Anna Swenn-Larsson, because both were exactly equally fast.

Wendy Holdener is an example of how **perseverance** pays off. For a long time she was on the slalom podium but never at the very top. Even so, she never gave up. She is very popular in Switzerland because of her cheerful manner.

begriffe.erklaerung: A ski discipline with many closely set gates.
A competition made of a fast race and a slalom.
A competition in which national teams race against each other in parallel races.
The steps for the first three places.

gewusst: Wendy Holdener was on the slalom podium a great many times before she finally celebrated her first slalom victory.
Her first World Cup slalom win was a shared victory, because two racers were equally fast to the hundredth of a second.

teile.einleitung: Human dignity means that every person has a value that nobody may take away. It applies to everyone, however old, rich or ill they are, and wherever they come from. Many constitutions and human rights are built on it.
wichtigste: Human dignity means: every person has a value that nobody may take away.
Article 7 of the Federal Constitution reads: ‘Human dignity must be respected and protected.’
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights begins with the dignity of all people.
The German Basic Law begins: ‘Human dignity shall be inviolable.’
Immanuel Kant said that a person must never be treated merely as a means.
Torture violates human dignity especially seriously and is banned worldwide.
Henry Dunant helped to found the International Committee of the Red Cross.

abschnitte.text: **Human dignity** is the special value that every person has. You do not have to earn it, and you cannot lose it either. It applies to babies just as much as to old people, to the healthy as to the sick. Anyone who respects dignity does not treat others like objects. Nobody may be humiliated, laughed at or shown up.

The philosopher **Immanuel Kant** strongly shaped thinking about dignity. He said that a person must never be used **merely as a means**, but must always also be treated as an **end**. Things have a price and can be replaced. People, on the other hand, have a dignity that is above any price. This idea is found in many laws today.

Article 1 of the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights** of 1948 begins like this: ‘All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.’ The German **Basic Law** of 1949 begins with the sentence: ‘Human dignity shall be inviolable.’ In the **Swiss Federal Constitution**, **Article 7** reads: ‘Human dignity must be respected and protected.’ All authorities at federal, cantonal and municipal level must abide by this.

**Torture** violates human dignity especially seriously. It is banned worldwide, among other things by a UN convention against torture. Slavery, exclusion and humiliation also violate dignity. In everyday life, respect begins with small things: not laughing at anyone, staying friendly and taking all people seriously.

abschnitte.titel: Henry Dunant and the Red Cross
abschnitte.text: After the Battle of Solferino in Italy in 1859, **Henry Dunant** from Geneva saw how thousands of wounded men were left without help. He worked to make sure that all the wounded would be helped, no matter which side they had fought on. In 1863 the **International Committee of the Red Cross** was founded in Geneva, and he was part of it. In 1901 Dunant received the first **Nobel Peace Prize**.

gewusst: The Red Cross emblem is the Swiss flag reversed: a red cross on a white background.
The Federal Constitution also protects the ‘dignity of living beings’, that is of animals and plants.

teile.einleitung: Artificial intelligence, or AI for short, writes texts, recognises faces and helps with decisions. The ethics of AI asks how such systems can be used fairly, safely and in the interests of people.
wichtigste: The EU's AI Act of 2024 sorts AI systems into levels of risk.
In the EU, social scoring is banned as an unacceptable risk.
Algorithmic bias often comes from distorted training data.
Explainable AI is meant to make machines' decisions understandable.
Deepfakes are AI forgeries that look deceptively real.
In 2024 the Council of Europe created the first binding international agreement on AI.
The alignment problem asks how AI can be tied to human values.

abschnitte.text: Long before today's computers, people were already thinking about moral machines. In 1942, in the short story ‘Runaround’, the writer **Isaac Asimov** formulated three **Laws of Robotics**. The first forbids a robot to injure a human being. These laws come from science fiction, but they are still quoted in debates about AI today.

AI systems learn from large amounts of data. If this data contains prejudices, the AI takes them on. This is called **algorithmic bias**, a systematic distortion. For example, some facial recognition systems were shown to recognise people with dark skin less well. That is why it is important to check data carefully and test systems for **fairness**.

Many learning systems are regarded as a **‘black box’**, because you cannot see how they reach a decision. That is tricky when it comes to loans, job applications or medicine. **Explainable AI**, XAI for short, is meant to make the reasons for a decision visible. Then people can check it and step in if there are mistakes.

**Deepfakes** are forgeries of videos, pictures or voices made with AI that look real. The name is made up of ‘deep learning’ and ‘fake’. They are a problem when used for disinformation, fraud or damaging someone's reputation. A big question for the future is the **alignment problem**: how can we make sure that an AI does what people really want? Even small mistakes in setting its goals can lead to unwanted behaviour.

In 2024 the EU adopted the **AI Act**. It distinguishes unacceptable, high, limited and minimal risk. The higher the risk, the stricter the obligations. Banned, for example, is **social scoring**, in which people get points for their behaviour and can be disadvantaged. Also in 2024 the **Council of Europe** adopted a framework convention on AI, human rights, democracy and the rule of law. Switzerland helped to draw it up.

gewusst: The Council of Europe's framework convention on AI is also open to states outside Europe.
During his life Isaac Asimov wrote or edited several hundred books.

teile.einleitung: Lara Gut-Behrami is a Swiss ski racer from Ticino and one of Switzerland’s most successful sportswomen. She has won the overall World Cup twice and became Olympic super-G champion in Beijing in 2022. Even as a teenager she raced among the best in the world.
wichtigste: Lara Gut-Behrami was born in Ticino in 1991.
Her strengths are the fast disciplines, super-G and downhill, but she also races giant slalom.
In 2016 and 2024 she won the overall World Cup.
In 2022 she became Olympic super-G champion in Beijing.
In 2021 she became world champion in the super-G and the giant slalom.
She is married to the former footballer Valon Behrami.
Her father Pauli Gut was her coach for a long time.

abschnitte.text: Lara Gut was born in **Sorengo** on 27 April 1991 and grew up in **Comano** in the canton of Ticino. Her father Pauli Gut coached her from an early age. Ticino is known more for sunshine and lakes than for skiing. Even so, she became one of the best skiers in the world.

At just 16 she was racing in the **World Cup**, the most important race series in skiing. At 17 she won two silver medals at the 2009 World Championships in Val d’Isère. Shortly before, she had celebrated her first World Cup victory in St Moritz. To date she has won more than 40 World Cup races.

The **overall World Cup** honours the best racer across all disciplines in a season. The winner receives the big crystal globe. Lara Gut-Behrami won it in 2016 and again in 2024, eight years later. On top of that she has several small crystal globes, especially in the super-G.

In 2014 in Sochi she won bronze in the downhill. At the 2021 World Championships in Cortina d’Ampezzo she became world champion in the **super-G** and the giant slalom. In 2022 in Beijing she finally won Olympic gold in the super-G as well. At these Games she also won bronze in the giant slalom.

In 2018 Lara Gut married the Swiss footballer **Valon Behrami**. Since then she has been called Lara Gut-Behrami. She speaks several languages, including Italian, German and English. Many fans in Ticino are especially proud of their skiing heroine.

begriffe.erklaerung: A fast ski discipline between downhill and giant slalom, raced without a training run.
The glass trophy for the winner of a World Cup ranking.
A series of races over the whole winter in which points are collected.
A technical discipline with many gates and wide turns.

gewusst: Eight years passed between her two overall World Cup wins.
Lara Gut-Behrami was only 17 when she won her first World Championship medals.

teile.einleitung: Animal welfare means protecting animals from suffering, pain and poor living conditions. Switzerland has a strict law for this. Organisations, animal shelters and every individual can also do a lot for animals.
wichtigste: Switzerland's current Animal Welfare Act has applied since 2008.
The Federal Constitution includes the concept of the ‘dignity of living beings’.
Keeping animals appropriately means keeping them according to their needs.
In Switzerland guinea pigs must not be kept alone, because they are sociable.
World Animal Day is on 4 October.
The WWF was founded in 1961 in Morges on Lake Geneva.
Animals without a home often go to an animal shelter.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland's current **Animal Welfare Act** was passed by parliament in 2005 and has applied since **2008**. By international standards it is considered strict. It protects not only against pain and suffering but explicitly also the **dignity of the animal**. Since 1992 the Federal Constitution has used the term **‘dignity of living beings’** for this. An animal welfare ordinance sets out many details, for example how much space an animal needs.

Keeping animals **appropriately for their species** means keeping them in a way that suits their **needs**. They need enough space, exercise, things to do and suitable food. This is different for every species. **Guinea pigs**, for example, are **sociable animals**, so in Switzerland they must not be kept alone. This also applies to other social animals such as budgerigars or rabbits.

For **animal experiments**, the **3R principle** applies: **Replace**, **Reduce** and **Refine**. So animal experiments should be replaced by other methods wherever possible. Where this is not possible, fewer animals should be used and the strain on them should be reduced.

The **WWF** was founded in **1961** in **Morges** on Lake Geneva. Today its international headquarters are in Gland in the canton of Vaud, and its emblem is the **giant panda**. The WWF works mainly for nature and wild animals. Animals that no longer have a home often go to an **animal shelter**. There they are cared for until they find new owners. Many animal shelters are run by animal welfare societies.

**World Animal Day** is on **4 October**. On this day the Church also remembers **Saint Francis of Assisi**. He lived in Italy in the 13th century and is regarded as the **patron saint of animals**. According to legend, he even preached to the birds. He saw animals as the brothers and sisters of human beings.

gewusst: The first World Animal Day took place in Berlin in 1925; in 1931 it was declared an international day.
World Animal Day falls on the feast day of Saint Francis of Assisi.

teile.einleitung: In organ donation, a person gives an organ so that someone who is ill can go on living. Most organs come from people who have died. In Switzerland the Transplantation Act sets out exactly when and how donation is allowed.
wichtigste: On 15 May 2022 Swiss voters approved the extended opt-out solution.
The proposal received about 60 per cent of the vote.
Before that, the extended consent solution applied.
‘Extended’ means that the relatives are involved.
Before organs are removed, brain death must be confirmed.
Swisstransplant coordinates the allocation of organs.
Organ donations must be free of charge.

abschnitte.text: On **15 May 2022** the Swiss people voted on a change to the **Transplantation Act**. With **about 60 per cent** voting yes, the **extended opt-out solution** was approved. Under it, anyone who did not object during their lifetime counts as a donor. Before that the **extended consent solution** applied: organs could only be removed if the person or their relatives had agreed. The new rule needs a register, which is why putting it into practice takes several years.

The word **‘extended’** means that the **relatives** are involved. If there is no documented decision, they are asked. They can refuse a removal if they know or suspect that the person would have been against it. That is why it helps to talk about the subject with your family. People in society judge the question differently, and every decision must be respected.

Before organs may be removed from a person who has died, **brain death** must be confirmed. This means that all functions of the brain have permanently stopped. Two specialists must confirm this independently of each other. Donation must be **free of charge**: nobody may receive money or other advantages for it. Trading in organs is a criminal offence.

The national foundation **Swisstransplant** coordinates the **allocation** of donor organs on behalf of the federal government and keeps the waiting list. Who receives an organ is decided according to legal criteria, for example medical urgency and waiting time. This is meant to make the distribution fair. Many people on the waiting list urgently need an organ.

In **April 1969** the surgeon **Åke Senning** carried out Switzerland's first heart transplant in **Zurich**. The world's first heart transplant had taken place in Cape Town in 1967. Living people can also donate. The most common is donating a **kidney**, because you can live well with one healthy kidney. It is also possible to donate part of the liver.

gewusst: Åke Senning came from Sweden and had earlier fitted the first pacemaker to be implanted in a human being.
After a partial donation, the liver can grow back.

teile.einleitung: Mathilde Gremaud is a Swiss freestyle skier from the canton of Fribourg. In slopestyle she performs spectacular jumps and tricks over kickers and rails. She has been Olympic champion twice and also world champion.
wichtigste: Mathilde Gremaud was born in Fribourg in 2000.
Her disciplines are slopestyle and big air.
In 2018 in Pyeongchang she won Olympic silver in slopestyle.
In 2022 in Beijing she became Olympic slopestyle champion and won bronze in big air.
In 2026, at the Games in Italy, she again became Olympic slopestyle champion.
In 2023 she became slopestyle world champion.
She has also won several gold medals at the X Games.

abschnitte.text: Mathilde Gremaud was born on 8 February 2000 in **Fribourg**. Her mother tongue is French. Fribourg lies on the border between German-speaking and French-speaking Switzerland. Later she discovered snow parks and **freestyle** skiing.

In **slopestyle** you ski down a course with kickers, rails and boxes. On the kickers you perform jumps with spins and somersaults. On the rails you slide along on your skis. A panel of judges scores the difficulty, cleanness and variety of the tricks.

In 2018 in **Pyeongchang** Gremaud won silver in slopestyle, and gold went to her teammate Sarah Höfflin. In 2022 in Beijing she became Olympic slopestyle champion and won bronze in **big air**. In 2026 in Livigno she defended her slopestyle title. That made her a two-time Olympic champion.

In 2023 in Bakuriani in Georgia, Gremaud became slopestyle **world champion**. In the 2023/24 season she won the big crystal globe as the best park freestyler. At the X Games, a well-known extreme sports competition, she has won gold in big air several times. She is one of the best freestyle skiers in the world.

Switzerland has many strong freestyle athletes. In Laax and other ski resorts there are big snow parks where you can practise. For difficult jumps, athletes often train first on trampolines or with airbags. That way they learn new tricks without getting hurt straight away.

A competition with a single, very large jump.
A rail that you slide along on skis or a snowboard.
Part of a ski resort with kickers and obstacles for tricks.

Freestyle professionals often practise new tricks first on a huge air cushion.

teile.einleitung: Medical ethics asks what is right and good in medicine. It deals with questions such as: who decides about a treatment? How can scarce resources be shared out fairly? What rules apply to research on human beings?
wichtigste: Beauchamp and Childress name four principles: autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence and justice.
A treatment needs the informed consent of the patient.
Paternalism means deciding against a person's will for their supposed good.
The Nuremberg Code of 1947 laid down rules for experiments on humans.
The World Medical Association adopted the Declaration of Geneva in 1948 and the Declaration of Helsinki in 1964.
Triage is sorting people by urgency when resources are not enough for everyone.
In Switzerland the advance directive has been regulated in the Civil Code since 2013.

abschnitte.text: In 1979 the Americans **Tom Beauchamp** and **James Childress** set out four principles that are widely used in everyday hospital life. **Autonomy** means respect for self-determination. **Non-maleficence** means not harming patients. **Beneficence** requires promoting their well-being, and **justice** a fair distribution. These principles can contradict each other and then have to be weighed against each other.

Before a treatment, **informed consent** is needed. The person must be given understandable information, be capable of judgement and be able to decide freely. Without consent, a medical procedure counts legally as bodily harm. The opposite is **paternalism**: experts decide against the will of a person who is capable of judgement, supposedly for their own good. The word comes from the Latin pater, father.

abschnitte.titel: Rules after the Second World War
abschnitte.text: Under the Nazis, doctors had carried out cruel experiments on people. In connection with the Nuremberg doctors' trial, the **Nuremberg Code** was drawn up in **1947**. Its first point requires the voluntary consent of the person being experimented on. In **1948** the **World Medical Association** adopted the **Declaration of Geneva**, a modern version of the Hippocratic Oath. In **1964** came the **Declaration of Helsinki**, with principles for medical research.

Sometimes there are not enough beds, machines or staff for everyone. Then patients are sorted according to urgency. This is called **triage**, from the French trier, to sort. Ethically this is very difficult, because human lives are at stake. That is why there are clear guidelines for it, so that decisions are not made arbitrarily.

The **Swiss Academy of Medical Sciences (SAMS)** draws up medical-ethical guidelines, for example on capacity for judgement or the end of life. The doctors' association **FMH** adopts many of them into its professional code, and they then become binding for its members. Since **1 January 2013** the **advance directive** has been expressly regulated in the Civil Code. With it, a person who is capable of judgement can decide in advance which treatments they agree to.

gewusst: The Hippocratic Oath is named after the Greek doctor Hippocrates, who lived about 2400 years ago.
The Declaration of Geneva has been revised several times, most recently in 2017.

teile.einleitung: Swiss-Ski is the Swiss Ski Association and one of the biggest sports associations in the country. It looks after the national teams in alpine skiing, cross-country skiing, ski jumping, snowboarding, freestyle and other snow sports. With stars such as Marco Odermatt and Lara Gut-Behrami, Switzerland is one of the best skiing nations in the world.
wichtigste: Swiss-Ski is the national association for skiing and snow sports.
The association was founded in 1904.
Marco Odermatt won the overall World Cup five times in a row.
The 2027 Alpine World Ski Championships take place in Crans-Montana.
Swiss-Ski also looks after cross-country skiing, ski jumping, snowboarding, freestyle and biathlon.
Switzerland has won the Nations Cup in the alpine World Cup many times.
The association is based in Muri near Bern.

abschnitte.text: **Swiss-Ski** was founded in 1904 and today has many thousands of members in hundreds of ski clubs. The association is responsible for the **national teams** in many disciplines: alpine skiing, cross-country skiing, ski jumping, Nordic combined, biathlon, snowboarding, freestyle and telemark. It organises World Cup races such as the Lauberhorn races in Wengen. It also supports young athletes in regional performance centres.

**Marco Odermatt** from Buochs in the canton of Nidwalden is one of the best ski racers in history. He won the **overall World Cup** five times in a row, from 2022 to 2026. In 2022 in Beijing he became Olympic champion in the giant slalom. He wins in giant slalom, super-G and downhill. That makes him a role model for many young skiers.

**Lara Gut-Behrami** from Ticino won the overall World Cup twice and Olympic gold in the super-G in 2022. Earlier legends include **Vreni Schneider**, Pirmin Zurbriggen and Michela Figini. In cross-country skiing, Dario Cologna shone with four Olympic victories. In snowboarding and freestyle, Swiss women such as Mathilde Gremaud have won Olympic gold.

The **2027 Alpine World Ski Championships** take place in **Crans-Montana** in Valais. The resort already hosted a World Championship in 1987, at which Switzerland won a great many medals. The races are held against a magnificent backdrop with views of the Valais Alps. For Switzerland, a home World Championship is a huge celebration. The last host was St Moritz in 2017.

Swiss-Ski runs programmes so that children learn to enjoy snow sports early. Talented young people attend **sports schools** such as those in Engelberg, Davos or Brig, where school and training fit together. The **Nations Cup** shows which country is strongest in the alpine World Cup, and Switzerland has won it several times in recent years. Important sponsors and cantons support the association.

In 2010 he was picked fifth in the NHL Draft, earlier than any Swiss player before him. He plays as a forward and is known for his strength and his goals.
wichtigste: Nino Niederreiter was born in Chur in 1992.
He plays ice hockey as a forward.
As a junior he played for HC Davos and for the Portland Winterhawks in the USA.
In 2010 he was picked fifth by the New York Islanders in the NHL Draft.
Later he played for Minnesota, Carolina, Nashville and Winnipeg, among others.
In 2013 he won World Championship silver with Switzerland.
He has played hundreds of NHL games.

abschnitte.text: Nino Niederreiter was born on 8 September 1992 in **Chur** in the canton of the Grisons. He was on the ice even as a little boy. As a youngster he played for **HC Davos**, among other clubs. At 16 he went to North America to develop further.

In the USA Niederreiter played for the **Portland Winterhawks** in a junior league. There he scored many goals and caught the eye of NHL talent scouts. He also played strongly for Switzerland at the Junior World Championships. In this way he became one of the greatest talents of his year.

The **NHL Draft** is an event at which the NHL clubs take turns to choose young players. In 2010 the **New York Islanders** picked Niederreiter fifth. At the time that was the highest position any Swiss player had ever reached. It was a great moment for Swiss ice hockey.

At the Islanders, Niederreiter did not get much of a chance at first. At the **Minnesota Wild** he became an important goal scorer from 2013. After that he played for the Carolina Hurricanes, the Nashville Predators and the Winnipeg Jets. He is seen as a powerful forward who puts a lot of pressure on in front of the goal.

Niederreiter also plays for the **Swiss national team**. In 2013 Switzerland surprisingly won silver at the World Championship in Stockholm. Niederreiter was part of that team. He has also taken part in the Olympic Games.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss women’s national ice hockey team represents Switzerland at world championships and the Olympic Games. It has already won two Olympic bronze medals, in 2014 in Sochi and in 2026 in Milan and Cortina. That makes it one of the most successful women’s teams in Swiss sport.
wichtigste: The Swiss women ice hockey players won bronze at the 2026 Olympic Games.

Goalkeeper Florence Schelling was voted the best player of the Olympic tournament in 2014.

abschnitte.text: The **women’s Nati** has played in international tournaments since the 1980s. Women’s ice hockey has been an Olympic sport since 1998. Because Switzerland has fewer players than Canada or the USA, its successes are especially remarkable. Many players train in women’s teams in the **Women’s League** or play at universities in North America. Some also play in the new professional league, the **PWHL**.

At the 2014 Olympic Games in **Sochi**, Switzerland played Sweden in the game for third place. It was already 0:2 down and still won 4:3. **Alina Müller**, who was only 15 at the time, scored the winning goal into the empty net. Goalkeeper **Florence Schelling** saved an incredible number of shots during the whole tournament. She was voted the most valuable player of the Olympic tournament.

teile.einleitung: Nevin Galmarini is a Swiss snowboarder from the Lower Engadine in the canton of the Grisons. He was a specialist in the parallel giant slalom, in which two riders race down the slope side by side at the same time. In 2018 he became Olympic champion in Pyeongchang.
wichtigste: Nevin Galmarini comes from Ardez in the Lower Engadine.
His discipline was the parallel giant slalom on a snowboard.
In the parallel giant slalom, two riders race at the same time on two courses.
In 2014 he won Olympic silver in Sochi.
In 2018 he won Olympic gold in Pyeongchang.
He rides a hard snowboard and hard-shell boots, similar to ski boots.
For many years he was among the best in the world in alpine snowboarding.

abschnitte.text: Nevin Galmarini grew up in **Ardez** in the Lower Engadine, a village in the canton of the Grisons. Romansh is spoken in this area. The mountains around Scuol gave him many chances to train. Even as a teenager he was taking part in snowboard races.

Galmarini did not ride in the halfpipe but did **alpine snowboarding**. In it you ride round gates as in ski racing. The riders stand on a long, hard board and wear stiff **hard-shell boots**. In the turns they lean so far into the slope that they almost touch the snow with their hand.

In the **parallel giant slalom** two riders race at the same time on two identical courses side by side. Whoever reaches the bottom first goes through to the next round. It continues like this in a **knockout system** right up to the big final. It is exciting for the spectators because you can see straight away who is in front.

At the 2014 Olympic Games in **Sochi**, Galmarini won silver in the parallel giant slalom. Four years later, in 2018 in **Pyeongchang** in South Korea, he won gold. In the final he beat the South Korean Lee Sang-ho in front of his home crowd. That made him one of the few Swiss Olympic champions in alpine snowboarding.

Switzerland is very successful in alpine snowboarding. As well as Galmarini, other Swiss riders such as Philipp Schoch have won Olympic gold in the parallel giant slalom. Many races take place in the Grisons, for example in Scuol. Young snowboarders can train in sports classes and performance centres.

teile.einleitung: Virtue ethics does not first ask ‘What should I do?’, but ‘What kind of person do I want to be?’. It goes back mainly to the Greek philosopher Aristotle. At its centre are good qualities of character, the virtues.
wichtigste: Aristotle's most important work on ethics is the ‘Nicomachean Ethics’.
According to Aristotle, every person strives for eudaimonia, the flourishing life.
The doctrine of the mean says: virtue is the middle between two extremes.
Courage lies between cowardice and foolhardiness.
Virtues of character are acquired through habit and practice.
Practical wisdom (phronesis) helps you decide correctly in concrete situations.
The four cardinal virtues are prudence, justice, courage and temperance.

abschnitte.text: **Aristotle** (384 to 322 BC) was a Greek philosopher and a pupil of Plato. He was also the teacher of the young Alexander the Great. His most important work on ethics is the **‘Nicomachean Ethics’**. It is probably named after his son or his father, who were both called Nicomachus. In it he asks how a person can live well.

According to Aristotle, every person ultimately strives for **eudaimonia**. The Greek word means a **flourishing life** or happiness. Everything else, such as money or fame, we only want because it contributes to this goal. Eudaimonia is not reached by chance but by living **virtuously**. What is meant is a life in which you develop your abilities well.

The **doctrine of the mean** says: a virtue is the **middle between two extremes**. **Courage** lies between **cowardice** and **foolhardiness**. Generosity lies between meanness and extravagance. But the right mean is not always exactly in the middle; it depends on the situation. To find it, you need **phronesis**, practical **wisdom**.

The ethical virtues, also called **virtues of character**, are not inborn. You acquire them through **habit and practice**. Aristotle compared this to learning a craft: you become just by acting justly, and brave by acting bravely. Over time, good action becomes a settled attitude. That is why upbringing is so important for him.

Since ancient times four **cardinal virtues** have been known: **prudence**, **justice**, **courage** and **temperance**. Other virtues, such as humility, are not among these four. For a long time virtue ethics stayed rather in the background. With his book **‘After Virtue’** (1981), the philosopher **Alasdair MacIntyre** contributed greatly to its revival. Today, alongside the ethics of duty and utilitarianism, it is one of the major approaches in ethics.

gewusst: The word ‘cardinal virtue’ comes from the Latin cardo, door hinge: all other virtues turn on these.
Aristotle founded his own school in Athens, the Lyceum.

teile.einleitung: The categorical imperative is the most important principle in Immanuel Kant's ethics. It is meant to show how you can test whether an action is morally right using reason alone.
wichtigste: Kant formulated the categorical imperative in 1785 in the ‘Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals’.
The basic formula requires you to act only on maxims that could become a universal law.
A maxim is a personal principle of what you will.
The formula of humanity says: never treat people merely as a means, but always also as an end.
A hypothetical imperative only applies if you have a particular goal.
Kant lived and taught almost all his life in Königsberg.
Autonomy of the will means that the will gives itself the law through reason.

abschnitte.text: **Immanuel Kant** (1724 to 1804) was one of the most important philosophers of the **Enlightenment**. He lived and taught almost all his life in **Königsberg** in East Prussia, today's Kaliningrad. In 1785 his work **‘Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals’** appeared. In it he set out the categorical imperative in detail for the first time. Later he developed his ethics further in other books.

The best-known version is called the **formula of universal law**: ‘Act only according to that maxim through which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.’ A **maxim** is a subjective principle, that is a personal rule by which you act. You check: could this rule apply to all people without cancelling itself out? If not, according to Kant the action is immoral.

Kant explains his idea with an example: someone needs money and promises to pay it back, although he knows he cannot. If everyone acted like this, **nobody would believe promises any more**. Promising would lose its meaning. So the maxim cannot be made universal, and that is why the action is wrong. What matters to Kant is not the consequences but the contradiction in the rule itself.

Another version is the **formula of humanity**. It requires you to treat every person never **merely as a means**, but always also as an **end**. So you must not simply use others to reach your own goals. Every human being has a **dignity** that must be respected. This idea has strongly shaped modern thinking about **human dignity** and human rights.

A **hypothetical imperative** only applies under a condition: ‘If you want to stay healthy, take exercise.’ A **categorical imperative**, by contrast, applies unconditionally, to everyone and always. For Kant a person is free when they do not simply follow their wishes but give themselves the law through reason. He calls this **autonomy of the will**. Autonomy literally means ‘giving oneself the law’.

gewusst: Kant is said to have hardly ever left Königsberg and its surroundings, even though he thought about the whole world.
Kant did not think the categorical imperative was the same as the Golden Rule and explicitly distinguished it from it.

teile.einleitung: Granit Xhaka is a Swiss footballer and long-standing captain of the Swiss national team. He was born in Basel and has played for big clubs in Germany and England. With Bayer Leverkusen he became German champion unbeaten in 2024.
wichtigste: Granit Xhaka was born in Basel in 1992.
His parents come from Kosovo.
He plays in midfield and is known for his passes and his strong left foot.
He began his professional career at FC Basel.
From 2016 to 2023 he played for Arsenal in London.
With Bayer Leverkusen he became German champion without a single defeat in 2024.
He has played more international matches for Switzerland than any other player.

abschnitte.text: Granit Xhaka was born in **Basel** on 27 September 1992. His family comes from Kosovo and came to Switzerland before he was born. As a child he played for FC Concordia Basel and then for **FC Basel**. His older brother Taulant is also a professional footballer and played for the Albanian national team.

In 2009 Xhaka became **under-17 world champion** with Switzerland in Nigeria. That was the first world title for a Swiss football team. At FC Basel he then became Swiss champion. In 2012 he moved to Borussia Mönchengladbach in the German Bundesliga.

In 2016 Xhaka went to Arsenal in London, where he played for seven years and was captain for a time. With Arsenal he won the English FA Cup. In 2023 he moved to **Bayer Leverkusen**. In the 2023/24 season Leverkusen won the league without losing a single Bundesliga match, and the German Cup as well.

Xhaka has played for the **Swiss national team** since 2011. He has taken part in several World Cups and European Championships. At Euro 2024 in Germany, with Xhaka as captain, Switzerland reached the quarter-finals. He is the player with the most international caps in Swiss history.

Xhaka is a **midfielder** who directs his team’s play. He spreads the ball with accurate passes and has a powerful left-footed shot. He is seen as a leader who is vocal and drives his teammates on. In 2025 he moved to AFC Sunderland in the English Premier League.

Granit and his brother Taulant played against each other at Euro 2016, Granit for Switzerland and Taulant for Albania.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss national ice hockey team is the men’s team that represents Switzerland at world championships and the Olympic Games. It is often simply called the “Nati” and today is one of the best teams in the world. At the home World Championship in 2026 it won the silver medal.
wichtigste: Ice hockey is one of the most popular sports in Switzerland.
The Nati won silver at the 2026 Ice Hockey World Championship.
Before that there was also world championship silver in 2013, 2018, 2024 and 2025.
Andres Ambühl has played the most international matches for the Swiss ice hockey team.
At the 1928 and 1948 Olympic Games in St Moritz, Switzerland won bronze.
Switzerland has never yet been world champion.
The association is called the Swiss Ice Hockey Federation.

abschnitte.text: Ice hockey has been played in Switzerland for over 100 years. The national association was founded in 1908 and is now called the **Swiss Ice Hockey Federation**. The top league is the **National League**, with clubs such as SC Bern, HC Davos and Fribourg-Gottéron. The games attract many spectators; in Bern there are often over 15,000 fans. Many children start at ice hockey school at the age of four or five.

For a long time Switzerland was only average internationally. In 2013 in Stockholm it surprisingly reached the **World Championship final** and won silver. In 2018 in Copenhagen it lost the final to Sweden only in the penalty shootout. Silver followed in 2024 and 2025. At the **home World Championship in 2026** in Zurich and Fribourg, the Nati won silver once again.

At the Winter Olympics of 1928 and 1948 in **St Moritz**, Switzerland won bronze each time. Back then the games were still played in the open air. Since then the men have not won another Olympic medal. Today professionals from the North American **NHL** often play at the Olympics too, which makes the tournaments very strong.

The record international is **Andres Ambühl** from the Grisons, who played for Switzerland for over two decades. He took part in more world championships than almost any other player in the world. Other stars play in the NHL, for example **Roman Josi**, captain of the Nashville Predators. Nico Hischier, Kevin Fiala and goalkeepers such as Leonardo Genoni have also shaped the Nati. The coach since 2015 has been **Patrick Fischer**.

Each team has five outfield players and a goalkeeper on the ice. The game is played with a hard rubber disc, the **puck**. A game lasts three times 20 minutes of actual playing time. Because ice hockey is so exhausting, players often change after only about 45 seconds. If the score is level after extra time, a **penalty shootout** decides.

A 20-minute section of the game.

Andres Ambühl was still playing at world championships when he was over 40.

teile.einleitung: Whistleblowers are people who make wrongdoing in a company, an authority or a state public. The English word means roughly “someone who blows the whistle”. Whistleblowing can uncover important scandals, but it often puts the people involved in difficult situations.
wichtigste: In 2013 Edward Snowden made public the worldwide mass surveillance by US secret services.
In 1971 Daniel Ellsberg gave the “Pentagon Papers” about the Vietnam War to the press.
In 1997 the security guard Christoph Meili saved bank files from being shredded in Zurich.
In 2019 the EU adopted a directive to protect whistleblowers.
In 2020 the National Council finally rejected a bill to protect whistleblowers in the private sector.
Federal employees can report wrongdoing to the Swiss Federal Audit Office.

abschnitte.text: A **whistleblower** reports wrongdoing they have discovered at work, such as fraud, dangers or breaches of the law. In German they are also called **Hinweisgeber**, informants. The report can go to someone inside the organisation, to an authority or to the press. Ethically, two values clash here: **loyalty** to the employer and the **public interest** in bringing injustice to light. Whistleblowers often risk their job or criminal proceedings.

In 1971 the military analyst **Daniel Ellsberg** gave the secret “Pentagon Papers” to the press. They showed that several US governments had misled the public about the Vietnam War. In the Watergate affair, FBI deputy director **Mark Felt**, under the codename **“Deep Throat”**, helped the journalists Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein. The affair led to the resignation of President Richard Nixon in 1974. In 2013 **Edward Snowden** handed journalists documents about programmes such as PRISM, and he has lived in Russia since then.

In January 1997 the night watchman **Christoph Meili** saved files from being shredded at the Union Bank of Switzerland in Zurich. They had to do with **dormant assets** from the Nazi era. After threats he was granted asylum in the USA, but later returned. The computer specialist **Hervé Falciani** took customer data from HSBC’s private bank in Geneva and gave it to tax authorities. The data was analysed as “Swiss Leaks”, and in 2015 the Federal Criminal Court convicted him in his absence.

In 2019 the **EU** adopted the **Whistleblower Directive**. It requires safe reporting channels and forbids retaliation such as dismissal. In Switzerland, in 2020, a revision of the Code of Obligations meant to protect whistleblowers in the **private sector** failed in the National Council after more than ten years of debate. For employees of the **federal administration** there has been a reporting office at the **Swiss Federal Audit Office** (SFAO) since 2011. Anyone who reports there in good faith must not be put at a disadvantage.

gewusst: Mark Felt kept his role as “Deep Throat” secret for over 30 years and only revealed himself in 2005.
Many companies today have their own reporting offices, often anonymous, that staff can turn to.

teile.einleitung: Happiness is a feeling of deep contentment and joy. Philosophers, psychologists and even whole states ask what makes people happy and how happiness can be measured.
wichtigste: For Aristotle, eudaimonia, the flourishing life, was the highest goal.
Hedonism sees pleasure as the most important goal; one of its representatives was Epicurus.
In flow you are completely absorbed in an activity.
Serotonin is often called the ‘happiness hormone’.
Finland has topped the World Happiness Report since 2018 (as of 2025).
Bhutan measures its success by ‘Gross National Happiness’.
The International Day of Happiness is on 20 March.

abschnitte.text: The ancient Greeks were already thinking about happiness. **Aristotle** called the flourishing, happy life **eudaimonia**. He saw it as humanity's highest goal and believed it could be reached through a virtuous, reasonable life. **Hedonism**, from the Greek ‘hedone’ for pleasure and joy, on the other hand, puts pleasure at the centre. A well-known representative was **Epicurus**. However, he taught that moderate pleasures and peace of mind were more important than luxury.

In the brain, **messenger substances** are at work that influence our mood. **Serotonin** is often called the ‘happiness hormone’. **Dopamine** and **endorphins** are also called this in everyday language. A special feeling of happiness is **flow**. In flow you are completely absorbed in an activity and forget the time. The term was coined by the psychologist **Mihály Csíkszentmihályi**. Flow often arises when a task is neither too easy nor too hard.

The **World Happiness Report** compares how satisfied people are in many countries every year. Since 2018 **Finland** has been in first place without a break (as of 2025). Switzerland is usually among the top ten. The country of **Bhutan** in the Himalayas measures its success by **Gross National Happiness**. It puts people's well-being above pure economic growth, and this goal is even written into its constitution.

The **UN General Assembly** declared **20 March** the International Day of Happiness. It has been marked since 2013. The day is meant to remind us that happiness and well-being are important goals for all people. The idea came from Bhutan. Many schools and organisations use the day to think about contentment and togetherness.

Many cultures have **lucky charms**. A well-known example is the **four-leaf clover**. Clover normally has three leaves; a four-leaf one is rare and is therefore seen as a symbol of luck. At New Year in Switzerland people also give each other chimney sweeps, horseshoes or little lucky pigs. Whether they really bring luck is another question, but they make many people happy.

gewusst: In the World Happiness Report people are asked how satisfied they are with their lives on a scale from 0 to 10.
The chimney sweep is seen as a lucky charm because in the past a clean chimney protected the house from fire.

teile.einleitung: Social contract theories ask why there is a state and shared rules at all. Their answer: because reasonable people would agree to such a contract. Famous thinkers such as Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau from Geneva developed this idea.
wichtigste: Social contract theories justify the state and morality through the reasonable agreement of those affected.
The contract is usually an imagined model, not a real historical event.
In “Leviathan” in 1651, Thomas Hobbes described the state of nature as a war of all against all.
According to John Locke, the state should protect life, liberty and property.
Jean-Jacques Rousseau from Geneva wrote “The Social Contract” in 1762.
The prisoner’s dilemma shows why binding agreements can benefit everyone.

abschnitte.text: Imagine there were no state, no police and no laws. Philosophers call this imagined situation the **state of nature**. Social contract theories ask: which rules would free and reasonable people agree on with each other there? Rules and authority are then justified if those affected would **reasonably agree** to them. The contract is a thought model; nobody has ever really signed it.

The Englishman **Thomas Hobbes** wrote his work “Leviathan” in 1651, under the impression of the English Civil War. The name comes from a biblical sea monster that stands for the mighty state. Without a state, according to Hobbes, there is a **war of all against all**: people distrust each other and fight for safety and goods. Life would be “solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short”. That is why people hand over their power to a strong ruler who keeps the peace.

The Englishman **John Locke** saw the task of the state differently. According to Locke, every person has **natural rights**: life, liberty and property. The state exists to protect these rights. If a government violates them, citizens may, according to Locke, offer **resistance**. These ideas later influenced the American Declaration of Independence and modern constitutions.

**Jean-Jacques Rousseau** was born in 1712 in Geneva, which was then an independent republic. He liked to call himself “citoyen de Genève”, citizen of Geneva. In his work “Du contrat social” of 1762 he describes the **volonté générale**, the general will. It is not simply the sum of private interests, but aims at what is good for everyone together. For Rousseau, only laws based on this general will are legitimate.

Philosophers still think about contracts today. In 1998, in “What We Owe to Each Other”, **Thomas Scanlon** founded a modern contractualism. According to him, an action is wrong if it breaks principles that nobody could reasonably reject. The **prisoner’s dilemma** comes from game theory: two prisoners betray each other, even though keeping silent together would be better for both. The model shows why cooperation and binding agreements benefit everyone.

gewusst: In Geneva there is a small island in the Rhône named after Rousseau: the Île Rousseau, with a statue of the philosopher.
The name “Leviathan” comes from the Bible, where it means a gigantic sea monster.

teile.einleitung: Beat Feuz is a former Swiss ski racer from the Emmental. He was one of the best downhill racers in the world and became Olympic champion in Beijing in 2022. Because of his compact build and his speed, his teammates called him “Kugelblitz”, the ball lightning.
wichtigste: Beat Feuz was born on 11 February 1987 and comes from Schangnau in the Emmental.
His special discipline was the downhill.
In 2017 he became downhill world champion in St Moritz.
In 2022 he won Olympic gold in the downhill in Beijing.
He won the World Cup downhill ranking four times in a row.
He won three times on the Streif in Kitzbühel and three times at the Lauberhorn.
He ended his career in January 2023.

abschnitte.text: Beat Feuz grew up as the son of a farming family in **Schangnau** in the upper Emmental. Even as a child he was on skis at the small ski lift in his village. As a junior he was a great talent and won medals at junior world championships. Then serious **knee injuries** held him back for years. Many people already thought his career was over.

Despite his knee problems, Feuz fought his way back to the top of the world. At the home World Championships in **St Moritz** in 2017 he became world champion in the **downhill**. In 2018 in Pyeongchang he won Olympic silver in the super-G and bronze in the downhill. He celebrated his greatest triumph in 2022 in Beijing with **Olympic gold** in the downhill. With that he had won all the big titles.

From 2018 to 2021 Feuz won the **downhill ranking** in the World Cup four times in a row, and with it the small crystal globe. On the famous **Streif** in Kitzbühel he won three times, twice in 2021 and once in 2022. At the **Lauberhorn** in Wengen he also won three times, in 2012, 2018 and 2020. These races are considered the most difficult downhills in the world.

Feuz was not especially tall, but strong and compactly built. That is why his teammates called him **Kugelblitz**, ball lightning. He was known for his feel for the terrain and his calm, down-to-earth manner. Because his knees had to be looked after, he often trained less than others. Even so, he was usually right on form in races.

In January 2023 Beat Feuz raced for the last time in Wengen and Kitzbühel. After the downhill in Kitzbühel he said goodbye to the fans to loud applause. He lives with his family in **Austria**; his partner comes from Tyrol. For many Swiss people he remains one of the most popular skiers.

begriffe.erklaerung: The fastest discipline in ski racing, with speeds of over 130 kilometres per hour.
A fast discipline with more gates and turns than the downhill.
The famous and feared downhill course in Kitzbühel.
The trophy for winning a World Cup ranking.

gewusst: Beat Feuz won the downhill globe four years in a row, something only very few racers have managed.
In 2021 in Kitzbühel Feuz won two downhills within just three days.
Despite many knee operations, he became world champion and Olympic champion.

teile.einleitung: Lia Wälti is a Swiss footballer from the Emmental and captain of the Swiss women’s national team. She played for many years in Germany and England. In 2025 she won the UEFA Women’s Champions League with Arsenal.
wichtigste: Lia Wälti was born in 1993 in Langnau im Emmental.
She plays in central midfield.
She is captain of the Swiss women’s national team.
From 2013 to 2018 she played for Turbine Potsdam in Germany.
From 2018 to 2025 she played for Arsenal in London.
In 2025 she won the Champions League with Arsenal.
At the home Euro 2025 she led Switzerland out onto the pitch as captain.

abschnitte.text: Lia Wälti was born on 19 April 1993 in **Langnau im Emmental**. At the age of eight she started playing football at FC Langnau. Later she played for **Young Boys** in Bern. With YB she became Swiss champion in 2011.

In 2013 Wälti moved to **Turbine Potsdam** in the German Bundesliga. There she played for five years against the best players in Europe. She developed into an important player in midfield. At the same time she became a regular in the Swiss national team.

In 2018 she went to **Arsenal** in London. In her very first season she became English champion with Arsenal. In 2025 Arsenal won the **Champions League** in the final in Lisbon against FC Barcelona. After that Wälti moved to Juventus in Turin in Italy.

Wälti is **captain** of the Swiss women’s national team. With Switzerland she has played at World Cups and European Championships. In 2025 the European Championship took place in Switzerland, and the stadiums were often sold out. Switzerland reached the quarter-finals.

abschnitte.titel: Style of play and role model
abschnitte.text: In midfield Wälti is the player who brings calm to the game and spreads the passes. She wins a lot of balls and has a good overview. Off the pitch she campaigns for women’s football. She is a great role model for many girls in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: The leader of a team on the pitch.
The most important competition for club teams in Europe.
The area between defence and attack, where the play is built up.
A European Championship that takes place in your own country.

gewusst: Lia Wälti started playing football at FC Langnau at the age of eight.
The Women’s Euro 2025 in Switzerland broke several attendance records.

teile.einleitung: Feelings are what we sense inside ourselves: joy, sadness, anger, fear and much more. All people have feelings, and it helps to recognise them and deal with them well.
wichtigste: All feelings are allowed, including anger and sadness.
Laughing and jumping about are signs of joy.
Tears often show sadness.
Clenched fists and a red face often show anger.
Fear warns us of danger.
Empathy means sensing how someone else is feeling.

abschnitte.text: You can often see feelings on someone's face and body. A child who **laughs and jumps about** is happy. If someone has **tears** in their eyes and hangs their head, they are probably sad. **Clenched fists** and a red face are often signs of anger. If you recognise feelings, you understand others better. If you are not sure, you can simply ask.

**Anger** is a strong feeling. It shows that something is bothering you. When you are very angry, it helps to **breathe deeply**. That calms the body down. Some people count slowly to ten or go away for a moment. Afterwards it is easier to say what is bothering you without hurting anyone.

**Fear** is the feeling you have when you are afraid of something. It is useful, because it **warns us of danger**. For example, if you feel afraid at a steep spot, you take more care. But sometimes a fear is bigger than it needs to be. Then it is good to talk to someone about it.

When you have managed something difficult, for example finished painting a difficult picture, you feel **proud**. You feel **envy** when you want something that someone else has, or begrudge them it. Everyone knows this feeling sometimes. You can then think about what you are good at yourself. Or you can be happy for the other person.

**Empathy** means putting yourself in other people's shoes. You sense how someone else is feeling. Then you can help better, for example by comforting them or listening. **All feelings are allowed**, including anger and sadness. What matters is how you deal with them. If you talk about your feelings, you often feel a bit better already.

gewusst: Many facial expressions, such as smiling, are understood by people all over the world.
Even tiny babies show feelings such as joy or discomfort, long before they can talk.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Davis Cup team is the men’s national tennis team. In 2014, with Roger Federer and Stan Wawrinka, it won the Davis Cup for the first time. The Swiss women tennis players are strong too and won the Billie Jean King Cup in 2022.
wichtigste: The Davis Cup is the most important team competition in men’s tennis.
Switzerland won the Davis Cup in 2014 with Roger Federer.
In the 2014 final, Switzerland beat France in Lille.
Besides Federer, Stan Wawrinka played an important part.
Switzerland had already reached the final once, in 1992, but lost to the USA.
The Swiss women won the Billie Jean King Cup in 2022.
The Davis Cup has been held since 1900.

abschnitte.text: The **Davis Cup** is a tennis tournament for men’s national teams. It was founded in 1900 by the American Dwight Davis. That makes it one of the oldest team competitions in any sport. In a tie, two countries play several **singles** matches and one **doubles** match against each other. The country that wins more matches goes through.

In November 2014 Switzerland played **France** in the final in Lille. In front of around 27,000 spectators, Switzerland led 2:1 after two days. Then **Roger Federer** won his singles match against Richard Gasquet clearly in three sets. That sealed Switzerland’s first Davis Cup victory. The team also included **Stan Wawrinka**, Marco Chiudinelli and Michael Lammer, and the captain was Severin Lüthi.

Switzerland had already reached the Davis Cup final in 1992. At that time Marc Rosset and Jakob Hlasek played for Switzerland. In the final in the USA, the team lost to the hosts, who had stars such as Andre Agassi and Pete Sampras. That same year Marc Rosset had become Olympic champion in Barcelona. So the 2014 victory was the crowning glory after a long wait.

The women’s equivalent is the **Billie Jean King Cup**, formerly called the Fed Cup. In 1998 the Swiss women, with Martina Hingis and Patty Schnyder, reached the final but lost to Spain. In 2021 they were in the final again. Then in 2022 they won the title in Glasgow with a victory over Australia in the final. The team included **Belinda Bencic** and Jil Teichmann, and the captain was Heinz Günthardt.

For a small country, Switzerland has produced a surprising number of tennis stars. **Roger Federer** won 20 Grand Slam singles titles, Stan Wawrinka three. Martina Hingis was world number 1. Tennis in Switzerland is organised by the association **Swiss Tennis** in Biel.

begriffe.erklaerung: A match in which one person plays against another.
A match with two people on each side.
The person who looks after the team and picks the players.
The four most important tennis tournaments in the world.

gewusst: The Davis Cup trophy is a large silver bowl, and all the winning countries are engraved on its base.
In his career Roger Federer represented Switzerland in the Davis Cup and at the Olympic Games, and in 2008 in Beijing he won doubles gold with Wawrinka.
The Billie Jean King Cup is named after an American tennis legend who campaigned strongly for equal rights for women.

teile.einleitung: A prejudice is a judgement about people before you really know them. It often concerns a whole group, for example people from another country. Prejudices can be unfair and hurt others, but they can be broken down.
wichtigste: A stereotype is a simplified, fixed picture of a whole group.
Prejudices are not inborn; they are learnt, for example from family and the media.
Anyone who wrongly blames others for problems is making them a scapegoat.
Hostility towards foreigners is also called xenophobia and is often based on prejudice.
Confirmation bias keeps prejudices alive.
Getting to know people personally is the best help against prejudice.

abschnitte.text: The word says it already: you **pre-judge**, that is you judge before you know someone. Closely related is the **stereotype**, a simplified, fixed picture of a whole group. A sentence such as “All people with glasses are swots” is a **generalisation** of this kind. The word “all” makes a whole group look the same, without knowing the individuals. Pictures like this are never fair to individual people.

Nobody is born with prejudices. They are **learnt**, often without our noticing. Children take them on from the **people around them**, for example their family, their friends or the **media**. Prejudices are hard to change because people tend to notice what confirms their opinion. They easily overlook counter-examples. This thinking error is called **confirmation bias**.

The term **scapegoat** comes from an old ritual in the Bible. In it a goat symbolically carried the people’s guilt into the desert. Today it means people who are wrongly blamed for problems. A hostile attitude towards people from other countries or cultures is called **hostility towards foreigners** or **xenophobia**. It can lead to exclusion and disadvantage. In Switzerland the criminal law forbids publicly degrading people because of their origin or religion.

The best help is to **get to know people personally**. Then you soon notice that everyone is different and does not fit the prejudice. **Meeting** people and talking to them reduces mistrust.
