It also helps to check your own thoughts: is that really true of everyone? How do I know? If you ask questions like these, you are less likely to fall for prejudices.

gewusst: The word “xenophobia” comes from Greek: “xenos” means foreign, “phobos” means fear.
Even positive generalisations such as “Everyone from country X is good at maths” are stereotypes, because they ignore individuals.

teile.einleitung: Moral courage means standing up bravely for other people and for values in everyday life. People who show moral courage do not look away when they see injustice. One rule always applies: help, yes; put yourself in danger, no.
wichtigste: The German word Zivilcourage is made up of “zivil”, meaning civil, and “Courage”, meaning courage.
In dangerous situations the most important thing is to get help without putting yourself at risk.
If there is bullying in your class, it helps to tell a teacher.
In 1938, as police commander in St Gallen, Paul Grüninger saved hundreds of Jewish refugees.
In 1944 in Budapest, Carl Lutz saved tens of thousands of Jews with protective letters.
In 1955 Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat on the bus.
In 2014, at the age of 17, Malala Yousafzai received the Nobel Peace Prize.

abschnitte.text: **Moral courage**, Zivilcourage in German, literally means “civil courage”. People who show it stand up for others and for values such as justice, even when it is uncomfortable. It can start small: you speak up when someone is being laughed at. If there is **bullying** in your class, you can first tell a **teacher**. Getting help is not telling tales; it is moral courage.

In a dangerous situation the most important thing is: **get help without putting yourself at risk**. It often works best to speak to other people directly, for example “You in the red jumper, please help me!”. Then you call the **police** on 117. Later you can help as a witness if you have memorised **features** such as clothing, height or the direction someone ran off in. Making a statement to the police is also a form of moral courage.

**Paul Grüninger** was police commander in the canton of St Gallen. In 1938 he let hundreds of Jewish refugees into Switzerland even though the border was closed, getting round the regulations to do so. He was dismissed and only fully rehabilitated in 1995. The diplomat **Carl Lutz** was vice-consul in **Budapest**. In 1944 he issued many **protective letters** and so saved tens of thousands of Jews. He is considered one of the greatest rescuers of that time.

abschnitte.titel: Role models from around the world
abschnitte.text: In 1955 **Rosa Parks** in Montgomery in the USA refused to give up her seat on the bus to a white passenger. She was arrested, and her courage sparked a big **bus boycott**. In Germany, in 1942 and 1943, the group **White Rose**, led by Sophie and Hans Scholl, handed out leaflets against the Nazi regime. The brother and sister were executed in 1943. The Pakistani **Malala Yousafzai** campaigns for girls’ education. She was badly injured in an attack in 2012 and in 2014, at the age of 17, received the **Nobel Peace Prize**.

gewusst: Malala Yousafzai is the youngest person ever to receive a Nobel Peace Prize.
Paul Grüninger died in 1972, long before a court fully rehabilitated him in 1995.

teile.einleitung: Roger Federer is a Swiss tennis player from Basel and is considered one of the best tennis players of all time. He won 20 Grand Slam tournaments in singles, eight of them at Wimbledon. Many people all over the world admire his elegant style of play.
wichtigste: Roger Federer was born in Basel on 8 August 1981.
He won 20 Grand Slam singles titles.
He won Wimbledon eight times, a record among men.
He was world number 1 for 310 weeks in total.
In 2008 he won Olympic gold in the doubles with Stan Wawrinka.
In September 2022 he ended his career.
The record for the most Grand Slam titles among men is held by Novak Djokovic (as of 2026).

abschnitte.text: Roger Federer grew up in and around **Basel**. His mother comes from South Africa, his father from Switzerland. As a child he was a ball boy at the Swiss Indoors, the big tennis tournament in Basel. Later he won that very tournament ten times himself.

The four most important tennis tournaments are called the **Grand Slam**. Federer won 20 of them: Wimbledon eight times, the Australian Open six times, the US Open five times and the French Open once. He won his first Grand Slam title at Wimbledon in 2003. For a long time this gave him the record among men, until Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic overtook him.

Federer was at the top of the **world rankings** for 310 weeks in total. Of these, 237 weeks were in a row, which is still a record. He won 103 tournaments on the ATP Tour. His duels with Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic are among the most famous in tennis history.

In 2008 in Beijing Federer won the **gold medal** in the doubles with Stan Wawrinka. In 2012 in London he won silver in the singles. In 2014 he won the **Davis Cup** with Switzerland for the first time. He was voted Swiss Sportsman of the Year many times.

In 2003 Federer founded the Roger Federer Foundation. It supports children’s **education** in southern Africa and in Switzerland. Federer is married to Mirka Federer, who was a professional tennis player herself, and has four children. After several knee operations he played his last match in September 2022 at the Laver Cup in London.

begriffe.erklaerung: The four most important tennis tournaments: the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open.
A list that shows which players are currently the best.
A competition in which countries play each other at tennis.
The playing surface at Wimbledon. The ball bounces fast and low on it.

gewusst: As a child, Roger Federer was a ball boy at the tournament in Basel that he later won ten times.
In 2020 Switzerland issued a commemorative coin with Federer’s picture, a great honour for a living person.

teile.einleitung: Intergenerational justice asks what we owe to the people who will live after us. It is about the environment, the climate, government debt and pensions, that is about sharing burdens and opportunities fairly between young and old.
wichtigste: The Brundtland Report of 1987 coined the best-known definition of sustainability.
The intergenerational contract is an image for solidarity in pension provision.
The federal debt brake was approved by the people in 2001.
In 2024 the KlimaSeniorinnen (Senior Women for Climate Protection) won against Switzerland in Strasbourg.
Discounting gives future costs less weight than present ones.
On 3 March 2024 voters approved a 13th AVS pension payment.
Since 2015 Wales has had a Commissioner for Future Generations.

abschnitte.text: In 1987 the UN report **‘Our Common Future’** was published, led by the Norwegian **Gro Harlem Brundtland**. It is called the **Brundtland Report**. It coined the best-known definition of sustainable development: meeting the needs of the present without taking away the ability of future generations to meet theirs. This made consideration for coming generations a political goal.

The **intergenerational contract** is not a real contract. It is an image for the fact that the younger generation pays for the pensions of the older one and will later be provided for itself. On 3 March 2024 Swiss voters approved the **initiative for a 13th AVS pension payment** by about 58 per cent. The pension initiative to raise the retirement age was clearly rejected on the same day. The debate was very much about how the burden is shared between young and old.

Taking on debts today puts a burden on the future. That is why in 2001 Swiss voters approved the **debt brake** with about 85 per cent voting yes. It has been applied since 2003. Over a whole economic cycle, federal spending should not exceed income. An **economic cycle** is the ups and downs of the economy over several years.

On 9 April 2024 the **European Court of Human Rights** in Strasbourg ruled on a complaint by the association **KlimaSeniorinnen Schweiz**. It found that Switzerland had violated the right to respect for private and family life because it was doing too little against climate change. The judgment is often discussed in connection with duties towards coming generations. Opinions about it are divided in Switzerland.

In economic calculations, future costs and benefits are often **given less weight** than present ones. This method is called **discounting**. The higher the discount rate, the less future climate damage counts today. That is why choosing the rate is also an ethical question. Some countries create special offices for the future: since 2015 **Wales** has had a law obliging public bodies to consider long-term consequences, and it has a Commissioner for Future Generations.

gewusst: Gro Harlem Brundtland was the first woman to become Prime Minister of Norway.
The KlimaSeniorinnen are an association of older women who see themselves as particularly affected by heatwaves.

teile.einleitung: Nino Schurter is a Swiss mountain biker from the Grisons and is considered one of the best cross-country riders of all time. At the Olympic Games he won bronze, silver and gold, in exactly that order. On top of that he has ten elite world titles.
wichtigste: Nino Schurter was born in 1986 in Tersnaus in the canton of the Grisons.
He became famous through mountain biking.
His discipline is cross-country.
He won Olympic bronze in 2008, silver in 2012 and gold in 2016.
He has been elite world champion ten times.
He has won the overall World Cup nine times.
With 36 World Cup victories he holds a record.

abschnitte.text: Nino Schurter was born on 13 May 1986 in **Tersnaus** in the Val Lumnezia. The valley lies in the Surselva in the canton of the Grisons. He grew up in an area where Romansh is spoken. Today he lives in **Chur**.

Schurter rides **cross-country**, the Olympic discipline in mountain biking. All the riders start at the same time and ride several laps of a difficult course. There are steep climbs, roots, rock gardens and fast descents. Schurter is known for his technique on the descents and his strong final sprint.

At the 2008 Olympic Games in **Beijing**, Schurter won bronze. In 2012 in London he won silver, just behind the Czech Jaroslav Kulhavý. In 2016 in **Rio de Janeiro** he finally became Olympic champion. In 2021 in Tokyo he just missed out on a medal, finishing fourth.

Schurter has been elite **world champion** ten times, first in 2009 and most recently in 2022. He has won the **overall World Cup**, the ranking for the whole season, nine times. With 36 World Cup race wins, he has won more races than any other man in cross-country. He has ridden for the Scott-SRAM team for many years.

Schurter has made mountain biking very well known in Switzerland. In **Lenzerheide**, not far from Chur, World Cup races and World Championships take place. Thousands of fans cheer him on there. Many children take up mountain biking because of him.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mountain bike race with a mass start over a hilly lap.
A series of races in different countries over one season.
The category for adult top athletes.
A last, fast attack shortly before the finish.

gewusst: Nino Schurter won his three Olympic medals in exactly the order bronze, silver and gold.
Thirteen years passed between his first and his tenth world title.

teile.einleitung: Someone who is helpful helps others when they need support. It can be something small, like carrying bags, or something important, like getting help after an accident.
wichtigste: Helpfulness means helping others when they need it.
If a child is crying because they have fallen over, you go over and help.
Before you help, it is best to ask whether the help is wanted.
In Switzerland you reach the ambulance on 144 and the fire brigade on 118.
Children and teenagers with worries can call the number 147.
You can help at home too, for example by laying the table.
Anyone who has been helped says ‘thank you’.

abschnitte.titel: Small acts of help every day
abschnitte.text: Helpfulness begins with small things. If a child has fallen over and is crying, you go over, comfort them and fetch an adult if necessary. If an older man is carrying heavy bags up the stairs, you ask kindly whether you can help. Asking is important, because not everyone wants help. In this way you show **consideration** and **respect**.

A family works better if everyone helps. You can **lay the table**, clear it, tidy your room or help carry the shopping. Helping little brothers and sisters get dressed is also helpful. If you help, you learn responsibility and take some of the load off the others.

After a serious accident you get help straight away. In Switzerland you call the **ambulance** on **144**, the **fire brigade** on **118** and the **police** on **117**. The European emergency number **112** also works. On the phone you say calmly who you are, where you are and what has happened. That is important help too, even if you cannot do anything else yourself.

Children and teenagers who have worries can call the number **147**. There, trained people listen and help, free of charge and in confidence. The number belongs to the foundation **Pro Juventute**. You can also call if you are worried about a friend. Getting help is brave and right.

Anyone who receives help says **‘thank you’**. This shows that you value the help. Helpfulness not only makes others happy, but often you too. Many people in Switzerland even help in their free time, for example in clubs or the fire brigade. This unpaid work is called **volunteering**.

gewusst: In many Swiss municipalities the fire brigade is made up largely of volunteers who help alongside their jobs.
You can not only call the number 147, you can also get in touch by chat or message.

teile.einleitung: Justice means that people are treated fairly and each person gets what they are entitled to. People have been thinking about what exactly is just since ancient times.
wichtigste: Justitia, the figure of justice, carries scales and a sword.
The blindfold stands for judging without regard to who someone is.
In justice according to need, everyone gets what they need.
Equality of opportunity means the same possibilities for everyone.
Aristotle distinguished between distributive and corrective justice.
John Rawls invented the ‘veil of ignorance’.
The Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne is Switzerland's highest court.

abschnitte.text: Justice is often shown as a woman, **Justitia** (Lady Justice). In her hands she holds **scales** and a **sword**. The scales stand for careful weighing up, the sword for enforcing the law. She often wears a **blindfold**. It shows that the law applies equally to everyone, without regard to who they are. In Bern there is the **Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen** (Fountain of Justice) with such a figure.

A simple form of justice is **equal distribution**. If three children share 12 biscuits equally, each gets 4 biscuits. But equal is not always just. In **justice according to need**, those who need more get more, for example a child who is ill gets more help. In **justice according to merit**, you receive according to what you have achieved.

**Equality of opportunity** means that everyone should have the same starting conditions, for example in access to education. What you make of them is then up to you. In 1971, in ‘A Theory of Justice’, the philosopher **John Rawls** described the **veil of ignorance**. You should choose rules without knowing what place you yourself will have in society. This produces rules that are fair for everyone.

The Greek philosopher **Aristotle** was already thinking about justice. In the ‘Nicomachean Ethics’ he distinguished two kinds. **Distributive justice** concerns how goods and honours are shared out in a community. **Corrective justice** concerns, for example, fair exchanges or compensation for damage. This distinction is still used today.

To make sure the law is applied fairly, there are **courts**. In Switzerland the cantonal courts give judgment first. The country's highest court is the **Federal Supreme Court**. Its main seat is in **Lausanne**, and as the last instance it reviews judgments of the cantonal courts. Independent courts are an important part of the **rule of law**.

gewusst: The Fountain of Justice in Bern dates from the 16th century.
Besides Lausanne, the Federal Supreme Court also has a site in Lucerne.

teile.einleitung: Ditaji Kambundji is a Swiss athlete from Bern. Her special events are the hurdles over 100 and 60 metres. In 2025 in Tokyo she sensationally became world champion in the 100 metres hurdles.
wichtigste: Ditaji Kambundji was born in Bern on 20 May 2002.
In 2025 in Tokyo she became world champion in the 100 metres hurdles.
There are ten hurdles in a 100-metre hurdles race.
In 2025 she also became European indoor champion over 60 metres hurdles, with a European record.
In 2024 she won European Championship silver in the 100 metres hurdles in Rome.
Her older sister is the sprinter Mujinga Kambundji.
She is the youngest of four sisters.

abschnitte.text: **Ditaji Kambundji** was born in **Bern** on 20 May 2002. Her mother is Swiss and her father comes from the Congo. She is the youngest of four sisters. Her sister **Mujinga Kambundji** is one of the best sprinters in Europe. Her sister Muswama is also an athlete and a bobsledder.

In the women’s **100 metres hurdles** there are **ten hurdles** on the track. Each hurdle is 84 centimetres high. The first hurdle comes after 13 metres, then the hurdles follow every 8.5 metres. The runners take exactly three steps between two hurdles. So it takes speed, technique and a perfect **rhythm**.

At the **2025 World Championships in Tokyo**, Kambundji pulled off the big surprise. She won the 100 metres hurdles final and became **world champion**. That puts her among the very few Swiss women athletes with an outdoor world title. The whole of Switzerland celebrated her success. It was one of the greatest moments in Swiss athletics.

Even as a junior Kambundji was very successful; in 2021 she became European under-20 champion. In 2022 she won European Championship bronze in Munich, and in 2024 **European silver** in Rome. There she ran a **Swiss record** of 12.40 seconds. In March 2025 in Apeldoorn she became **European indoor champion** over 60 metres hurdles. With 7.67 seconds she set a European record.

abschnitte.titel: A role model for young athletes
abschnitte.text: The Kambundji sisters have had a big influence on Swiss athletics. Thanks to them many children in Switzerland take up sprinting and hurdles. Ditaji grew up in **Bern** and competes for a Bern club. She shows that you can be among the best in the world even if you come from a small country. Her cheerful manner makes her very popular.

begriffe.erklaerung: A sprint in which you have to jump over obstacles called hurdles.
The best performance ever achieved by a European woman.
Competitions in winter in an indoor hall, often over shorter distances.
The even sequence of steps between the hurdles.

gewusst: Men run 110 metres hurdles with higher hurdles than women.
Ditaji and Mujinga Kambundji have both won medals at European Championships.
Knocking over a hurdle does not get you disqualified, but it usually costs you time.

teile.einleitung: Simone Niggli-Luder is a Swiss orienteer and one of Switzerland’s most successful sportswomen. She became world champion 23 times. In orienteering you need not only fast legs, but also a clever head.
wichtigste: Simone Niggli-Luder was born on 9 January 1978 and comes from the canton of Bern.
She won 23 world titles in orienteering.
In orienteering you need a map and a compass.
She also won the overall World Cup several times.
She was voted Swiss Sportswoman of the Year several times.
In 2013 she ended her career as a top athlete.

abschnitte.text: Simone Niggli-Luder comes from the canton of **Bern**. She studied biology at the University of Bern. She got to know orienteering as a child. From the early 2000s she was one of the best in the world for more than a decade.

In **orienteering**, OL for short in German, you run through forests and countryside. You have to find several **controls** one after another, which are marked on a map. For this you have only a map and a compass with you. Whoever chooses the best route and runs fast wins.

Simone Niggli became **world champion** 23 times in total. She won her first title in 2001 and her last in 2013. She won races over short, middle and long distances as well as in the relay. That makes her the most successful orienteer of all time.

Orienteering is a popular sport in Switzerland for all age groups. There are many races for families and schools. With her successes Simone Niggli made orienteering much better known in Switzerland. She was voted **Swiss Sportswoman of the Year** several times, even though orienteering is not often on television.

Simone Niggli is married and the mother of three children. Even after her children were born she won more world titles. That shows how well she was able to combine sport and family. After retiring in 2013 she continued to work for the sport of orienteering.

begriffe.erklaerung: A running sport in which you use a map and compass to find controls in the countryside.
A checkpoint with a red and white marker that you have to find.
A device whose needle points north.
A competition in which several runners run one after another for a team.

gewusst: In orienteering you often only see the map at the start, so you cannot practise the course beforehand.
Simone Niggli won more orienteering world titles than any other runner in history.

teile.einleitung: Children's rights are special rights for everyone under 18. They are set out in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child and are meant to protect children, help them develop and give them a voice.
wichtigste: The UN adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child on 20 November 1989.
Every person under 18 counts as a child.
Switzerland joined the Convention in 1997.
The well-being of the child must come first in all decisions.
Article 12 guarantees the right to be heard.
Children's rights also include education, play and leisure.
The USA is the only UN member that has not ratified the Convention (as of 2025).

abschnitte.titel: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
abschnitte.text: The **UN General Assembly** adopted the **Convention on the Rights of the Child** on **20 November 1989**. That is why 20 November is the international day of children's rights. According to Article 1, every person **under 18** counts as a child. Almost every country in the world has ratified the Convention, that is accepted it as binding. Only the **USA** has signed it but never ratified it (as of 2025).

**Switzerland** ratified the Convention in **1997**. Since then it has had to report regularly to the UN on how it is putting children's rights into practice. A committee of experts examines these reports and makes recommendations. There was a link with Switzerland even earlier: in 1924 the League of Nations in **Geneva** adopted a first declaration on the rights of the child.

Article 3 requires that the **best interests of the child** be a primary consideration in all measures. This applies to courts, authorities and schools. According to Article 12, children have the **right to be heard**: they may give their opinion on everything that affects them. This opinion must be taken into account according to their age and maturity. In addition, children must not be disadvantaged, no matter where they come from.

Every child has a **right to education**. If children have to work in factories instead of going to school, this right is violated. The Convention also protects children from economic exploitation and violence. Article 31 guarantees the **right to play and leisure**, to rest and to cultural activities. Playing is important for healthy development.

The UN's children's fund is called **UNICEF**. It was founded in **1946** and works for children's rights all over the world. UNICEF helps with health, clean water, education and protection, especially in poor countries and in disasters. In Switzerland other organisations also work for children's rights, for example Pro Juventute with its helpline number 147.

gewusst: The Convention on the Rights of the Child is the human rights treaty that more countries around the world have joined than any other.
The Convention has 54 articles and applies to every child, whatever their language, religion or origin.

teile.einleitung: Mujinga Kambundji is a Swiss athlete from Bern and the most successful sprinter in Switzerland. She has twice been world indoor champion over 60 metres and in 2022 became European champion over 200 metres. With her successes she has made sprinting well known in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Mujinga Kambundji was born in Bern in 1992.
Her father comes from the Congo, and her mother is Swiss.
Her strength is sprinting over 60, 100 and 200 metres.
In 2019 she won bronze over 200 metres at the World Championships in Doha.
In 2022 she became world indoor champion over 60 metres in Belgrade.
That same year she became European champion over 200 metres in Munich.
Her younger sister Ditaji is a successful hurdler.

abschnitte.text: Mujinga Kambundji was born in **Bern** on 17 June 1992. Her father comes from the Democratic Republic of the **Congo**, her mother from Switzerland. She has three sisters, who also do sport. Even as a child she was the fastest at school.

A **sprint** is a race over a short distance as fast as possible. Outdoors you run 100 or 200 metres, indoors usually 60 metres. A good **start** from the starting blocks and a high top speed are important. The best women run 100 metres in under eleven seconds.

In 2019 Kambundji won bronze over 200 metres at the World Championships in **Doha**. It was the first World Championship medal for a Swiss woman sprinter. She has also set several **Swiss records**, for example over 100 and 200 metres. That put her among the best in the world.

In 2022 she became world indoor champion over 60 metres in **Belgrade**. In the summer of 2022 she became European champion over 200 metres in Munich. Later she won the world indoor title over 60 metres a second time. She has also won gold at European Indoor Championships, for example in Istanbul in 2023.

Her younger sister **Ditaji Kambundji** is a 100 metres hurdler and also world class. The sisters support each other. Mujinga Kambundji has been voted Swiss Sportswoman of the Year several times. She shows that you can reach the top of the world in sprinting even from a small country.

begriffe.erklaerung: A race over a short distance at top speed.
A device on the ground that sprinters push off from at the start.
A World Championship held in winter in an indoor arena.
The best performance ever achieved.

gewusst: For the best women, a 60-metre race takes only just over seven seconds.
The four Kambundji sisters are all sporty, and two of them are among the best in the world.

teile.einleitung: Rules say what is allowed and what is not. They help people to live together well and safely. There are rules at school, on the roads, in games and throughout the country.
wichtigste: Rules exist so that everyone can live together well.
As a pedestrian you may cross the road when the light is green.
At zebra crossings in Switzerland the rule is: ‘Warte, luege, lose, laufe’.
If you want to say something in class, you put up your hand.
A class can agree rules together with the teacher.
A cycle helmet protects your head when cycling.
Rules that apply to everyone in a country are called laws.

abschnitte.text: At school there are rules so that **everyone can get on well** and learn. If you want to say something, you **put up your hand**, so that not everyone talks at once. Often the **class** agrees rules together with the **teacher**. Rules like these are easier to understand, and people are happier to keep to them. In the playground, the usual rule for ball games is: do not hit anyone with the ball on purpose.

On the **roads**, rules protect people from accidents. As a pedestrian you cross the road when the light is **green** and wait when it is red. Before crossing at a zebra crossing, children in Switzerland learn: **‘Warte, luege, lose, laufe’**. In Swiss German this means: stop, look left and right, listen, and only then walk. When **cycling** it is best to wear a **cycle helmet**; it protects your head if you fall.

Every game has **rules**. They make sure that the game is fair and that everyone has the same chances. If nobody keeps to the rules, there is often a **quarrel**. You can also change the rules together if everyone agrees. The only important thing is to agree before the game starts.

Rules that apply to everyone in a country are called **laws**. In Switzerland **parliament** decides on federal laws. But the people can have a say: with a **referendum** they can vote on a law. The **cantons** and **municipalities** also have their own rules. Anyone who does not keep to the law can expect a penalty.

gewusst: The saying ‘Warte, luege, lose, laufe’ is Swiss German and is already practised in kindergarten.
In Switzerland the people can vote directly on many laws, which is rare in the world.

teile.einleitung: An ethical dilemma is a predicament: you have to choose between two options, and each one breaks an important duty. Philosophy, psychology and law use such dilemmas to think about morality.
wichtigste: In a real dilemma, two duties rule each other out.
Lawrence Kohlberg used the Heinz dilemma to study moral development.
The highest level in Kohlberg's scheme is the post-conventional level.
The plank of Carneades is an ancient thought experiment.
The tragedy of the commons describes the overuse of shared resources.
In the prisoner's dilemma, self-interest leads both into a worse outcome.
The principle of double effect goes back to Thomas Aquinas.

abschnitte.text: In a **moral dilemma** there are two well-founded duties, but you can only fulfil one. Whoever chooses one inevitably breaks the other. So there is **no way out without a moral loss**. A very old example is the **plank of Carneades**: two shipwrecked men fight over a plank that can only carry one. The Greek philosopher Carneades asked whether you may push the other one away. In law this is regarded as an example of excusable necessity.

The psychologist **Lawrence Kohlberg** presented people with the **Heinz dilemma**. In it, a man wonders whether he should steal an unaffordable medicine for his terminally ill wife. Kohlberg was not interested in the answer but in the **reasoning**. From this he developed stages of moral development. At the highest, the **post-conventional level**, people are guided by general principles such as justice, even against the rules in force.

In 1968, in the journal ‘Science’, **Garrett Hardin** described the **tragedy of the commons**. If everyone takes their own advantage from a shared pasture, it is destroyed for everyone. The economist **Elinor Ostrom** later showed that communities such as Swiss **alpine pasture cooperatives** can prevent this with clever rules. Similarly, the **prisoner's dilemma** from game theory shows: betrayal pays off for each person individually, but staying silent together would be better.

In 2006 Germany's Federal Constitutional Court ruled on shooting down a hijacked passenger plane with innocent people on board. It declared the rule in the Aviation Security Act **unconstitutional**. The state must not sacrifice innocent people as mere objects, and human lives must **not be weighed against each other**. Questions like these show how hard dilemmas are in real life.

The **principle of double effect** goes back to **Thomas Aquinas**. Under certain conditions it allows a good action even if a terrible side effect can be foreseen. But the terrible effect must not be intended and must not be the means to the end. Garrett Hardin's **lifeboat ethics** of 1974 is controversial. He compared rich countries to a lifeboat that sinks if it is overloaded and rejected unlimited aid. His position was strongly criticised.

gewusst: In 2009 Elinor Ostrom became the first woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Economics.
Garrett Hardin deliberately set his lifeboat ethics against the image of ‘spaceship Earth’.

teile.einleitung: Kilian Wenger is a Swiss wrestler from the Bernese Oberland. In 2010 in Frauenfeld he won the Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival and became Schwingerkönig, the king of Swiss wrestling, at only 20. That makes him one of the best-known athletes in this typically Swiss national sport.
wichtigste: Kilian Wenger was born in 1990 and comes from the Diemtig valley in the canton of Bern.
His sport is Schwingen, a kind of wrestling in trousers made of tough fabric.
In 2010 he became Schwingerkönig in Frauenfeld.
At the time he was only 20 years old.
He belongs to the Bern cantonal wrestling association.
He won many wreath festivals and mountain wreaths.
As Schwingerkönig he became known all over Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Kilian Wenger was born in 1990 and grew up in **Horboden** in the Diemtig valley. The valley is in the Bernese Oberland, not far from Spiez. Many wrestlers come from rural areas with a long wrestling tradition. Wenger started wrestling as a boy.

**Schwingen** is a traditional Swiss one-on-one contest. Two wrestlers fight in a round ring of **sawdust**. They wear short trousers of tough fabric over their clothes and hold on to them. Whoever gets their opponent onto his back in the sawdust with both shoulder blades down wins the bout.

The **Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival** takes place every three years and is the most important wrestling festival. In 2010 it was held in Frauenfeld in the canton of Thurgau. Kilian Wenger won the final bout and became Schwingerkönig. At 20 he was one of the youngest kings in history.

In Schwingen there is no prize money as in many other sports. The best wrestlers receive a **wreath** of oak leaves. At the Federal Festival there is a prize table with gifts, and the most important is often a bull, the **winner’s Muni**. Wenger won many wreath festivals in his career.

Schwingen is very popular in Switzerland; more than 50,000 spectators come to the Federal Festival. Kilian Wenger’s victory in 2010 made him famous at a stroke. He showed that even very young wrestlers can become king. To this day he is a role model for many young wrestlers.

begriffe.erklaerung: The winner of the Federal Wrestling Festival.
Finely ground wood on which wrestling takes place, so that falls are soft.
The last and most important bout of a wrestling festival.
A wreath of oak leaves awarded to the best wrestlers.

gewusst: In Schwingen it is a tradition for the winner to brush the sawdust off the loser’s back after the bout.
The winner’s Muni at a Federal Festival is a live bull.

teile.einleitung: The trolley problem is one of the best-known thought experiments in ethics. It asks whether you may cause harm in order to prevent greater harm. Today it also plays a part in the debate about self-driving cars.
wichtigste: The British philosopher Philippa Foot formulated the problem in 1967.
In 1976 Judith Jarvis Thomson coined the name ‘trolley problem’.
In the basic version, a utilitarian would switch the points.
The doctrine of double effect distinguishes intended consequences from those that are accepted.
Many people find pushing a man off a bridge more wrong, because he is used as a means.
With the ‘Moral Machine’, MIT collected millions of judgements about autonomous vehicles.
German guidelines from 2017 forbid choosing victims by age or other characteristics.

abschnitte.text: A tram, in American English a **trolley**, is rolling out of control towards five people. You could switch the **points**, and then it would go onto another track where one person is standing. Should you switch them? The British philosopher **Philippa Foot** formulated the example in an essay in **1967**. It is an imaginary situation meant to help people think about moral principles.

In **1976** the American **Judith Jarvis Thomson** coined the name **‘trolley problem’** and invented further versions. In the **bridge version**, you could only stop the tram by pushing a man off a bridge onto the tracks. Many people find this much worse than switching the points, even though the result would be the same. One reason: the man would be used as a **mere means**. With the points, the death is a side effect.

For **utilitarianism**, the consequences count: one victim is less bad than five, so a utilitarian would **switch the points**. Other approaches stress that people must not be used as a means, as Kant demanded. The **doctrine of double effect**, which goes back to **Thomas Aquinas**, distinguishes between **intended** consequences and those that are only **accepted**. Philosophers use it to try to explain why the two versions feel so different.

Today the question arises in a new form: how should an **autonomous vehicle** decide in an unavoidable accident? With the online experiment **‘Moral Machine’**, **MIT** in the USA collected millions of judgements from all over the world. The results were published in the journal ‘Nature’ in 2018 and showed differences between regions of the world. In **2017** a German **ethics commission** laid down that victims must not be chosen according to **personal characteristics such as age**.

Courts have also had to rule on similar questions. A German law allowed a hijacked passenger plane to be shot down in order to save other people. In **2006** the **Federal Constitutional Court** declared this rule **incompatible with human dignity** and void. The passengers must not be treated as mere objects for saving others.

gewusst: Philippa Foot was originally not interested in trams at all, but in the doctrine of double effect.
The trolley problem is one of the most discussed examples in ethics and is often talked about in schools and universities.

teile.einleitung: Christian Stucki is a former Swiss wrestler from the Bernese Seeland. In 2019 he became Schwingerkönig, the king of Swiss wrestling, at the Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival in Zug. At 34 he was then the oldest king in history.
wichtigste: Christian Stucki was born in 1985 and comes from the Bernese Seeland.
In 2019 he won the title of Schwingerkönig in Zug.
He was the oldest wrestler ever to win the title of king.
In the final bout he beat Joel Wicki from Lucerne.
Almost two metres tall and weighing around 150 kilograms, he was a giant in the sawdust.
In 2017 he also won the Unspunnen wrestling festival.
He ended his career in 2023.

abschnitte.text: **Christian Stucki** was born on 7 June 1985 and lives in **Lyss** in the Bernese Seeland. He is about 1.98 metres tall and at his peak weighed around 150 kilograms. That is why many called him the gentle giant. Alongside his sport he worked as a lorry driver. He is known for his friendly and modest manner.

The **Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival** takes place only every three years and is the most important event in Swiss wrestling. In 2019 it was held in **Zug**, in front of more than 50,000 spectators in the arena. Stucki fought his way into the **final bout** and beat Joel Wicki there. In this way he became Schwingerkönig at the age of 34. No wrestler before him had been so old when he won the title of king.

At the Federal Festival the winner gets no prize money but a live **Muni**, a bull for breeding. In 2019 Christian Stucki won the bull **Kolin**. The best wrestlers also get a wreath of oak leaves. Anyone who wins a federal wreath may call himself an **Eidgenosse**. Stucki won many wreaths in the course of his career.

Stucki won several big wrestling festivals. In 2017 he won the **Unspunnen festival** in Interlaken, an event especially rich in tradition. He also won many wreath festivals all over Switzerland. For a long time he was one of the best wrestlers without being king. That made the joy at his late title all the greater.

**Schwingen** is a traditional Swiss form of wrestling. Bouts take place in a round ring of **sawdust**. The wrestlers wear short trousers of tough fabric over their clothes, the Zwilchhosen, which they grip each other by. The winner is the one who puts his opponent on his back with both shoulder blades on the ground. After the bout the winner brushes the sawdust off the loser’s back as a sign of respect.

begriffe.erklaerung: The winner of the Federal Wrestling and Alpine Festival.
The last and deciding bout at a wrestling festival.
Short over-trousers of tough fabric by which the wrestlers grip each other.
Swiss German for a breeding bull.
An award made of oak leaves for the best wrestlers at a festival.

gewusst: At almost two metres tall, Christian Stucki was one of the tallest wrestlers of his time.
More than 400,000 people came to the festival grounds in Zug for the festival at which Stucki became king.
The Schwingerkönig keeps his title for three years, until the next Federal Festival.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss national floorball teams are among the best in the world. Floorball, called Unihockey in Switzerland, is a fast indoor sport played with a light plastic ball and sticks. The Swiss women have already been world champions twice, and the men have won many World Championship medals.
wichtigste: Unihockey is called floorball internationally and comes from Sweden.
By 2025 the Swiss women had been world champions twice, in 2005 and 2019.
The Swiss men won silver at the 1998 World Championship.
Since then the men have won many bronze medals.
The big rivals are Sweden, Finland and the Czech Republic.
Floorball is one of the most popular team sports among young people in Switzerland.
The association is called Swiss Unihockey.

abschnitte.text: **Floorball** is a kind of indoor hockey. It is played with a light plastic stick and a plastic ball with 26 holes. Each team has five outfield players on the court and a goalkeeper, who plays without a stick. The court is 40 metres long and 20 metres wide and is surrounded by low **boards**. A game lasts three periods of 20 minutes.

The sport came about in the 1970s in **Sweden**. From there it spread to Finland and Switzerland. There have been world championships for men since 1996 and for women since 1997. To this day Sweden and Finland dominate most tournaments. Switzerland, together with the Czech Republic, is the most important challenger.

The Swiss women became world champions for the first time in **2005** in Singapore. In 2019 they won the title again at the **home World Championship in Neuchâtel**. That makes them world champions twice by 2025. On top of that they have many other World Championship medals. The women’s Nati is one of the most successful Swiss national teams of all.

The men won silver at the **1998 World Championship** in the Czech Republic, their best result so far. Since then they have won many **bronze medals**, but against Sweden and Finland it was usually not quite enough. In 2012 Switzerland hosted the men’s World Championship in Bern and Zurich. The games attracted many spectators. Well-known players such as Matthias Hofbauer shaped the Nati for many years.

In Switzerland there are tens of thousands of registered players. Floorball is especially popular with children, because you only need a stick and a ball. Many first get to know it in **school sport**. The top league is called the **Unihockey Prime League**. Well-known clubs include SV Wiler-Ersigen and Floorball Köniz.

begriffe.erklaerung: The international name for Unihockey.
The low surround of the court.
In floorball plays without a stick and blocks the ball with their body.
Hitting an opponent’s stick, which is not allowed.

gewusst: A floorball weighs only about 23 grams, less than a letter.
The name Unihockey comes from a company that used to make the sticks.
In Switzerland, floorball is one of the biggest team sports among young people after football.

teile.einleitung: Nicola Spirig is a former Swiss triathlete from the Zurich Unterland. In 2012 in London she became Olympic champion after a photo finish decided the winner. Four years later she won silver in Rio.
wichtigste: Nicola Spirig was born in 1982 in Bülach in the canton of Zurich.
Her sport is triathlon.
A triathlon consists of swimming, cycling and running, in that order.
In 2012 she became Olympic champion in London.
The race was decided by a photo finish.
In 2016 she won Olympic silver in Rio de Janeiro.
Alongside her sport she completed a law degree.

abschnitte.text: Nicola Spirig was born on 7 February 1982 in **Bülach** in the canton of Zurich. Even as a child she did a lot of sport, including athletics and swimming. Her talent for endurance sports showed early. Later she became a professional triathlete.

A **triathlon** is made up of three sports one straight after another: swimming, cycling and running. Over the Olympic distance you swim 1.5 kilometres, cycle 40 kilometres and run 10 kilometres. The changes between the parts take place in the **transition area**. The clock keeps running, so the changes have to be very fast.

At the 2012 Olympic Games in **London**, Spirig crossed the finishing line at the same time as the Swede Lisa Nordén. Both had exactly the same time. Only the **photo finish** showed that Spirig was just ahead. So she won the gold medal, the second Swiss gold in women’s triathlon after Brigitte McMahon in 2000.

In 2016 in **Rio de Janeiro**, Spirig won silver behind the American Gwen Jorgensen. She also became European triathlon champion several times. Altogether she took part in five Olympic Games. In 2021 in Tokyo she raced her last Olympic race.

Spirig is married to the former triathlete **Reto Hug**. They have several children. Alongside top-level sport she studied law at the University of Zurich. She showed that sport, education and family can be combined.

begriffe.erklaerung: A competition of swimming, cycling and running one after another.
A photo taken exactly at the finishing line that shows who arrived first.
The place where you change from swimming to cycling and from cycling to running.
The ability to keep doing sport for a long time without a break.

gewusst: At her Olympic victory in 2012, Nicola Spirig was only a few centimetres ahead of her rival.
Triathlon has only been an Olympic sport since 2000.

teile.einleitung: Didier Cuche is a former Swiss ski racer from the canton of Neuchâtel. He was one of the best speed racers of his time and won the legendary downhill on the Streif in Kitzbühel five times. In 2009 he became world champion in the super-G.
wichtigste: Didier Cuche was born in 1974 and comes from Le Pâquier in the Neuchâtel Jura.
He won five times on the Streif in Kitzbühel, more often than any other downhill racer.
In 2009 he became super-G world champion in Val d’Isère.
In 1998 he won Olympic silver in the super-G in Nagano.
He won the World Cup downhill ranking four times.
He became known for his ski flip at the finish, in which he threw one ski up into the air.
He retired from top-level sport in 2012.

abschnitte.text: **Didier Cuche** was born on 16 August 1974 and grew up in **Le Pâquier** in the Neuchâtel Jura. The region is known more for cross-country skiing than for downhill racing. Even so, Cuche learnt to ski fast early on. Alongside his sport he trained as a **butcher**. His mother tongue is French.

The **Streif** in Kitzbühel is considered the most dangerous and most famous downhill in the world. Cuche won there five times, more than any other racer. He celebrated his victories in 1998, 2008, 2010, 2011 and 2012. That makes him the record winner of the **Hahnenkamm downhill**. Because of this he was very popular with the fans in Austria.

In 2009 in **Val d’Isère** in France, Cuche became world champion in the **super-G**, and he won silver in the downhill. As early as 1998 he had won Olympic silver in the super-G in Nagano. He won the **downhill ranking** in the World Cup four times, plus other small crystal globes. Altogether he celebrated 21 World Cup victories. That makes him one of the most successful Swiss skiers.

Cuche also became famous for a special gesture at the finish. After the race he stood one **ski** upright, let it tip over and flicked it high into the air with his foot. Then he caught it again. This **ski flip** became his trademark. Many children tried to copy it.

In January 2012 Cuche announced that he would retire at the end of the season. A few days later he won in Kitzbühel for the fifth time, a perfect farewell. By then he was already 37, much older than most of his rivals. After his career he worked for a ski manufacturer and as an **ambassador** for skiing. He is seen as a modest and fair sportsman.

begriffe.erklaerung: The famous downhill course on the Hahnenkamm in Kitzbühel.
A fast discipline between the downhill and the giant slalom.
A win in a race of the World Cup series.
The annual ski races in Kitzbühel.

gewusst: Ten years passed between Cuche’s first and second victories in Kitzbühel.
At his last win in Kitzbühel, Cuche was 37, an unusually high age for a downhill winner.
Didier Cuche raced his last season at the age of 37 and still won several World Cup races in it.

teile.einleitung: A generation is a group of people who were born at roughly the same time. A family often includes three or four generations: children, parents, grandparents and sometimes great-grandparents.
wichtigste: In the **intergenerational contract**, people in work pay the pensions of older people.
Switzerland has had the AVS (old-age insurance) since 1948.
The baby boomers are the large age groups born after the Second World War.
Generation Z was born roughly between 1997 and 2012.
Pro Senectute has been working for older people since 1917.
The International Day of Older Persons is on 1 October.

abschnitte.text: A **generation** includes people who were born at roughly the same time and have had similar experiences. The large age groups born after the Second World War are called **baby boomers**. After 1945 a great many children were born in many countries. **Generation Z** was born roughly between 1997 and 2012. It grew up with smartphones and the internet. After that comes **Generation Alpha**.

The **Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (AVS)** is the most important pillar of Swiss pension provision. The people approved it in 1947, and the first pensions were paid out in 1948. The AVS works on the **pay-as-you-go system**. People in work pay today's pensions with their contributions. Later they receive pensions themselves from the younger generation. This principle is called the **intergenerational contract**.

The Swiss foundation **Pro Senectute** has been working for older people since 1917. The name is Latin and means ‘for old age’. It offers advice, courses and support for older people. Since 1991 the UN has marked the International Day of Older Persons every year on **1 October**. It honours the achievements of older people.

In a **multi-generation house**, young and old deliberately live together and help each other. Older people look after children, for example, and younger people help with shopping or with the computer. In this way all generations benefit. Grandparents who look after their grandchildren are another example of generations being there for each other.

Each generation grows up in different conditions. This can lead to differences of opinion, for example about fashion, music or technology. This is called a **generation gap** or conflict between generations. If people listen to each other, they can learn a lot from each other. The younger ones often know new technology, while the older ones have a lot of life experience.

gewusst: The 1947 vote on the AVS was approved by a large majority.
The word ‘senior’ comes from the Latin ‘senex’, old.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss national football team is the men’s team that represents Switzerland at World Cups and European Championships. Fans lovingly call it the “Nati”. At the 2026 World Cup in North America it made it to the quarter-finals.
wichtigste: The Swiss national football team is often called the “Nati”.
The first international match took place in 1905 against France.
At the 2026 World Cup the Nati reached the quarter-finals.
Switzerland hosted a football World Cup in 1954.
At Euro 2021 Switzerland beat world champions France on penalties.
The record goal scorer is Alexander Frei, the most capped player Granit Xhaka.
The Nati is run by the Swiss Football Association.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Football Association** was founded in 1895 and is one of the oldest in the world. Switzerland played its first international match in 1905 in Paris against France. At the 1924 Olympic Games in Paris it won the **silver medal**. In the 1930s it reached the World Cup quarter-finals twice. Switzerland is also home to the football governing bodies **FIFA** in Zurich and **UEFA** in Nyon.

In 1954 the **football World Cup** took place in Switzerland. The Nati reached the quarter-finals and lost there 5:7 to Austria in Lausanne. To this day it is the highest-scoring match in World Cup history. The final in Bern’s Wankdorf Stadium was won by Germany against Hungary. This match became famous as the **Miracle of Bern**.

Since the 2000s Switzerland has almost always qualified for the big tournaments. At **Euro 2021** it beat world champions France on penalties in the round of 16. At Euro 2024 in Germany it again reached the quarter-finals and only went out on penalties against England. At the **2026 World Cup** in the USA, Canada and Mexico, the Nati also reached the quarter-finals. The last time it had done that at a World Cup was in 1954.

The record goal scorer is **Alexander Frei** with 42 goals. **Granit Xhaka** is the player with the most international caps and was captain for a long time. Goalkeeper Yann Sommer saved decisive penalties at Euro 2021. Xherdan Shaqiri also thrilled fans with spectacular goals. The coach since 2021 has been **Murat Yakin**.

The Nati reflects the diversity of Switzerland. Its players come from all parts of the country and speak German, French or Italian. Many have roots in other countries, for example in Kosovo, Albania or Africa. At big tournaments, hundreds of thousands watch at **public viewings**. Then the whole of Switzerland is on the edge of its seat together.

begriffe.erklaerung: Short for national team.
Taking penalties to decide a drawn match.
Matches in which teams fight for a place at a tournament.
A match between two national teams.

gewusst: Switzerland is the only country where both FIFA and UEFA have their headquarters.
At the 2006 World Cup Switzerland went out without conceding a single goal, because it lost to Ukraine on penalties.
The 7:5 between Austria and Switzerland in 1954 is also called the Heat Battle of Lausanne.

teile.einleitung: Noè Ponti is a Swiss swimmer from Ticino. He is especially fast at butterfly. In 2024 he became world champion three times and even set world records.
wichtigste: Noè Ponti was born on 1 June 2001 in Locarno in the canton of Ticino.
His sport is swimming, and his speciality is butterfly.
In 2021 he won Olympic bronze in the 100 metres butterfly in Tokyo.
It was Switzerland’s first Olympic swimming medal since 1984.
At the 2024 Short Course World Championships in Budapest he became world champion three times.
He holds short course world records over 50 and 100 metres butterfly (as of 2024).

abschnitte.text: Noè Ponti is a swimmer from **Locarno** on Lake Maggiore. He was born on 1 June 2001 and, as someone from Ticino, speaks Italian as his mother tongue. At six he joined the swimming club Nuoto Sport Locarno. Later he went to a secondary school in Locarno with a special class for athletes.

Ponti is strongest at **butterfly**, a stroke called “Delfin” (dolphin) in German. In it both arms swing forward over the water at the same time. The legs move together like a dolphin’s tail fin. The stroke is very powerful, but also especially tiring.

At the Olympic Games in **Tokyo**, which because of the Covid pandemic only took place in 2021, Ponti won bronze in the 100 metres butterfly. For Switzerland it was the first Olympic medal in swimming since 1984. Back then Étienne Dagon had won bronze in Los Angeles. In Paris in 2024 Ponti came fourth in the 100 metres butterfly and only just missed a medal.

In December 2024 Ponti had his greatest success at the **Short Course World Championships** in Budapest. He became world champion in the 50 metres butterfly, the 100 metres butterfly and the 100 metres individual medley. In the 50 metres butterfly he swam a **world record** of 21.32 seconds. In the 100 metres butterfly, too, he set a world record of 47.71 seconds.

Switzerland is not a big swimming nation, so Ponti’s successes are something special. He is considered one of the best swimmers Switzerland has ever had. Many children in Ticino and all over Switzerland see him as a role model. His successes show that you can reach the top of the world even from a small country.

begriffe.erklaerung: A swimming pool 25 metres long. Long course competitions take place in 50-metre pools.
A swimming stroke in which both arms swing over the water at the same time. In German it is also called Schmetterling.
A race in which you swim all four strokes one after another.
The fastest time anyone has ever swum in an event.

gewusst: Between October and December 2024 Ponti improved the short course world record over 50 metres butterfly several times.
A world-class swimmer like Ponti often trains twice a day and covers many kilometres in the water.

teile.einleitung: Corinne Suter is a Swiss ski racer from the canton of Schwyz. She is one of the best speed racers in the world and became Olympic downhill champion in Beijing in 2022. As early as 2020 she had won the World Cup rankings in downhill and super-G.
wichtigste: Corinne Suter was born in Schwyz in 1994.
Her strengths are the fast disciplines, downhill and super-G.
In 2020 she won the discipline rankings in downhill and super-G.
In 2021 she became downhill world champion in Cortina d’Ampezzo.
In 2022 she became Olympic downhill champion in Beijing.
Even as a junior she won several world titles.
Like many ski stars, she has also struggled with injuries.

abschnitte.text: **Corinne Suter** was born on 28 September 1994 in **Schwyz**. She grew up in a family that loved skiing. Early on she stood out for her talent in the fast disciplines. At the **Junior World Championships** in 2014 she won gold in downhill and super-G. After that she made the jump to the World Cup.

Her breakthrough came in the 2019/20 season. Corinne Suter won the **downhill** ranking and the **super-G** ranking. For this she received two small **crystal globes**. That was a magnificent success for a Swiss woman. It made her the best speed racer of that winter.

At the 2019 World Championships in Åre, Suter had already won silver and bronze. In 2021 in **Cortina d’Ampezzo** she became **world champion** in the downhill and won silver in the super-G. She celebrated her greatest success in February 2022 in **Beijing**. There she won Olympic gold in the downhill, just ahead of the Italian Sofia Goggia. With that she had won all the important titles.

Downhill and super-G are the fastest disciplines in skiing. The racers reach speeds of over 120 kilometres per hour. This takes a lot of **courage**, strength and good technique. Suter is known for her calm and powerful style. After tearing a cruciate ligament she had to fight her way back to the top.

Corinne Suter belongs to the successful Swiss women’s team at **Swiss-Ski**. With Lara Gut-Behrami, Michelle Gisin and Wendy Holdener she forms a strong generation. Together they have won many medals at Olympic Games and World Championships. In the canton of Schwyz, Suter is a big star.

begriffe.erklaerung: The fast ski races, downhill and super-G.
The trophy for winning a World Cup ranking.
An important ligament in the knee that is often injured in skiing falls.
World championships for young athletes.

gewusst: Corinne Suter won her Olympic gold medal by a margin of only 16 hundredths of a second.
At a single Junior World Championships she won two gold medals.
By the finish of a downhill, the racers have often covered a distance of over two kilometres.

teile.einleitung: Nina Christen is a Swiss sport shooter from the canton of Nidwalden. She shoots with a rifle and became Olympic champion in the three positions event in Tokyo in 2021. In this event you shoot kneeling, lying down and standing.
wichtigste: Nina Christen comes from Wolfenschiessen in the canton of Nidwalden.
Her sport is rifle shooting.
In the three positions event you shoot kneeling, lying down and standing.
In 2021 in Tokyo she became Olympic champion in the 50 metres three positions event.
At the same Games she won bronze with the air rifle.
Sport shooting takes a lot of calm, concentration and body control.
Shooting has a long tradition in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Nina Christen was born in 1994 and grew up in **Wolfenschiessen** in Nidwalden. She started shooting as a teenager at the local shooting club. People soon noticed that she could aim especially calmly and accurately. She was soon in the Swiss national squad.

In **sport shooting** you aim at a target with a rifle or a pistol. The closer the hit is to the centre, the more points you get. The centre of the target is tiny; for the air rifle it is only about half a millimetre across. A steady hand, good **breathing** and great concentration are important.

In the **three positions event** you shoot from three positions: kneeling, lying down and standing. The distance to the target is 50 metres, and you shoot with a small-bore rifle. Lying down is the easiest, standing the hardest. So you have to be very good in all three positions.

At the Olympic Games in **Tokyo** in 2021, Christen first won bronze with the **air rifle** over 10 metres. A few days later she became Olympic champion in the three positions event over 50 metres. It was a great success for Swiss shooting. Later she spoke openly about how exhausting the time after her Olympic victory was for her.

There are a great many **shooting clubs** in Switzerland. Every year the Feldschiessen takes place, the biggest shooting festival in the world. In Zurich there is the Knabenschiessen, a youth shooting contest in which girls may also take part. Sport shooting is strictly regulated and takes place only at secure shooting ranges.

begriffe.erklaerung: A shooting competition in the kneeling, lying and standing positions.
A rifle that uses compressed air to fire small lead pellets.
A rifle with small, light cartridges for sport shooting.
A club in which people practise shooting as a sport.

gewusst: The centre of the air rifle target is smaller than a pinhead.
The Federal Feldschiessen is considered the biggest shooting festival in the world.

teile.einleitung: Pirmin Zurbriggen is one of the most successful ski racers Switzerland has ever had. The skier from Valais was strong in every discipline, from slalom to downhill. In 1988 he became Olympic downhill champion in Calgary.
wichtigste: Pirmin Zurbriggen was born on 4 February 1963 in Saas-Almagell in the canton of Valais.
In 1988 he won Olympic gold in the downhill in Calgary.
That same year in Calgary he also won bronze in the giant slalom.
He won the overall World Cup four times.
He celebrated 40 World Cup victories in all five disciplines.
In 1990 he ended his career at only 27.

abschnitte.text: Pirmin Zurbriggen comes from **Saas-Almagell**, a mountain village in the Saas valley in the canton of Valais. He learnt to ski there as a small child. He was a so-called **all-rounder**, good at every discipline. In the 1980s he was one of the best ski racers in the world.

At the 1988 Winter Olympics in **Calgary** in Canada, Zurbriggen won the downhill. His Swiss teammate Peter Müller came second. Zurbriggen also won bronze in the giant slalom. With that he fulfilled his dream of Olympic gold.

Zurbriggen won the **overall World Cup** four times, in 1984, 1987, 1988 and 1990. Altogether he celebrated 40 World Cup victories. He became world champion several times at World Championships, for example in the downhill in Bormio in 1985, and in the giant slalom and super-G in Crans-Montana in 1987. He won races in downhill, super-G, giant slalom, slalom and combined.

At the beginning of 1985 Zurbriggen had to have an operation on his **knee**. Many thought he would not be able to take part in the World Championships in Bormio. But only a few weeks later he became downhill world champion there. This story made him even more popular with many fans.

After retiring in 1990, Zurbriggen stayed in Valais. With his family he runs **hotels** in Saas-Almagell and Zermatt. His sister Heidi Zurbriggen was also a successful ski racer. To this day Pirmin is seen as one of the greatest Swiss sportsmen.

begriffe.erklaerung: The fastest ski discipline, with long courses and jumps.
A ranking over a whole season with all the disciplines. Whoever collects the most points wins the big crystal globe.
An athlete who is good at many different disciplines.
A fast discipline that lies between the downhill and the giant slalom.

gewusst: Pirmin Zurbriggen won World Cup races in all five disciplines, something only very few manage.
In the 1988 Olympic downhill, two Swiss racers, Zurbriggen and Peter Müller, finished right at the front.

teile.einleitung: Volunteering is work that people do unpaid for others or for the community. In Switzerland many people volunteer, in clubs, in their neighbourhood or in public offices.
wichtigste: An unpaid post, for example on a club committee, is called an **honorary position**.
In the **militia system**, citizens hold public offices alongside their jobs.
The **Sozialzeitausweis** (volunteering certificate) confirms voluntary work.
Jubla and the Scouts are largely run by young volunteers.
International Volunteer Day is on 5 December.
Helping your neighbours also counts as informal volunteering.

abschnitte.text: There are two kinds of volunteering. **Formal volunteering** takes place in organisations, for example in sports clubs, churches or charities. **Informal volunteering** happens outside clubs, for example when you help your neighbour with her shopping. An unpaid post, for example on a club's committee, is called an **honorary position**. People in honorary positions receive no wages, at most a small allowance.

In Switzerland many municipal councillors, firefighters and members of parliament work **part-time alongside their jobs**. This system is called the **militia system**. It depends on citizens taking on public tasks as well as their jobs. As a result, those in charge know people's everyday lives well. At the same time, some municipalities today find it hard to find enough people for their offices.

In the **Scouts**, older teenagers lead the groups of younger ones as volunteers. Their sign is the neckerchief. The Scout movement was founded by the Briton **Robert Baden-Powell**. In **Jubla**, the association of Jungwacht and Blauring, young adults lead group sessions and camps for children. Jubla has a church background. In both organisations, young leaders learn to take responsibility.

Many organisations could not exist without volunteers. **Tischlein deck dich** saves surplus food from being thrown away. Volunteers hand it out to people affected by poverty in Switzerland. Volunteers also lend a hand with visiting services, lunch clubs and homework help. This creates support that the state could not provide on its own.

With the **Sozialzeitausweis**, volunteers can have their work, tasks and hours officially confirmed. This helps, for example, with job applications, because the commitment becomes visible. In 1985 the UN declared **5 December** International Volunteer Day. On this day people all over the world thank everyone who works for others without pay.

gewusst: The word ‘militia’ comes from the Latin ‘militia’, military service, and originally meant citizens who did military service alongside their jobs.
Many Swiss municipalities are run by a part-time municipal council.

teile.einleitung: ‘A Theory of Justice’ is the main work of the American philosopher John Rawls. The book appeared in 1971 and asks according to which principles a just society should be built.
wichtigste: John Rawls published ‘A Theory of Justice’ in 1971.
He sums up his theory as ‘justice as fairness’.
In the **original position**, free and equal people choose the principles of justice.
Behind the **veil of ignorance** nobody knows their future position.
Equal basic liberties for all have priority.
The difference principle only allows inequality if it benefits the least well-off most.
In 1974 Robert Nozick criticised Rawls from a libertarian point of view.

abschnitte.text: **John Rawls** lived from 1921 to 2002 and taught at Harvard University. His book **‘A Theory of Justice’** appeared in 1971 and greatly revived political philosophy. In German it is called ‘Eine Theorie der Gerechtigkeit’. Rawls sums up his theory with the slogan **‘justice as fairness’**. He deliberately sets it against **utilitarianism**, which only looks at the greatest total benefit.

Rawls carries out a thought experiment. In the **original position**, people are to choose the rules of their society. They are free, equal and rational. But they are behind a **veil of ignorance**: nobody knows their background, talents, wealth or future position. So nobody chooses rules that favour only themselves. The principles are fair because they are chosen under fair conditions.

The **first principle** guarantees everyone an equal system of **basic liberties**, such as freedom of opinion and freedom of conscience. This principle has **priority** over all others. Basic liberties must not be restricted just to gain economic advantages. The second principle also demands **fair equality of opportunity** in access to offices and positions.

According to the **difference principle**, inequalities in income and wealth are only allowed if they benefit the **least advantaged** the most. So a doctor may earn more if this benefits everyone, including the poorest. Why choose this way? According to Rawls, in the original position people use the **maximin rule**: you choose the option whose worst outcome is the best. If you do not know where you will end up, you protect yourself against the worst fate.

Rawls's theory was widely discussed. **Robert Nozick**, a colleague at Harvard University, criticised it in 1974 in ‘Anarchy, State, and Utopia’ from a **libertarian** point of view. He defended a minimal state and saw redistribution through taxes as an intrusion into property rights. Others thought that Rawls demanded too little equality. To this day the book is a basic text of political philosophy.

gewusst: As a young soldier, John Rawls served in the Pacific in the Second World War.
‘A Theory of Justice’ has been translated into many languages.

teile.einleitung: Utilitarianism is a school of thought in ethics. It asks: which action brings the most happiness and the least suffering overall? This idea still shapes many discussions about politics, the economy and animal welfare today.
wichtigste: The Englishman Jeremy Bentham (1748 to 1832) is regarded as the founder of classical utilitarianism.
The aim is: the greatest happiness of the greatest number.
Utilitarianism judges actions by their consequences and therefore belongs to consequentialism.
John Stuart Mill distinguished higher, intellectual pleasures from lower, bodily ones.
Rule utilitarianism judges rules, act utilitarianism individual actions.
Peter Singer demands that the interests of all beings capable of suffering be considered equally.
Critics warn that the rights of individuals could be sacrificed to the overall benefit.

abschnitte.text: The word comes from the Latin ‘utilitas’, which means usefulness. According to utilitarianism, the right action is the one that produces the most **well-being** overall. The happiness of each person affected counts equally, whether rich or poor. The famous formula is: **the greatest happiness of the greatest number**. So you do not look at the intention but at what comes out in the end. That is why utilitarianism belongs to **consequentialism**, the ethics of consequences.

The English philosopher **Jeremy Bentham** made the principle of utility the basis of morality and law-making. His main work appeared in 1789. Bentham wanted to make pleasure and pain measurable. With the **hedonic calculus** you were supposed to weigh up pleasure and pain according to criteria such as intensity, duration, certainty and nearness. In this way he wanted to solve the question of the best action almost like a maths problem.

abschnitte.titel: John Stuart Mill and the quality of pleasure
abschnitte.text: In the 19th century **John Stuart Mill** developed Bentham's ideas further. For him it mattered not only how much pleasure is produced, but also what kind of pleasure. He distinguished **higher**, intellectual pleasures, such as reading or learning, from **lower**, bodily pleasures. He is the source of the sentence: ‘It is better to be a dissatisfied human being than a satisfied pig.’

There are different forms of utilitarianism. **Act utilitarianism** examines each individual action on its own. **Rule utilitarianism**, on the other hand, asks which generally followed rule would have the best consequences. This can be used, for example, to justify the rule ‘keep your promises’, even if breaking one would be useful in a particular case. Because if nobody keeps promises any more, everyone loses trust.

Bentham thought that with animals what matters is not whether they can think or speak, but whether they can **suffer**. The Australian **Peter Singer** holds a form of preference utilitarianism and in 1975 wrote the book ‘Animal Liberation’. He criticises favouring one's own species as **speciesism**. A common objection to utilitarianism is that it could sacrifice the rights of individuals if many people benefit. Critics see this as a problem for justice and human dignity.

gewusst: Jeremy Bentham had his body preserved after his death. His clothed skeleton with a wax head still sits in a cabinet at University College London today.
When experts in politics compare the costs and benefits of a measure, there is often a utilitarian idea behind it.

teile.einleitung: Respect means valuing other people, animals, nature and other people's things. Respectful people are considerate and treat others kindly. Respect is important for living well together.
wichtigste: If you let others finish speaking, you show respect.
In Switzerland people often greet each other with ‘Grüezi’.
You treat other people's things carefully.
Taking your rubbish home shows respect for nature.
If someone does not want to be hugged, you respect that.
On the bus you offer your seat to older people.
A swear word is an insulting word.

abschnitte.text: You show respect in conversation: you let others **finish speaking** and you listen. You greet each other in a friendly way, in German-speaking Switzerland often with **‘Grüezi’**. On the **bus** you offer your seat to older people. **Swear words** are insulting words and hurt others. Respectful people do without them, even when they are angry.

Every person may decide for themselves who is allowed to touch them. If a child does **not want to be hugged**, then you do not hug them. This also applies among friends and in the family. A ‘no’ must be taken seriously. That shows respect for the other person's wishes.

You treat other people's things **carefully**. You give back a borrowed book in good condition, and you only use someone else's bicycle if you have asked. This also includes school materials and public things such as playgrounds or benches. If you break something, you say so honestly. That way things stay usable for everyone.

**Nature** deserves respect too. You **take** your **rubbish home** instead of leaving it lying around, and you do not pick protected plants. You leave **animals** in peace, especially wild animals in the forest. You do not chase them and do not simply feed them. That way their habitats stay protected.

Switzerland has four national languages. As well as **‘Grüezi’** you hear **‘Bonjour’** in French, **‘Buongiorno’** in Italian and **‘Allegra’** in Romansh. Respect also means valuing other languages, customs and opinions. The word respect comes from the Latin respectus, which means roughly ‘consideration’.

gewusst: In Switzerland many people say ‘Grüezi’ even to strangers when they are out hiking.
In Romansh, ‘Allegra’ originally means ‘be glad’.

teile.einleitung: Friendship is a special bond between people who like each other and trust each other. Good friends stick together, listen and have fun together.
wichtigste: Good friends stick together, even when things are difficult.
If you listen and ask questions, you show that the other person matters to you.
You can have lots of friends.
You keep harmless secrets to yourself.
If a secret means that someone is being hurt, you get help.
A compliment is something nice you say about someone.

abschnitte.text: Good friends **stick together**. They support each other, even when things are difficult. They spend **time together**, playing, talking and laughing. That makes the friendship stronger. You can be friends with more than one child. Every friendship is something special.

When a friend is sad, you can **ask what is wrong**. Often it helps just to **listen**. If a friend has made a mistake in a drawing, you can say: ‘That can happen to anyone.’ Encouraging words are comforting. A **compliment** is a friendly remark, for example ‘You've drawn that beautifully’. It makes others happy.

A new child in the class often does not know anyone yet and feels unsure. It is friendly to **invite the child to play**. That makes it easier for them to fit in. Many friendships begin with a small invitation or a smile. If you are open towards others, you often find new friends yourself.

If a friend tells you a secret that does not harm anyone, you keep it **to yourself**. That shows that people can **trust** you. But there are secrets where someone is afraid or is being hurt. You may and should tell such secrets to an **adult you trust**, for example your parents or a teacher. That is not betrayal but help.

On the internet and in the class chat there are also rules for treating each other well. They are called **netiquette**. The word is made up of ‘net’ and ‘etiquette’. This includes staying friendly and **not showing others up**. What you would not say to someone's face, you do not write in the chat either.

gewusst: The UN's International Day of Friendship is on 30 July.
Friendships also exist between people of different ages, for example between children and grandparents.

teile.einleitung: Business ethics asks how companies, consumers and states can act responsibly in the economy. Is it only about profit, or also about people and the environment? People have argued about this for centuries, in Switzerland too.
wichtigste: In 1970 Milton Friedman wrote that the responsibility of a company is to increase its profits.
The stakeholder approach demands that the interests of all groups affected be taken into account.
In 1759 Adam Smith wrote “The Theory of Moral Sentiments”.
