The Responsible Business Initiative failed in 2020 because it did not win a majority of the cantons.
The first Fairtrade label, “Max Havelaar”, was created in the Netherlands in 1988.
Peter Ulrich developed integrative business ethics at the University of St Gallen.
Greenwashing means presenting yourself as more environmentally friendly than you are.

abschnitte.text: In 1970 the economist **Milton Friedman** wrote in the “New York Times” that the social responsibility of a company is to increase its **profits**. Managers, he said, owe a duty to the owners as long as they keep to the rules of the game. The opposite view is the **stakeholder approach**, which R. Edward Freeman made well known in 1984. According to it, companies should take into account the interests of all **stakeholders**: staff, customers, suppliers, neighbours and the environment. Both views are still debated today.

The Scot **Adam Smith** is considered the father of economics. His best-known work is “The Wealth of Nations” of 1776. But as early as 1759 he published **“The Theory of Moral Sentiments”**. In it he explains morality through **sympathy** and the view of an “impartial spectator”. So Smith saw himself as a moral philosopher and not only as an economist.

At the **University of St Gallen**, **Peter Ulrich** became the first professor of business ethics in the German-speaking world in 1987. His **integrative business ethics** asks what kind of good life the economy should serve. On 29 November 2020 Switzerland voted on the **Responsible Business Initiative**. It won around 50.7 per cent of the votes but failed because it did not win the **majority of the cantons**: most cantons said no. Instead the indirect counter-proposal, with reporting obligations, came into force.

abschnitte.titel: Fair trade and the Global Compact
abschnitte.text: The first Fairtrade label, **“Max Havelaar”**, was created in 1988 in the **Netherlands**. It is named after the main character of a novel that criticises exploitation on coffee plantations. The Swiss Max Havelaar Foundation followed in 1992. The **UN Global Compact** of 2000 invites companies to keep to ten principles on human rights, labour, the environment and fighting corruption. UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan presented the idea at the World Economic Forum in **Davos** in 1999. Taking part is voluntary.

Some companies present themselves in their advertising as more **environmentally friendly** than they really are. This is called **greenwashing**. The word is made up of “green” and “whitewashing”, which means covering up faults. Greenwashing deceives consumers and undermines real sustainability. So when you shop, you can look out for checked labels and question advertising promises critically.

gewusst: In Switzerland a popular initiative can fail despite a majority of the votes if the majority of the cantons does not agree as well.
Adam Smith revised his “Theory of Moral Sentiments” several times. The last version appeared in 1790, the year he died.

teile.einleitung: Environmental ethics asks what responsibility humans have towards nature. Do only humans have moral value, or do animals, plants and whole ecosystems have it too? There are different positions and important principles on this.
wichtigste: According to anthropocentrism, only humans have intrinsic moral value.
Pathocentrism grants intrinsic value to all living things that can suffer.
Albert Schweitzer coined the phrase ‘reverence for life’.
In 1949 Aldo Leopold formulated the ‘land ethic’.
In 1973 Arne Naess coined the term ‘deep ecology’.
In 1713 Hans Carl von Carlowitz applied the idea of sustainability to forests.
The polluter pays principle and the precautionary principle are important principles of environmental protection.

abschnitte.text: Environmental ethics distinguishes several positions. According to **anthropocentrism**, only **humans** have intrinsic moral value, and nature matters because it is useful to people. **Pathocentrism** grants intrinsic value to all living things that are **able to suffer**. **Biocentrism** includes all living things, including plants. Finally, **holism** takes whole ecosystems into account.

The doctor and theologian **Albert Schweitzer** coined the phrase **‘reverence for life’**. For him all life deserves respect, not only human life. This attitude is seen as the basis of a **biocentric** ethics. Schweitzer founded a hospital in Lambaréné in what is now Gabon and received the Nobel Peace Prize. His ideas influenced many later environmentalists.

In his book **‘A Sand County Almanac’** (1949), the American **Aldo Leopold** formulated the **‘land ethic’**. According to it, people should respect soils, waters, plants and animals as a community to which they themselves belong. In **1973** the Norwegian philosopher **Arne Naess** coined the term **deep ecology**. He demanded that nature be protected not only for the benefit of people but for its own sake.

The idea of **sustainability** originally comes from **forestry**. In **1713** the Saxon official **Hans Carl von Carlowitz** wrote that you should only cut as much wood as can grow back. Today sustainability means living in such a way that future generations will also have good living conditions. In Switzerland the Federal Constitution requires the federal government and the cantons to promote sustainable development. The Swiss Forest Act has long protected the area of forest.

According to the **polluter pays principle**, those who cause environmental pollution bear its costs. The **precautionary principle** demands that possible environmental damage be prevented even when there is still scientific **uncertainty**. So you do not wait until damage has definitely been proven. Both principles are laid down in the Swiss **Environmental Protection Act**. They also apply in many other countries and in international environmental law.

gewusst: The word ‘sustainable’ (in German ‘nachhaltig’) was first used for forests more than 300 years ago and is now on everyone's lips.
In 1979, in ‘The Imperative of Responsibility’, the philosopher Hans Jonas called for people to think about the consequences of their actions for future generations too.

teile.einleitung: Marcel Hug is a Swiss wheelchair athlete from Thurgau and one of the fastest wheelchair racers in the world. Because of his silver helmet he is called the “Silver Bullet”. At the Paralympics in Tokyo he won gold four times.
wichtigste: Marcel Hug was born in 1986 in Pfyn in the canton of Thurgau.
He was born with a malformation of the spine, spina bifida.
He races in a racing wheelchair in the T54 class.
His nickname is the “Silver Bullet”.
In 2016 in Rio he won gold over 800 metres and in the marathon.
In 2021 in Tokyo he won gold four times.
He has won many big city marathons such as Boston, London and Berlin.

abschnitte.text: Marcel Hug was born on 16 January 1986 in **Pfyn** in the canton of Thurgau. He was born with **spina bifida**, an open spine. That is why he depends on a wheelchair. Even as a child he discovered how much he enjoyed fast races.

Hug races with an eye-catching **silver helmet**. That is where his nickname “Silver Bullet” comes from; in German it would be “silberne Kugel”. He lives and trains in **Nottwil** in the canton of Lucerne. There is a racing track there and the Swiss Paraplegic Centre.

Hug won his first medals in Athens in 2004, two bronzes. In London in 2012 came silver over 800 metres and in the marathon. In Rio in 2016 he became Paralympic champion over 800 metres and in the marathon. In 2021 in **Tokyo** he won gold over 800, 1500 and 5000 metres and in the marathon.

Hug is also very strong on the road. He has won the big **marathons** in Boston, London, Berlin, Chicago and New York. In 2016 he won in all these cities and so took the overall ranking of the marathon series. In Boston he has won more often than almost anyone else.

A **racing wheelchair** weighs only a few kilograms and has three wheels. Hug worked with engineers to develop a particularly fast racing wheelchair. He trains every day, often on long roads around Lake Sempach. He is a great role model for many people with disabilities.

begriffe.erklaerung: A malformation of the spine present from birth, often also called open spine.
The Olympic Games for people with disabilities.
A light, fast wheelchair with three wheels for competitions.
An extra name that friends or fans give someone.

gewusst: In Tokyo Marcel Hug won gold over four very different distances, from 800 metres to the marathon.
Going downhill in his racing wheelchair, Marcel Hug reaches speeds like a car in town.

teile.einleitung: Giulia Steingruber is a former Swiss artistic gymnast from eastern Switzerland. In 2016 in Rio de Janeiro she became the first Swiss woman to win an Olympic medal in artistic gymnastics. Her speciality was the vault.
wichtigste: Giulia Steingruber was born in St Gallen in 1994.
She did gymnastics for the gymnastics club in Gossau.
Her sport was artistic gymnastics.
In 2016 she won bronze on the vault at the Olympic Games in Rio.
She became European champion six times.
In 2017 she won bronze on the vault at the World Championships.
She ended her career in 2021.

abschnitte.text: Giulia Steingruber was born in **St Gallen** on 24 March 1994. She grew up in Gossau and did gymnastics at the Gossau gymnastics club. Even as a child she showed great strength and courage. She was soon in the national squad of the Swiss Gymnastics Federation.

In **artistic gymnastics** women perform routines on four pieces of apparatus: vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor. Judges score the difficulty and how cleanly it is performed. In the **all-around**, all four apparatus count together. Steingruber was good on all of them, but strongest on the vault.

At the 2016 Olympic Games in **Rio de Janeiro**, she carried the Swiss flag at the opening ceremony. Afterwards she won the bronze medal in the vault final. That made her the first Swiss woman ever to win an Olympic medal in artistic gymnastics. She was greatly celebrated for it in Switzerland.

Steingruber became **European champion** six times in total. On the vault she won in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2021. In 2015 in Montpellier she became European all-around champion. In 2016 in Bern, in front of a home crowd, she also won the title on the floor.

After the Olympic Games in Tokyo, she announced her retirement in October 2021. In her career she had also come through serious injuries that forced her to take long breaks. In 2017 Gossau made her an honorary citizen. She showed many girls in Switzerland that you can get right to the top in gymnastics.

begriffe.erklaerung: Gymnastics on apparatus such as bars, beam or vault, scored by judges.
A padded piece of apparatus that you leap over with a somersault after a run-up.
A competition in which the points from all the apparatus are added together.
A special award from a municipality for a person who has achieved a great deal.

gewusst: A vault lasts only a few seconds, but has to be practised for years.
She won some of her European titles in Switzerland, namely in Bern and Basel.

teile.einleitung: Hope is the expectation that something good will happen. It gives people the strength to keep going, even in hard times. It plays a big part in religion, legends, history and language.
wichtigste: Hope means trusting in something good that is still to come.
Green is traditionally the colour of hope.
In Christianity the anchor is a symbol of hope.
Paul names faith, love and hope together.
In the legend of Pandora, hope stayed behind in the box.
Martin Luther King's words ‘I have a dream’ became a symbol of hope in 1963.
Resilience is the ability to regain strength after a crisis.

abschnitte.text: The colour **green** is traditionally seen as the colour of hope, because it reminds people of plants growing in spring. In Christianity the **anchor** is a symbol of hope: just as an anchor holds a ship steady in a storm, hope is meant to give people something to hold on to. In a letter, the apostle **Paul** names **faith, love and hope** together. They are called the three theological virtues.

A Greek legend tells of **Pandora**. She opened a jar from which all evils escaped into the world, such as illness and hardship. Only **hope** stayed behind inside. The legend is interpreted in different ways: some see hope as a comfort that remains for people. Today we say ‘to open Pandora's box’ when something sets off lots of problems.

The **Cape of Good Hope** is at the southern tip of Africa. The Portuguese seafarer Bartolomeu Dias sailed round it in 1488. The name expressed the hope of finding the sea route to India this way. In 1963 **Martin Luther King** gave a famous speech in Washington against the unfair treatment of Black people. His words **‘I have a dream’** became a symbol of the hope for equal rights.

Anyone who expects good things has an attitude of **optimism**. Hope can help you get through difficulties. The ability to regain strength after a crisis is called **resilience**. It comes from the Latin word for ‘to spring back’. Resilience can be strengthened, for example through good friendships and through people you trust.

The German saying **‘Die Hoffnung stirbt zuletzt’** (hope dies last) means that you should not give up too quickly. But hope is not the same as simply wishing: often it also means doing something yourself. The German philosopher **Ernst Bloch** wrote a large work called ‘The Principle of Hope’. In it he describes how people keep dreaming of a better future.

gewusst: Bartolomeu Dias is said to have first called the cape the ‘Cape of Storms’; only later did it get its hopeful name.
In the original Greek legend, Pandora's ‘box’ was actually a large storage jar, not a small box.

teile.einleitung: Sharing means letting others have part of something you have. You can share things, but also time and fun. If you share, you make others happy and show that they matter to you.
wichtigste: If you have three apples and your friend has none, you can give one away.
8 jelly bears shared fairly between two makes 4 each.
If two children want the same swing, they can take turns.
You can also share time and fun.
You must not simply take other people's things; you ask first.
You give back a borrowed book carefully.

abschnitte.text: If you have three apples and your friend has none, it is kind to **give away one apple**. Sharing shows that others matter to you. Often sharing makes you happy too. You can share not only food or toys but also **time and fun**. When you play or laugh together, you are sharing something valuable.

When you share fairly, each person gets the same amount. If you share **8 jelly bears** with a friend, each of you gets **4**. If you cut a pizza into **4** equal slices for **4** children, each child gets **1** slice. In maths this is called **division**. You write it, for example, as 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

Some things cannot be divided, for example a **swing**. If two children want to swing at the same time, **taking turns** is a good solution. You can agree how long each child may have. That way everyone gets a turn and there is no quarrel. You can also take turns with a toy or a computer game.

You must not simply take something that belongs to someone else in order to share it. First you **ask** the owner. A polite way to ask is, for example: ‘May I have it, please?’ You look after a **borrowed book** and **give it back carefully**. Then others will be happy to lend you something again.

gewusst: A well-known legend tells how Saint Martin cut his cloak in two with his sword to help a beggar who was freezing.
In many Swiss municipalities St Martin's Day is celebrated on 11 November, for example with lantern processions.

teile.einleitung: Bullying, called ‘Mobbing’ in German, means that someone is deliberately excluded, insulted or tormented over a long period. It can happen at school, at work or on the internet. It is important not to look away and to get help.
wichtigste: Bullying is repeated, targeted harassment of a person.
A single quarrel is not yet bullying.
Bullying by mobile phone and internet is called cyberbullying.
The German word ‘Mobbing’ comes from English.
Bystanders play an important part and can help.
From the 1970s Dan Olweus made bullying in schools widely known.
Getting help is not telling tales, for example at the number 147.

abschnitte.text: We speak of **bullying** when someone is harassed **repeatedly** and **deliberately** over a long period. This can mean laughing at them, insulting them, leaving them out or spreading rumours. A single quarrel is not yet bullying. Typically, the person affected can hardly defend themselves alone. The German word ‘Mobbing’ comes from the English ‘to mob’, which means roughly to crowd round and harass someone. In English, bullying among children is usually simply called ‘bullying’.

When bullying happens via mobile phone and internet, it is called **cyberbullying**. People are shown up, for example, in chats, with photos or comments. This can go on round the clock and reach many people. Those affected should save **screenshots** as evidence and show them to parents or teachers. Then you can block and report the person.

With bullying there are often children who watch but do not step in. They are called **bystanders**. They are important: if they take the side of the person affected, bullying often loses its power. You can stand by the child affected, talk to them or tell an adult. **Getting help is not telling tales**. Children and teenagers can also call the number **147**.

From the 1970s the psychologist **Dan Olweus** studied violence among schoolchildren in **Norway** and **Sweden**. He developed a well-known programme against bullying in schools. Bullying also exists among adults at work. If it comes from a boss, it is called **bossing** in German, from the English word boss.

In the **No Blame Approach** nobody is blamed. The teacher forms a support group, which also includes those involved, and together they look for a solution. The aim is for the bullying to stop without punishing anyone. In **peer mediation**, pupils are trained to settle quarrels among people of their own age. ‘Peers’ are people of the same age.

gewusst: The behavioural scientist Konrad Lorenz used the word ‘mobbing’ for animals that band together in a group against an enemy.
Bullying often stops more quickly when several children say together that they do not think it is all right.

teile.einleitung: Roman Josi is an ice hockey player from Bern who plays in the NHL, the best ice hockey league in the world. He is a defenceman and captain of the Nashville Predators. In 2020 he received the Norris Trophy as the best defenceman in the league.
wichtigste: Roman Josi was born in Bern on 1 June 1990.
He began his career at SC Bern.
Since 2011 he has played for the Nashville Predators in the NHL.
He is a defenceman and has been captain of his team since 2017.
In 2020 he won the Norris Trophy as the best defenceman in the NHL.
With Switzerland he won World Championship silver in 2013 and was voted most valuable player of the tournament.

abschnitte.text: Roman Josi comes from **Bern** and learnt to play ice hockey there. With SC Bern he became Swiss champion in 2010. In 2008 the Nashville Predators picked him in the **Draft**. Since 2011 he has played in North America.

The NHL is the best **ice hockey league** in the world, with teams from the USA and Canada. Josi plays for the Nashville Predators in the state of Tennessee. In 2017 he reached the Stanley Cup Final with Nashville but lost it to Pittsburgh. Since 2017 he has been the team captain.

As a **defenceman**, Josi’s main job is to stop the other team scoring. But he is also known for setting up many goals and scoring them himself. He is a very good skater and often carries the puck forward. In some seasons he collected more points than many forwards.

In 2020 Josi received the **Norris Trophy**. This award goes each year to the best defenceman in the NHL. He was the first Swiss player to win this prize. In other years too he was among the candidates for this trophy.

With the Swiss **national team**, Josi won the silver medal at the 2013 World Championship in Stockholm. There he was voted the most valuable player of the whole tournament. In 2024 in Prague, too, he won World Championship silver with Switzerland. He is a great role model for many young hockey players in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: National Hockey League, the best ice hockey league in the world, in North America.
A player whose main job is to protect his own goal.
The leader of a team. He wears a “C” on his shirt.
A selection process in which NHL teams pick young players.

gewusst: Roman Josi was the first Swiss player to win the Norris Trophy as the best defenceman in the NHL.
Nashville, where Josi plays, is actually best known as the city of country music.

teile.einleitung: Quarrels are part of life, because people do not always want the same thing. What matters is how a conflict is resolved. By talking, listening and finding fair solutions, a quarrel can end well.
wichtigste: In a quarrel, talking to each other helps most.
While the other person is explaining, you listen carefully.
An I-message says how you feel yourself, without blaming.
In a compromise both sides give way a little.
Hitting is never a good solution.
A short break helps you calm down.
A mediator or a teacher can help find a solution.

abschnitte.text: The most important thing in a quarrel is to **talk to each other**. Each side explains what is bothering them and what they would like. While the other person is speaking, you **listen** and do not interrupt. That way you understand better why the other person is angry or sad. Often you realise that it was only a misunderstanding.

An **I-message** says how you feel yourself. It begins, for example, with ‘I feel …’ or ‘I am sad when …’. A you-message such as ‘You're mean!’, on the other hand, sounds like an accusation. The other person feels attacked and defends themselves. With I-messages the conversation stays calmer and fairer.

When you are very angry, a **short break** helps. You breathe deeply, walk a few steps or count slowly to ten. That way you **calm down** and can think more clearly afterwards. **Hitting**, kicking or calling names is never a good idea. Violence only makes a quarrel worse and hurts others.

Often there is a solution that both are happy with. If two children want to read the same book, they can **read it together** or take turns. When both give way a little, this is called a **compromise**. Sometimes you can even find a solution in which both win. What matters is that nobody feels unfairly treated in the end.

Not every quarrel can be solved alone. Then a **teacher** or another adult can help. A person who helps people in a quarrel to reach an agreement is called a **mediator**. The technical term for this is **mediation**. Some Swiss schools have trained pupils who help with quarrels among children of their own age.

gewusst: The word ‘compromise’ comes from Latin and originally meant ‘a mutual promise’.
The idea of the I-message was made known by the American psychologist Thomas Gordon.

teile.einleitung: Iouri Podladtchikov is a Swiss snowboarder who was among the best in the world in the halfpipe. In 2014 he became Olympic champion in Sochi. He is also famous for a very difficult jump of his own.
wichtigste: Iouri Podladtchikov was born in Russia in 1988.
As a child he moved to Switzerland with his family.
His discipline is the halfpipe.
In 2013 he became halfpipe world champion.
In 2014 he won Olympic gold in Sochi.
His nickname is “I-Pod”.
He developed the trick known as the “YOLO Flip”.

abschnitte.text: Iouri Podladtchikov was born in 1988 in **Podolsk** near Moscow. As a child he moved west with his family and finally to **Switzerland**. Among other places he lived in Davos, where he was able to train a lot. At first he competed for Russia, later for Switzerland.

The **halfpipe** is a channel of snow shaped like half a tube. In competitions the walls are up to about seven metres high. The riders go from one wall to the other and jump high above the edge. In the air they perform spins and somersaults, which are scored by a panel of judges.

Podladtchikov was known for a jump with two somersaults and four full spins around his own axis. He called this trick the **YOLO Flip**, after the English saying “You only live once”. He was one of the first to perform such a jump in competition. In this way he moved the whole sport forward a step.

At the 2014 Winter Olympics in **Sochi**, Podladtchikov won the gold medal in the halfpipe. In doing so he beat Shaun White from the USA, who was the favourite at the time. He had already become world champion in 2013. For Switzerland it was a great success in snowboarding.

Podladtchikov is also interested in photography and art. He has struggled with injuries again and again, for example after a bad fall at the X Games in 2018. Because of this he could not take part in the 2018 Olympic Games. He is seen as a creative athlete who goes his own way.

begriffe.erklaerung: A half-round channel of snow in which snowboarders perform jumps.
A group of experts who score the jumps with points.
A jump with spins or somersaults in the air.
Someone who is expected to win.

gewusst: The name YOLO Flip comes from “You only live once”, in German “Man lebt nur einmal”.
Shaun White, whom Podladtchikov beat in 2014, had won the halfpipe at the two Games before that.

teile.einleitung: Responsibility means answering for what you do and its consequences. It begins with small things, in the family and at school, and goes as far as caring for nature and future generations. Swiss law also sets out who is responsible for what.
wichtigste: Anyone who takes responsibility stands by their actions and deals with the consequences.
In Switzerland juvenile criminal law applies from a person's 10th birthday.
In Switzerland you come of age at 18, and have done since 1996.
Anyone who does not help a person whose life is in danger, although it could reasonably be expected, commits an offence.
In 1979 Hans Jonas wrote the book ‘The Imperative of Responsibility’.
In diffusion of responsibility, nobody in a large group feels it is their job.

abschnitte.text: The German word ‘Verantwortung’ is linked to ‘antworten’, to answer: whoever is responsible must be able to answer the question of why they did something. Taking responsibility means **answering for the consequences**. This also includes admitting mistakes and putting them right where possible. You are responsible for yourself, for other people, for animals and for things you use.

If a school class borrows a piece of equipment, **everyone who uses it** is responsible for it. They handle it carefully and report any damage. Shared responsibility does not mean that nobody has to bother. But this is exactly where a trap lies: **diffusion of responsibility**. In large groups, everyone thinks someone else will act. That is why sometimes nobody helps, even though many people are watching.

In Switzerland the **Juvenile Criminal Law Act** applies to young people from their 10th birthday. Protection and education come first, not punishment. At 18 you come of **age**; before 1996 you only did so at 20. Adults may, for example, sign contracts themselves. Article 128 of the Criminal Code punishes **failure to offer help in an emergency**: anyone who does not help a person in immediate danger of death, although it could reasonably be expected, commits an offence. Often it is enough to call for help, for example on the emergency number 112.

In 1979 the philosopher **Hans Jonas** wrote the book ‘The Imperative of Responsibility’. He believed that modern technology has become so powerful that people are also responsible for **future generations** and nature. His book became important for environmental ethics. This includes using resources **sustainably**: using only so much that later generations can live well too. Saving energy and avoiding waste are simple examples.

gewusst: Until 1996 people in Switzerland only came of age at 20.
In psychology, diffusion of responsibility is also called the ‘bystander effect’.

teile.einleitung: Belinda Bencic is a Swiss tennis player from eastern Switzerland. In 2021 in Tokyo she became Olympic singles champion, the first Swiss woman ever to do so in tennis. In 2022 she won the Billie Jean King Cup with Switzerland.
wichtigste: Belinda Bencic was born in 1997 in Flawil in the canton of St Gallen.
As a child she was coached by Melanie Molitor, the mother of Martina Hingis.
In 2021 she won Olympic gold in the singles in Tokyo.
In the doubles in Tokyo she won silver together with Viktorija Golubic.
In 2022 she won the Billie Jean King Cup with Switzerland.
Her highest world ranking was number 4.
After her daughter was born in 2024, she made a successful return to the tour.

abschnitte.text: **Belinda Bencic** was born in Flawil on 10 March 1997. Her parents come from Slovakia. From the age of four she trained with **Melanie Molitor**, the mother and coach of Martina Hingis. As a junior she won the junior tournaments in Paris and at **Wimbledon** in 2013. After that she was number 1 in the junior world rankings.

At the Olympic Games in **Tokyo** in 2021, Bencic won the singles tournament. In the final she beat the Czech Markéta Vondroušová. That made her the first Swiss woman to win Olympic gold in **tennis singles**. Together with **Viktorija Golubic** she also won silver in the doubles. With two medals she was one of the most successful Swiss women at these Games.

Bencic has played for the Swiss team for many years. In 2022 in Glasgow she won the **Billie Jean King Cup** with Switzerland, the most important team competition in women’s tennis. In 2018 and 2019 she had already won the Hopman Cup with **Roger Federer**, a tournament for mixed teams. She enjoys playing for Switzerland and is seen as a team player.

Bencic is known for her fast and clever game; she takes the ball early. In 2019 she reached the **semi-final of the US Open**. In 2020 she was world number 4. She has won several WTA tournaments. She has been held back by injuries again and again, but has always come back.

In 2024 Belinda Bencic became the mother of a daughter. Just a few months later she returned to the **WTA Tour**. In February 2025 she was already winning a tournament again, in Abu Dhabi. In this way she showed that family and top-level sport can be combined. She is a role model for many young players.

begriffe.erklaerung: A tennis match in which one person plays against another.
The organisation that runs the women’s professional tournaments.
A list that shows how good players are compared with each other.
A tennis tournament in which countries compete with one woman and one man each.

gewusst: Belinda Bencic and Martina Hingis had the same coach, Melanie Molitor.
Bencic was the first Swiss woman to win Olympic gold in tennis singles.
At the Games in Tokyo, Bencic won two medals, gold and silver.

teile.einleitung: Everyone sometimes makes mistakes or hurts others, often without meaning to. With an apology you show that you are sorry and clear the way for making up.
wichtigste: You apologise even for an accident.
A good apology includes admitting the mistake.
A real apology has no ‘but’.
You can also make up for damage you have caused.
It is best to apologise as soon as possible.
Forgiving means letting go of your anger.

abschnitte.text: If you bump into someone by accident, you say: ‘Sorry!’ That way the other person knows it was **not on purpose**. An apology shows that the other person matters to you. It helps make sure that nobody stays angry or sad for long. It is best to apologise **as soon as possible**; then the anger passes more quickly.

In a good apology you say **what you did wrong**. For example: ‘I'm sorry I knocked over your tower.’ You look at the other person and mean it honestly. A bad apology would be: ‘Sorry, but it's your fault.’ Anyone who blames the other person in the same sentence is not really apologising. A real apology has **no ‘but’**.

You can also show an apology through actions. If you build a knocked-over tower back up, you **make amends** for the damage. If you have damaged a book, you can help to mend it. That shows you mean it. Words and actions together are often the best apology.

When someone apologises to you, you can say: ‘That's all right, thanks.’ Anyone who **accepts** an apology ends the quarrel. **Forgiving** means no longer holding the mistake against the other person and letting go of your anger. That does both of you good. Sometimes you need a little time for this, and that is fine.

When two people are friends again after a quarrel, this is called **making up** or reconciliation. It often begins with an apology. Afterwards you can play and laugh together again. Quarrels are part of life. What matters is learning how to end them again.

gewusst: The German word ‘Entschuldigung’ actually means freeing someone from their guilt.
In everyday life in Switzerland people also often say ‘Exgüsi’, which comes from the French ‘excusez’.

teile.einleitung: Jolanda Neff is a Swiss mountain biker from the canton of St Gallen. In 2021 in Tokyo she became Olympic champion in cross-country. Three Swiss women won all three medals between them.
wichtigste: Jolanda Neff was born in 1993 and comes from the canton of St Gallen.
Her sport is mountain biking, especially cross-country.
In 2017 she became cross-country world champion.
She won the overall World Cup several times.
In 2021 she became Olympic champion in Tokyo.
Sina Frei won silver and Linda Indergand bronze.
Neff also rides races on the road and long-distance races off-road.

abschnitte.text: Jolanda Neff was born on 5 January 1993 and grew up in **Thal** in the canton of St Gallen. Her family supported her cycling from an early age. Even as a junior she won important races. She was soon one of the strongest riders in the world.

In **cross-country** all the riders start at the same time. The course leads over steep climbs, roots, stones and fast descents. A race lasts about an hour and a half, and you ride several laps. You need a lot of stamina, but also skill on the **mountain bike**.

In 2017 in Cairns in Australia, Neff became cross-country **world champion**. She also won the **overall World Cup** several times, for example in 2014, 2015 and 2018. That meant she was the best over the whole season. In 2019 she had a bad fall in training, but fought her way back.

Because of the Covid pandemic, the Tokyo Olympic Games did not take place until 2021. In the race Jolanda Neff rode away from everyone and won **gold**. Behind her came Sina Frei in second place and Linda Indergand in third. It is very rare for one country to win all three medals.

Switzerland is one of the strongest countries in mountain biking. As well as Jolanda Neff, Nino Schurter was also among the best in the world for many years. World Cup races are held regularly in Lenzerheide. Many children ride in cycling clubs and learn to ride off-road there.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mountain bike race with a mass start over a hilly lap.
The ranking across all the World Cup races of a season together.
Everyone starts at the same time, and whoever finishes first wins.
The steps on which the top three stand.

gewusst: Before her first elite world title, Jolanda Neff had also become under-23 world champion.
At the medal ceremony in Tokyo, three Swiss women stood on the podium together.

teile.einleitung: Grief is the feeling people have when they lose someone or something important. It is completely natural and can look very different. There are many customs and kinds of help that support people when they are grieving.
wichtigste: Grief is a natural reaction to a loss.
The Zurich-born doctor Elisabeth Kübler-Ross described stages of dying.
The Swiss psychologist Verena Kast described four phases of grief.
In Europe mourners traditionally wear black.
Offering condolences means expressing your sympathy to those left behind.
A flag at half mast is a sign of mourning.
Hospices and palliative care support seriously ill people at the end of their lives.

abschnitte.text: **Grief** arises when you lose something or someone that was important to you. This can be a person, a pet or even a home when you move house. People who are grieving can be sad, angry, tired or confused. Sometimes the feelings change quickly. There is no right or wrong way to grieve, and it helps to talk about it with people you trust.

The doctor **Elisabeth Kübler-Ross** (1926 to 2004), who was born in **Zurich**, worked with dying people in the USA. She described five **stages of dying**, and her model is often applied to grief too. The Swiss psychologist **Verena Kast** described **four phases of grief**. At the beginning there is often a refusal to accept what has happened; later strong feelings break through. In the end a new relationship with yourself and the world can develop. But the phases do not happen in the same way for everyone.

In Europe mourners traditionally wear **black**, while in some Asian countries white is the colour of mourning. A narrow black band on the sleeve is called a **mourning band**; athletes sometimes wear one too. If a flag is raised only halfway up the pole, it is at **half mast**, a **sign of mourning**. This happens, for example, after the death of important people or after disasters.

When you express your sympathy to those left behind, you **offer your condolences**. The word comes from the Latin condolere, ‘to suffer with’. You can offer condolences in person, with a card or in a book of condolence. Often a simple sentence, or just being there, helps. People who are grieving sometimes need a long time, and patience is important.

abschnitte.titel: Support at the end of life
abschnitte.text: A **hospice** is a place where seriously ill people are cared for and supported at the end of their lives. Their relatives are supported there too. **Palliative care** is care that no longer aims to cure, but above all **relieves pain** and preserves quality of life. The term comes from the Latin pallium, cloak. Children and teenagers who are sad can also talk to the number **147**.

gewusst: Elisabeth Kübler-Ross wrote the famous book ‘On Death and Dying’, which was translated into many languages.
The word ‘palliative’ recalls a cloak that is wrapped protectively round a person.

teile.einleitung: Xherdan Shaqiri is a Swiss footballer who won the Champions League with Bayern Munich and Liverpool FC. He began and ended his career in Switzerland at FC Basel. For the Swiss national team he scored many important goals at big tournaments.
wichtigste: Xherdan Shaqiri was born in Gjilan in Kosovo on 10 October 1991.
As a baby he came with his family to Switzerland, to Augst in the canton of Basel-Landschaft.
His professional career began at FC Basel, and in 2024 he returned there.
He won the Champions League in 2013 with Bayern Munich and in 2019 with Liverpool FC.
He played over 120 international matches for Switzerland.
In 2024 he retired from the national team.

abschnitte.text: Xherdan Shaqiri was born in **Kosovo** and moved to Switzerland with his family when he was still a toddler. He grew up in **Augst** near Basel. There he played football as a child and was soon in FC Basel’s youth teams. He is fairly small, but very strong and fast.

With **FC Basel**, Shaqiri became Swiss champion several times as a young player. His dribbling and shots quickly made him known. In 2012 he moved to Bayern Munich in Germany. In the summer of 2024 he returned to Basel and ended his career there.

With **Bayern Munich**, Shaqiri won the Champions League in 2013, the most important competition for clubs in Europe. Later he also played for Inter Milan and Stoke City. In 2019 he won the Champions League again with **Liverpool FC**. After that he played for Olympique Lyon and for Chicago Fire in the USA.

Shaqiri played over 120 times for the Swiss **national team**. At the 2014 World Cup in Brazil he scored three goals in one match against Honduras. At Euro 2016 he scored a famous overhead kick against Poland. At Euro 2024, too, he scored against Scotland with a fine shot.

Shaqiri is known for his strong left foot and spectacular goals. Because of his powerful build, many fans call him the “Kraftwürfel”, the power cube. He scored at several World Cups and European Championships in a row. He is a role model for many children with roots in other countries, because he shows what is possible in Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: The most important competition for football clubs in Europe.
A shot in which you kick the ball backwards over your head while in the air.
A match between two national teams.
When a player runs past opponents with the ball at their feet.

gewusst: Shaqiri won the Champions League with clubs from two different countries, Germany and England.
His overhead kick against Poland at Euro 2016 is considered one of the most beautiful goals in Swiss football history.

teile.einleitung: Conscience is the inner voice that tells us whether what we do is right or wrong. It often makes itself felt as a good or bad feeling and stays with us all our lives.
wichtigste: Conscience judges your own actions as good or bad.
Pangs of conscience arise when you have acted against your own values.
Conscience is shaped by upbringing and experience.
Article 15 of the Federal Constitution protects freedom of religion and conscience.
Switzerland has had civilian service since 1996.
Antigone and Martin Luther are famous examples of acting according to conscience.

abschnitte.text: **Conscience** is the inner awareness of whether your own actions are right or wrong. If you have done something wrong, you often feel **pangs of conscience**. This unpleasant feeling shows that you have acted against your own values. It can lead you to apologise or to make up for something. If you are convinced you have done nothing wrong, you have a **clear conscience**.

Nobody is born with a finished conscience. According to psychology today, it is shaped by **upbringing and experience**. Children learn from parents, teachers and other role models what is right and wrong. Over many years their own conscience forms in this way. Later people also test these rules for themselves and develop their own convictions.

**Article 15** of the Swiss Federal Constitution guarantees **freedom of religion and conscience**. Every person may freely choose and profess their religion and their philosophical beliefs. Nobody may be forced to join a religious community. So this basic right protects what a person believes deep down to be right.

In Switzerland men are obliged to do military service. Since 1996, anyone who cannot reconcile military service with their conscience can do **civilian service** instead. It lasts longer than military service. It is carried out, for example, in hospitals, care homes, schools or in **nature conservation**. In this way people serve the community in a different way.

In the Greek tragedy **‘Antigone’** by **Sophocles**, Antigone buries her brother even though King Creon has forbidden it. The play shows the conflict between conscience and the law of the state. In 1521, at the Diet of Worms, the reformer **Martin Luther** refused to take back his writings. He is said to have declared that his conscience was captive to the Word of God.

gewusst: The famous sentence ‘Here I stand, I can do no other’ is attributed to Luther, but it was probably only handed down in this form later.
Sophocles wrote ‘Antigone’ about 2,400 years ago.

teile.einleitung: Manuela Schär is a Swiss wheelchair athlete from the canton of Lucerne and one of the best wheelchair racers in the world. She has won Paralympic gold over 800 metres and all the big city marathons. She races in a light three-wheeled racing wheelchair.
wichtigste: Manuela Schär was born in 1984 and comes from the canton of Lucerne.
She has used a wheelchair since an accident in her childhood.
She races in a racing wheelchair in the T54 class.
In Tokyo in 2021 and in Paris in 2024 she won Paralympic gold over 800 metres.
She has won each of the big World Marathon Majors at least once.
She often trains in Nottwil, home of the Swiss Paraplegic Centre.
She is one of the most successful Swiss para athletes.

abschnitte.text: Manuela Schär was born on 5 December 1984. As a child she was badly injured at a children’s birthday party when a badly fixed **swing** fell on her. Since then she has been paraplegic and can no longer move her legs. Even so, she soon found her way to sport.

A **racing wheelchair** is quite different from a normal wheelchair. It has two large wheels at the back and one small wheel at the front, and it is very light. The racer kneels in it and strikes the push rims with special gloves. On the flat you can reach speeds of over 30 kilometres per hour this way.

As early as 2004 in Athens, Schär won her first **Paralympic** medals, silver over 200 metres and bronze over 100 metres. Later she switched to longer distances. In Tokyo in 2021 and Paris in 2024 she became Paralympic champion over **800 metres**. She has also won other medals over other distances.

Schär is also a brilliant **marathon racer**. She has won the big city marathons in Boston, New York, London, Berlin, Chicago and Tokyo. In the 2018/19 season she even won every race in the Marathon Majors series. In 2013 in Lyon she became marathon world champion.

Manuela Schär shows that you can do top-level sport with a disability. She trains very hard, often for several hours a day. Together with Marcel Hug and Catherine Debrunner she is part of a strong Swiss team. Switzerland is one of the most successful countries in the world in wheelchair racing.

begriffe.erklaerung: A light wheelchair with three wheels, built for fast races.
The Olympic Games for athletes with disabilities.
An injury to the spinal cord that means parts of the body can no longer be moved.
The class for wheelchair racers with full strength in the arms and trunk.

gewusst: A wheelchair marathon is often more than an hour faster than the race of the best women runners.
Manuela Schär won every race of the big marathon series in a single season.

teile.einleitung: Gender equality means that women and men have the same rights and opportunities, in the family, at work and in politics. People in Switzerland fought for this for a long time, and much of the progress is quite recent.
wichtigste: The Federal Office for Gender Equality has existed since 1988.
Big women's strikes took place on 14 June 1991 and 2019.
International Women's Day is on 8 March.
Since 2005 there has been paid maternity allowance.
Since 2021 fathers have had two weeks of paid paternity leave.
In 1999 Ruth Dreifuss was the first female President of the Swiss Confederation.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland women only got the right to vote and stand for election at federal level in **1971**. In 1981 the principle of **equal rights** for women and men was written into the Federal Constitution. In 1958 the lawyer **Iris von Roten** published the book ‘Frauen im Laufgitter’ (Women in the Playpen). In it she criticised the way women were restricted in marriage, at work and in politics. The book caused fierce debates at the time.

Since 1988 there has been the **Federal Office for Gender Equality (FOGE)**. It belongs to the Department of Home Affairs. The office works, for example, for **equal pay** and for combining family and work. Fighting violence is also one of its tasks. Many cantons have their own equality offices.

On **14 June 1991** and again on 14 June 2019, hundreds of thousands of women took to the streets in Switzerland. Among other things they demanded **equal pay**. Since then 14 June has been regarded as the day of the women's strike. Worldwide, **International Women's Day** on **8 March** recalls the struggle for women's rights. It has been marked for more than a hundred years.

After several failed attempts, the people approved **maternity insurance** in 2004. Since July 2005, working mothers have received money for **14 weeks** after a child is born. In September 2020 the people also approved paid **paternity leave**. Since 2021 fathers have been entitled to **two weeks**. This is meant to make it easier for both parents to combine family and work.

In 1984 **Elisabeth Kopp** became the first woman elected to the Federal Council. In 1993 she was followed by **Ruth Dreifuss**, a Social Democrat from Geneva. In **1999** she became the first female President of the Swiss Confederation. Since then several women have held this office. Today women are far better represented in parliaments and governments than in the past.

gewusst: In the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden women had to wait until 1990: only a ruling by the Federal Supreme Court gave them the cantonal right to vote.
The motto of the 1991 women's strike was ‘Wenn Frau will, steht alles still’ (when women want, everything stands still).

teile.einleitung: Simon Ammann is a Swiss ski jumper from the Toggenburg. He won Olympic gold four times, twice in 2002 and twice in 2010. That makes him one of the most successful ski jumpers in history.
wichtigste: Simon Ammann was born on 25 June 1981 in Grabs in the canton of St Gallen.
He grew up in Unterwasser in the Toggenburg.
In 2002 in Salt Lake City he won gold on the normal hill and the large hill.
In 2010 in Vancouver he did the same thing again.
He is the only ski jumper with two individual gold medals at each of two different Olympic Games.
In 2007 he became world champion, and in 2010 he won the overall World Cup.

abschnitte.text: Simon Ammann comes from the **Toggenburg** in the canton of St Gallen. He grew up in Unterwasser, a village at the foot of the Churfirsten. Even as a teenager he was jumping off ski jumps. In 1998, at 16, he took part in the Olympic Games for the first time.

At the 2002 Olympic Games in **Salt Lake City**, hardly anyone knew him. But the young Swiss sensationally won on the normal hill and on the large hill. Because of his glasses and boyish looks, people called him “Harry Potter”. Suddenly he was famous all over Switzerland.

Eight years later, in 2010 in **Vancouver**, Ammann again won both individual events. No ski jumper had ever done that before. For the Games he used a new kind of curved binding, which was much discussed at the time. That same winter he also won the overall World Cup.

In 2007 in **Sapporo** in Japan, Ammann became world champion on the large hill. He won many World Cup competitions and was often on the podium. He jumped among the world’s best for many years, much longer than most ski jumpers. He has taken part in several Olympic Games since 1998.

In **ski jumping** you go down a steep in-run and take off at the end of the ramp. In the air, the jumpers hold their skis in a V shape so that they glide better. Both distance and style are judged, for example a clean **telemark landing**. On the large hill, professionals jump well over 120 metres.

begriffe.erklaerung: A structure with a steep in-run from which ski jumpers take off.
A landing with one leg in front of the other, which earns good style marks.
The position in which the skis form a V in the air.
A ranking over the whole season. Whoever has the most points wins.

gewusst: Before the 2002 Olympics, Simon Ammann had never won a World Cup competition.
Simon Ammann jumped in the World Cup for more than two decades, which is unusually long for a ski jumper.

teile.einleitung: Bernhard Russi is a Swiss skiing legend from Andermatt in the canton of Uri. In 1972 he became Olympic downhill champion in Sapporo. After his career he became world famous as a designer of Olympic downhill courses.
wichtigste: Bernhard Russi was born in Andermatt in 1948.
In 1972 he became Olympic downhill champion in Sapporo.
In 1970 he became downhill world champion in Val Gardena.
In 1976 he won Olympic silver in Innsbruck behind Franz Klammer.
He won the downhill World Cup twice, in 1971 and 1972.
Since the end of his career he has designed downhill courses, including for Olympic Games.
For a long time he was a skiing expert on Swiss television.

abschnitte.text: **Bernhard Russi** was born on 20 August 1948 in **Andermatt** in the canton of Uri. The mountain village by the Gotthard is a well-known winter sports resort. Russi learnt to ski there early and made it into the national team. Alongside his sport he trained as a building draughtsman. This knowledge of terrain and plans helped him a great deal later.

In 1970 Russi surprisingly became downhill world champion in **Val Gardena** in Italy. Two years later, in 1972 in **Sapporo** in Japan, he became Olympic champion in the **downhill**. In these years he also won the World Cup downhill ranking twice. In 1976 in Innsbruck he won Olympic silver as well. Gold went to the Austrian Franz Klammer.

After retiring in 1978, Russi began to design **downhill courses**. Since the 1988 Olympic Games in Calgary he has planned the downhill courses of many Winter Games. These include, for example, Sochi 2014, Pyeongchang 2018 and Beijing 2022. As a **course architect** he looks for a line through the terrain that is exciting, fast and safe. He is in demand all over the world for this.

For many years Russi commented on ski races as an **expert** on Swiss television. He also appeared in adverts and is one of the best-known sportsmen in Switzerland. His calm knowledge of ski racing is highly valued.

Russi belongs to a golden generation of Swiss skiers in the 1970s. Together with stars such as Marie-Theres Nadig, he made the 1972 Games in Sapporo a great Swiss success. In Andermatt he is still the village’s famous son. Young racers see him as a role model for a career that carries on after racing.

begriffe.erklaerung: The fastest discipline in alpine ski racing.
A person who plans where and how a race course runs.
A series of races over a whole winter.
Someone who wins the gold medal at the Olympic Games.

gewusst: Bernhard Russi has designed more Olympic downhill courses than anyone else.
In Switzerland the 1972 Games in Sapporo are often called the golden days of Sapporo.
Russi was already world champion before he turned 22.

teile.einleitung: Courage means doing something even though you are afraid, because it is right or important. Being brave does not mean having no fear. And courage is not the same as recklessness.
wichtigste: You show courage if you try something even though you are afraid.
Helping a child who is being picked on is brave.
Running across the road when the light is red is not brave but reckless.
It is brave to say ‘no’ when others want something wrong.
Admitting a mistake takes courage.
The opposite of brave is cowardly.

abschnitte.text: **Courage** means doing something even though you are afraid. If you are afraid of a task and still try it, you are showing courage. Fear is completely normal; brave people feel it too. The opposite of brave is **cowardly**. Someone is cowardly if, out of fear, they do not do something important even though they could.

Not everything that is dangerous is brave. Running across the road when the light is red is **reckless**, because you put yourself in danger for no good reason. Real courage has a good aim, for example helping someone. Reckless people often just want to show off. Brave people think first and judge what they can do.

If a child is being picked on or laughed at, it is brave to **help** them. A clear sentence such as **‘Stop it!’** can make a big difference. Anyone who just watches and does nothing is a **bystander**. But you do not have to put yourself in danger: fetching an adult is brave too. The courage to stand up for others is called **moral courage**.

It takes courage to say **‘no’** when others want something wrong or dangerous. You risk the others laughing at you. **Admitting a mistake** is also brave, because it is uncomfortable. If you admit your mistake, you show honesty and can put it right. Others will then trust you more.

gewusst: The ancient Greeks already counted bravery among the four most important virtues.
The philosopher Aristotle said that bravery lies in the middle between cowardice and foolhardiness.

teile.einleitung: Tolerance means accepting and respecting other opinions, beliefs and ways of life, even if you do not share them yourself. It is an important basis for living together peacefully.
wichtigste: The word tolerance comes from the Latin tolerare, to bear.
In 1689 John Locke wrote a famous ‘Letter Concerning Toleration’.
Lessing's play ‘Nathan the Wise’ is regarded as a work about religious tolerance.
In 1598 the Edict of Nantes granted French Protestants freedom of religion.
The International Day for Tolerance is on 16 November.
According to a widely held view, tolerance ends where the rights of others are violated.
The opposite of tolerance is intolerance.

abschnitte.text: The word **tolerance** comes from the Latin **tolerare**, which means ‘to bear’ or ‘to endure’. A tolerant person accepts other opinions and ways of life, even if they do not share them. The opposite is **intolerance**. In class you show tolerance by **listening** and letting others **finish speaking**. You can still disagree and say so in a friendly way.

For a long time there were fierce struggles between Christian denominations in Europe. In **1598**, with the **Edict of Nantes**, King Henry IV granted the French Protestants, the Huguenots, freedom of religion. It was later revoked, and many Huguenots fled, including to Switzerland. In **1689** the English philosopher **John Locke** wrote a famous **‘Letter Concerning Toleration’**. In it he demanded that the state should not force people's beliefs.

The German poet **Gotthold Ephraim Lessing** wrote the play **‘Nathan the Wise’**. It is regarded as the best-known work about religious tolerance. It contains the **parable of the rings**: a father has three sons and has two rings made that cannot be told apart from the real one. The three rings stand for Judaism, Christianity and Islam. The story invites people to respect each other instead of arguing about which faith is the right one.

Tolerance does not mean accepting everything. According to a widely held view, it ends **where the rights of others are violated**, for example with violence or discrimination. The philosopher **Karl Popper** described the **paradox of tolerance**: a society that tolerates even intolerance without limit could in the end lose tolerance itself. That is why the rule of law protects basic rights for everyone.

On **16 November** the UN celebrates the **International Day for Tolerance**. In Switzerland the Federal Constitution guarantees **freedom of religion and conscience**. In a country with four national languages and many religions, tolerance is especially important. It helps people of different backgrounds to live well together.

gewusst: In engineering, ‘tolerance’ means the permitted deviation from a measurement, for example with screws.
Many Huguenots who fled to Switzerland brought their knowledge with them, for example of watchmaking.

teile.einleitung: Ethics is a branch of philosophy. It asks what good and right action is and how moral rules can be justified.
wichtigste: The word ethics comes from the Greek ‘ethos’, meaning habit, custom and character.
Aristotle made ethics a subject in its own right.
Morality is the practice people live by; ethics thinks about it.
Descriptive ethics describes morality without judging it.
Metaethics examines the meaning of moral statements.
Applied ethics includes, for example, medical, business and environmental ethics.
According to David Hume, an ought does not automatically follow from an is.

abschnitte.text: The word **ethics** comes from the Greek **‘ethos’**. It refers to a person's usual dwelling place, their customs and their character. **Aristotle** is regarded as the founder of ethics as a field of its own. He treated it as a separate discipline alongside logic and physics. His well-known work is called the ‘Nicomachean Ethics’.

In philosophy a distinction is often made between **morality** and **ethics**. Morality is the norms and values a community actually lives by, for example ‘You should not steal’. Ethics is **thinking about morality**. It asks why a rule applies and whether it is well justified. In everyday life, however, the two words are often used to mean the same thing.

**Descriptive ethics** describes which moral ideas apply in a society, without judging them. It works rather like sociology or ethnology. **Normative ethics** asks what we should do. Important approaches are virtue ethics, the ethics of duty and consequentialist ethics. **Metaethics** stands one level above: it examines what words such as ‘good’ mean and whether moral statements can be true.

**Applied ethics** transfers ethical theories to concrete areas of life. These include **medical ethics**, **business ethics** and **environmental ethics**. Typical questions are about fair wages, protecting nature or how we treat animals. In Switzerland, for example, the National Advisory Commission on Biomedical Ethics advises the authorities and the public on human medicine.

In the 18th century the Scottish philosopher **David Hume** noticed that many authors switch from ‘is’ to ‘ought’ without realising it. But an ought does not simply follow from statements about what is. This is called the **is-ought problem**. Another disputed question concerns **ethical relativism**. It says that moral norms only apply relative to a culture. Critics object that then you could no longer condemn, for example, slavery in other cultures.

gewusst: Aristotle was a pupil of Plato and the teacher of Alexander the Great.
The ‘Nicomachean Ethics’ is probably named after Nicomachus, the son or father of Aristotle.

teile.einleitung: Stan Wawrinka is a Swiss tennis player from the canton of Vaud. He won three Grand Slam tournaments and, in 2008, Olympic gold in the doubles with Roger Federer. He is famous for his powerful one-handed backhand.
wichtigste: Stan Wawrinka was born in Lausanne on 28 March 1985.
He won three Grand Slam singles tournaments.
In 2008 in Beijing he won Olympic gold in the doubles with Roger Federer.
In 2014 he won the Davis Cup with Switzerland.
His highest world ranking was number 3.
His one-handed backhand is considered one of the best in the world.

abschnitte.text: Stanislas “Stan” Wawrinka comes from French-speaking Switzerland and speaks French as his mother tongue. He grew up on a farm in **Saint-Barthélemy** in the canton of Vaud. Early on he showed great talent for tennis. In 2003 he won the Roland Garros junior tournament.

Wawrinka won the **Australian Open** in 2014, the French Open in Paris in 2015 and the US Open in 2016. In all three finals he beat the world number 1. In 2015 he beat Novak Djokovic, in 2014 Rafael Nadal. That makes him one of the few players who managed to win big titles against Federer, Nadal and Djokovic in that era.

At the 2008 Olympic Games in **Beijing**, Wawrinka played doubles together with Roger Federer. The two Swiss players won the gold medal in the final against a team from Sweden. Their celebration went round the world. This medal is one of the finest moments in Swiss tennis.

In 2014 Switzerland won the **Davis Cup**, the most important team competition in tennis, for the first time. Wawrinka and Federer were the two stars of the team. In the final in Lille they beat France. The whole country celebrated this historic success.

Wawrinka is known for his powerful **one-handed backhand**. Many players today hit the backhand with two hands, which is why his shot stands out so much. He plays with great force from the baseline. Because of his fighting spirit, fans also call him “Stan the Man”.

begriffe.erklaerung: The four most important tennis tournaments in the world.
A shot in which the back of the hand faces the ball.
A tennis match with two players on each side.
A competition in which national teams play each other at tennis.

gewusst: Stan Wawrinka only won his three Grand Slam titles at the ages of 28, 30 and 31, so relatively late.
In all three Grand Slam finals he won, he beat the world number 1 of the time.

teile.einleitung: Gender roles are ideas about which tasks, jobs or behaviours are seen as typical for women and men. Such role models come from tradition, upbringing and the media, and they change over time.
wichtigste: A role model shows what a society expects of people.
Around 1900 pink was often seen as a suitable colour for little boys.
A househusband runs the household and looks after the children.
More and more fathers work part-time.
On National Future Day, children discover jobs without stereotypes.
In 2025 the Women's European Football Championship took place in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: A **role model** (in the sense of a set of expectations) describes which tasks and behaviours a society expects of people. For a long time, for example, it was thought that men earn money and women look after the household and the children. Role models come from **upbringing, the media and tradition**. They are not laws of nature and can change a great deal. Today many families share the tasks differently.

One example shows how ideas change. Around 1900 **pink** was often seen as a suitable colour for little **boys**. At that time pink was regarded as the little sister of strong red, and red was seen as masculine. The idea of pink for girls only caught on during the 20th century. So colours for boys and girls are a matter of **habit**, not nature.

A **househusband** is a man who mainly runs the household and looks after the children, often while his partner goes out to work. In the past this was seen as a typical woman's role. In Switzerland many people work **part-time**, that is fewer hours than in a full-time job. This makes it easier to combine family and work. More and more fathers are reducing their working hours for this.

Every job should be open to everyone, whatever their gender. That is why there are **gender-neutral** job titles, such as ‘Fachperson Gesundheit’ (healthcare specialist). On **National Future Day**, children in years 5 to 7 often go to work with a parent or someone they know. The idea is that they also discover **untypical jobs**, for example girls in engineering or boys in nursing.

For a long time football was seen as a typical **men's sport**. In summer 2025 the **Women's European Football Championship** took place in Switzerland. Women's EURO 2025 drew many spectators into the stadiums. This shows that sport is for everyone. In ballet, figure skating or Swiss wrestling, too, people of every gender take part today.

gewusst: In Switzerland women only got the right to vote and stand for election at federal level in 1971.
National Future Day takes place every year in November.

tq47zyr.t: National Advisory Commission on Biomedical Ethics

teile.einleitung: The National Advisory Commission on Biomedical Ethics, NEK for short in German, advises politicians and the public in Switzerland on ethical questions in medicine. The Federal Council set it up in 2001.
wichtigste: The Federal Council set up the NEK in 2001.
The NEK is responsible for ethical questions in human medicine.
Its secretariat is based at the Federal Office of Public Health.
It is an extra-parliamentary commission and is independent in what it says.
Individual research projects are reviewed by the cantonal ethics committees, not by the NEK.
In 2019 the NEK recommended the declaration model for organ donation.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Council** set up the NEK on **3 July 2001**. Its full name is the **National Advisory Commission on Biomedical Ethics** (in German, Nationale Ethikkommission im Bereich der Humanmedizin). It is an **extra-parliamentary commission**, that is a federal expert body whose members are chosen by the Federal Council. Its **secretariat** is based at the **Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH)** in Bern. In what it says, however, it works **independently** and is not bound by any instructions.

The NEK writes **opinions**, advises the authorities and informs the public. Its mandate expressly includes encouraging **public dialogue** on ethical questions in medicine. It deals, for example, with questions at the end of life, with vaccinations or with **organ donation**. In 2019 it spoke out against the opt-out solution and recommended the **declaration model**: people should be asked regularly to state their wishes on organ donation. But it does not pass any laws.

The NEK comments on fundamental questions, not on individual applications. Specific **research projects involving humans** are reviewed and approved by the **cantonal ethics committees**, on the basis of the Human Research Act. Since **1998** the **ECNH** (in German EKAH) has been responsible for ethical questions of bio- and gene technology in animals, plants and other organisms. It has, for example, dealt with the dignity of plants.

gewusst: In French the NEK is called the ‘Commission nationale d'éthique’, abbreviated CNE.
The ECNH published a much-discussed report on the dignity of plants.

teile.einleitung: Socrates was a philosopher in ancient Athens and is regarded as one of the founders of Western philosophy. He wrote nothing down himself, but held conversations. We know his thoughts mainly through his pupil Plato.
wichtigste: We know Socrates' thoughts mainly through his pupil Plato.
With maieutics, Socrates helped others to bring out knowledge themselves.
The oracle of Delphi is said to have declared that nobody was wiser than Socrates.
An inner voice, the daimonion, held him back from wrong actions.
The thesis is attributed to him: nobody does wrong knowingly.
In 399 BC he was condemned for impiety and corrupting the young.
He died by drinking a cup of hemlock.

abschnitte.text: **Socrates** lived in **Athens** in the 5th century BC. He wrote no books himself, but talked with people in the marketplace about questions such as: what is just? What is a good life? We know his thoughts mainly through his pupil **Plato**, who wrote down many conversations. The writer Xenophon also reported on him.

Socrates usually did not give ready-made answers. He kept asking questions until the people he was talking with reached new insights themselves. This method is called **maieutics**, in English the **art of midwifery**. Socrates compared himself to a midwife: just as she only helps at a birth, he helped others to bring their own knowledge to light. Often his questions also showed that someone knew less than they thought.

The **oracle of Delphi** is said to have announced that nobody was wiser than Socrates. Socrates explained it like this: at least he knew that he knew nothing. This became the well-known saying **‘I know that I know nothing’**. Socrates also spoke of an inner voice that held him back from wrong actions. He called it the **daimonion**.

For Socrates, knowledge and good action were closely linked. The thesis is attributed to him: **nobody does wrong knowingly**. According to this view, anyone who really knows what is good will also act well. Wrongdoing therefore comes from ignorance. This attitude is called **ethical intellectualism**.

In **399 BC** Socrates was put on trial in Athens. He was accused of **impiety** and **corrupting the young**. He was sentenced to death and had to drink a **cup of hemlock**, a drink made from a poisonous plant. Plato's work **‘Apology’** records his speech in his defence before the court. Socrates is said to have refused to escape because he wanted to respect the laws of his city.

gewusst: According to Plato, Socrates' mother was herself a midwife, which is why his comparison fitted especially well.
The poet Aristophanes made fun of Socrates in his play ‘The Clouds’ while Socrates was still alive.

teile.einleitung: Assisted dying is an umbrella term for actions relating to the death of a seriously ill person. The subject is ethically very controversial. Switzerland has its own rules on it, which differ from those of many other countries.
wichtigste: A distinction is made between passive, indirect active and direct active euthanasia, as well as assisted suicide.
Direct active euthanasia is a criminal offence in Switzerland as ‘killing on request’.
Under Art. 115 of the Criminal Code, assisting suicide is only a criminal offence if done for selfish motives.
Passive euthanasia means not starting or stopping life-sustaining treatment.
Exit was founded in 1982, and Dignitas in 1998 by Ludwig A. Minelli.
In 2012 Vaud became the first canton to regulate assisted suicide in hospitals and care homes by popular vote.

abschnitte.text: In **passive euthanasia**, life-sustaining treatment is not started or is stopped, for example artificial ventilation. In **indirect active euthanasia**, painkillers are given that may shorten life as a side effect. The intention is to relieve suffering. Both forms are regarded as permissible in Switzerland if they match the patient's wishes. You can set out your own wishes in an **advance directive**.

**Direct active euthanasia** is forbidden in Switzerland. The Criminal Code punishes it as **killing on request** (Art. 114). **Assisted suicide** is different: under **Art. 115 of the Criminal Code** it is only a criminal offence if someone acts for **selfish motives**, for example out of greed. What matters is that the person concerned carries out the final act themselves. The Swiss assisted dying organisations base their work on this rule.

The organisation **Exit** was founded in **1982** and is the largest of its kind in Switzerland. In **1998** the lawyer **Ludwig A. Minelli** founded the organisation **Dignitas**, which also accompanies people from abroad. In **2012** voters in the canton of **Vaud** were the first to approve rules on assisted suicide in hospitals and nursing homes. In September 2024 a new, controversial device was used for the first time in the canton of **Schaffhausen**, after which the authorities opened criminal proceedings.

Assisted dying is much discussed in society. Supporters stress a person's **self-determination** over the end of their life. Critics fear that ill or old people could feel under pressure. Many religious communities also view assisted dying critically. An important alternative is **palliative care**, which relieves pain and accompanies people at the end of their lives. Anyone who has worries can find help: children and teenagers, for example, on the number **147**, and adults with Die Dargebotene Hand (the Swiss helpline) on **143**.

gewusst: Switzerland is one of the few countries where assisted suicide is allowed under certain conditions.
Exit only accompanies members who live in Switzerland or have Swiss citizenship.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss national handball team is the men’s team that represents Switzerland in handball. Handball is a fast team sport in which the ball is thrown into the goal by hand. The best-known Swiss handball player is Andy Schmid, who is also the Nati’s record goal scorer.
wichtigste: A handball team has 7 players on the court at a time, six outfield players and a goalkeeper.
Andy Schmid is the record goal scorer of the Swiss national handball team.
Andy Schmid later became coach of the Nati.
Switzerland won Olympic bronze in field handball in 1936.
Switzerland hosted the men’s World Championship in 1986 and the European Championship in 2006.
Since 2020 the Nati has again qualified more often for big tournaments.
The national association is called Swiss Handball.

abschnitte.text: In handball two teams each have **7 players** on the court at the same time, six outfield players and a goalkeeper. The court is 40 metres long and 20 metres wide. Around each goal there is a **goal area** that only the goalkeeper may enter. With the ball in your hand you may take at most three steps; then you have to bounce, pass or shoot. A game lasts two halves of 30 minutes.

Handball came about at the end of the 19th century in Denmark and Germany. In the past it was often played outdoors on large grass pitches, as **field handball** with eleven players. At the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin, Switzerland won bronze in this version. Later indoor handball took over. Switzerland hosted a men’s World Championship in 1986 and a European Championship in 2006.

**Andy Schmid** from Horgen is the best Swiss handball player in history. He played for ten years for the Rhein-Neckar Löwen in the German **Bundesliga**, one of the strongest leagues in the world. There he was voted the best player in the league several times. He scored more goals for Switzerland than anyone else and is the **record goal scorer**. After his playing career he took over as national coach in 2024.

For a long time Switzerland missed almost all the big tournaments. Since **Euro 2020** it has been there more often again, for example at the 2021 World Championship and Euro 2024. Young players such as Manuel Zehnder play in the German Bundesliga. The Swiss league is called the **Quickline Handball League**; well-known clubs are Kadetten Schaffhausen, Pfadi Winterthur and HC Kriens-Luzern.

Many children and young people in Switzerland play handball, especially in German-speaking Switzerland. The women’s Nati is getting stronger too and co-hosted the 2024 Women’s European Championship, with matches in Basel. Everything is organised by the association **Swiss Handball**. Handball is seen as fast, physical and very high-scoring; often more than 50 goals are scored in a game.

begriffe.erklaerung: The area in front of the goal that only the goalkeeper may enter.
Tapping the ball onto the floor with one hand and catching it again (dribbling).
A penalty throw straight at the goal from seven metres away.
The players who stand further back and often shoot from a distance.

gewusst: Handball players rub resin on their hands so that the ball sticks better.
A hard handball throw can travel at over 100 kilometres per hour.
In handball the goalkeeper may also stop the ball with their feet.

teile.einleitung: Human rights are rights that every person has, simply because they are human. The most important foundation is the UN's Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948. Binding treaties followed later.
wichtigste: The UN adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on 10 December 1948.
The Declaration is a resolution and is not binding under international law.
Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the commission that drew up the Declaration.
Human rights are regarded as universal, inalienable and indivisible.
They are often divided into three generations.
The UN Human Rights Council was founded in 2006 and is based in Geneva.
In 1992 Switzerland joined the two UN human rights covenants.

abschnitte.text: On **10 December 1948** the UN General Assembly in Paris adopted the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights**. Since then 10 December has been Human Rights Day. The Declaration has 30 articles. It is a **resolution**, that is a recommendation, and is not legally binding. Even so, it has strongly shaped thinking about human rights all over the world.

The Declaration was drawn up by the UN Commission on Human Rights. It was chaired by **Eleanor Roosevelt**, the former First Lady of the USA. She worked hard to make sure that many countries could agree on a shared text. Experts from different cultures took part.
