Binding treaties only followed later, above all the two **human rights covenants** of **1966**.

Human rights are regarded as **universal**: they apply to all people everywhere. They are **inalienable**: you cannot give them away or sell them, and nobody may take them away from you. And they are **indivisible**: they belong together and must not be played off against each other. The state has the task of respecting and protecting human rights.

Human rights are often divided into **generations**. The **first generation** covers freedoms such as freedom of expression and the right to vote. The **second generation** are economic, social and cultural rights, for example the **right to education** or to health care. The **third generation** includes rights that often belong to peoples or groups, such as the **right to a healthy environment**, to development and to peace.

The **UN Human Rights Council** was founded in **2006** and is based in **Geneva**. It meets in the Palais des Nations and replaced the former Commission on Human Rights. In **1992** **Switzerland** joined the covenant on civil and political rights and the covenant on economic, social and cultural rights, ten years before it joined the UN in 2002. Switzerland had already ratified the **European Convention on Human Rights** in 1974.

gewusst: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights is one of the texts that has been translated into the most languages in the world.
Even before it joined the UN, Switzerland hosted many UN meetings in Geneva.

teile.einleitung: Swiss Olympic is the umbrella organisation of Swiss sport and at the same time the National Olympic Committee of Switzerland. It selects the athletes for the Olympic Games and supports the sports associations. At the 2026 Winter Games in Milan and Cortina, Switzerland won 23 medals in total.
wichtigste: Swiss Olympic is the National Olympic Committee of Switzerland.
It is also the umbrella organisation of over 80 Swiss sports associations.
It is based at the House of Sport in Ittigen near Bern.
St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics twice, in 1928 and 1948.
At the 2026 Winter Games, Switzerland won 23 medals.
The International Olympic Committee is based in Lausanne.
Swiss Olympic supports top-level sport, young athletes and fair sport.

abschnitte.text: **Swiss Olympic** is the umbrella organisation of Swiss sport. More than 80 national **sports associations** belong to it, from football and skiing to Swiss wrestling. At the same time it is the **National Olympic Committee** of Switzerland. Swiss Olympic was created in 1997 from the merger of the Olympic Committee and the national sports association. It is based at the House of Sport in Ittigen near Bern.

Swiss Olympic puts together the Swiss team for the **Olympic Games**. It distributes funding to the associations and supports talented athletes with the **Swiss Olympic Card**. It also works for clean sport without doping and promotes values such as respect and fairness. Together with the Confederation it also looks after sports schools and the training of coaches.

**St Moritz** in the Engadine hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948. It is one of only a few places in the world to have held the Winter Games twice. In 2020 the **Winter Youth Olympic Games** took place in Lausanne. Several later bids, for example for Sion or the Grisons, failed in popular votes or in the selection process. The IOC is in talks with Switzerland about the 2038 Winter Games.

At the 2026 Winter Olympics in **Milan and Cortina**, Switzerland won **23 medals** in total. There were medals, for example, in alpine skiing, curling and women’s ice hockey. Switzerland is one of the strongest nations in the world in winter sport, and measured by its population even one of the very best. In summer, tennis, cycling, rowing and triathlon are particularly successful.

Since 1915 the **International Olympic Committee** has been based in Lausanne on Lake Geneva. The founder of the modern Games, Pierre de Coubertin, had moved its headquarters there. The **Olympic Museum** is also in Lausanne. On top of that, dozens of international sports federations have settled in the region. That is why Lausanne calls itself the Olympic capital.

begriffe.erklaerung: An organisation that brings many associations together.
The International Olympic Committee, which organises the Olympic Games.
All the athletes and staff that a country sends to a competition.
Banned substances used to boost performance artificially.

gewusst: The Olympic rings were designed by Pierre de Coubertin, who is buried in Lausanne.
At the 1948 Games in St Moritz there was skeleton on the Cresta Run, a sport that is seldom seen today.
Switzerland has taken part in almost all the Olympic Games of modern times.

teile.einleitung: Michelle Gisin is a Swiss ski racer from Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. She became Olympic champion in the alpine combined in 2018 and 2022. She is an all-rounder who skis well in both the fast and the technical disciplines.
wichtigste: Michelle Gisin was born in Samedan in 1993 and grew up in Engelberg.
She races in almost all the disciplines of skiing.
In 2018 in Pyeongchang she became Olympic champion in the combined.
In 2022 in Beijing she won the combined a second time.
In Beijing she also won bronze in the super-G.
Her sister Dominique Gisin became Olympic downhill champion in 2014.
Her brother Marc Gisin was also a ski racer.

abschnitte.text: Michelle Gisin was born on 5 January 1993 in **Samedan** in the Engadine. She grew up in **Engelberg** in the canton of Obwalden, a well-known ski resort with a famous monastery. There she skied on the Titlis even as a small child. Her whole family is closely connected with skiing.

In the **alpine combined** a fast discipline and a slalom count together. First you race a downhill or a super-G, then a **slalom**. The two times are added together, and the shortest total time wins. So you have to be fast and at the same time be able to ski tight gates cleanly.

At the 2018 Olympic Games in **Pyeongchang**, Gisin won the combined. Four years later in **Beijing** she was able to defend the title. There she also won a bronze medal in the super-G. Only a few skiers have won the same discipline twice in a row.

Michelle Gisin comes from a real **skiing family**. Her older sister Dominique Gisin became Olympic downhill champion in Sochi in 2014, in exactly the same time as Tina Maze. Her brother Marc Gisin also raced in the World Cup. Her partner is the Italian ski racer Luca De Aliprandini.

Gisin races in downhill, super-G, giant slalom and slalom. Racers like this are called **all-rounders**. She has also won World Cup races and medals at World Championships. Several times she has had to fight her way back after illnesses and falls.

begriffe.erklaerung: A competition made of a fast discipline and a slalom together.
The discipline with the tightest gates and quickest changes of direction.
Someone who is good at many different disciplines.
The fastest ski discipline, with high speeds and jumps.

gewusst: The sisters Dominique and Michelle Gisin are both Olympic champions.
In 2014 Dominique Gisin and Tina Maze won the downhill in exactly the same time, to the hundredth of a second.

teile.einleitung: Animal ethics asks how humans should treat animals and what consideration they owe them. Philosophers have given very different answers to this. In Switzerland the subject also plays a part in the constitution and in popular votes.
wichtigste: Speciesism is disadvantaging living beings solely because of their species.
Jeremy Bentham asked whether animals can suffer, not whether they can think.
In the 17th century René Descartes regarded animals as machines without souls.
In 1983 Tom Regan founded a rights-based approach.
The three Rs in animal experiments stand for Replace, Reduce, Refine.
Since 1992 the ‘dignity of living beings’ has been in the Federal Constitution.
On 25 September 2022 voters rejected the factory farming initiative by about 63 per cent.

abschnitte.text: In the 17th century the French philosopher **René Descartes** regarded animals as **automata without souls**, that is as machines without consciousness. This view was later sharply criticised. In 1789 the Englishman **Jeremy Bentham**, one of the founders of utilitarianism, wrote that the decisive question is not whether animals can think or talk, but **whether they can suffer**. For him the **ability to suffer** was the reason to take animals into moral account.

The term **speciesism** means disadvantaging living beings solely because of the species they belong to. It was coined in 1970 by Richard Ryder and made well known by the philosopher **Peter Singer**. With his book **‘The Case for Animal Rights’** (1983), the American **Tom Regan** founded a rights-based approach. For him animals have a value of their own and therefore rights. Other philosophers, on the other hand, think it is justifiable to use animals as long as they are treated well.

abschnitte.titel: Animal experiments and the three Rs
abschnitte.text: For **animal experiments**, the **3R principle** is meant to apply. The three Rs stand for **Replace**, **Reduce** and **Refine** (that is, lessening the strain on the animals). The researchers William Russell and Rex Burch formulated it in 1959. In Switzerland a dedicated 3R competence centre promotes these aims. Animal experiments in Switzerland need a permit.

abschnitte.titel: Switzerland and the dignity of animals
abschnitte.text: In **1893** the Swiss people approved the very first popular initiative: it banned **slaughtering without stunning**. In **1992** the **‘dignity of living beings’** was added to the Federal Constitution; it applies to animals, plants and other organisms. Switzerland was one of the first countries with such a concept. On **25 September 2022** voters rejected the **factory farming initiative** by **about 63 per cent**. Opponents pointed to Switzerland's already strict animal welfare law.

gewusst: Bentham's sentence is often quoted in English: ‘Can they suffer?’
Switzerland is one of very few countries whose constitution also speaks of the dignity of plants and other living things.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss women’s national football team is the women’s football team that represents Switzerland internationally. In 2025 Switzerland hosted the Women’s European Championship and enjoyed a great festival of football. The Nati reached the quarter-finals and thrilled the whole country.
wichtigste: The 2025 Women’s European Championship took place in Switzerland.
Matches were played in eight Swiss cities, and the final was in Basel.
The women’s Nati went out in the quarter-finals against Spain.
The coach at Euro 2025 was the Swede Pia Sundhage.
The team first took part in a World Cup in 2015 in Canada.
The record goal scorer is Ana-Maria Crnogorčević.
Women’s football is becoming more and more popular in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **women’s Nati** is run by the Swiss Football Association. For a long time it was in the shadow of the men. Since the 2010s, however, it has regularly qualified for big tournaments. It played its first **World Cup** in 2015 in Canada and reached the round of 16 there. At the 2023 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand it also reached the round of 16.

From 2 to 27 July 2025 the **Women’s Euro** took place in Switzerland. Matches were played in Basel, Bern, Geneva, Zurich, Lucerne, St Gallen, Sion and Thun. The stadiums were often sold out, and thousands of fans marched through the cities in **fan marches**. In the final in Basel, England beat Spain on penalties. It was one of the biggest sporting events in Switzerland for years.

In the group stage Switzerland played Norway, Iceland and Finland. It beat Iceland 2:0. Against Finland, **Riola Xhemaili** equalised to make it 1:1 in stoppage time, which secured a place in the quarter-finals. There Switzerland lost 0:2 in Bern to **Spain**, one of the best teams in the world. Even so, the fans celebrated the team.

**Ana-Maria Crnogorčević** is by far the record goal scorer of the women’s Nati. **Lara Dickenmann** was one of the first Swiss players to play for big foreign clubs. Lia Wälti was captain for a long time and played for many years at Arsenal in England. Young talents such as **Sydney Schertenleib** now play for top clubs such as FC Barcelona.

More and more girls and women are playing football in Switzerland; today there are tens of thousands of registered players. The top league is called the **Women’s Super League**. After the home Euro, the association and the clubs want to support women’s football further. The aim is for girls everywhere to find a team nearby. The Nati’s matches are now also shown on television.

begriffe.erklaerung: The round with the last eight teams of a tournament.
The country in which a tournament takes place.
Extra minutes at the end of a match to make up for interruptions.
The player who has scored the most goals.

gewusst: At Euro 2025 more than 600,000 spectators came to the stadiums altogether, more than ever before at a Women’s Euro.
The home Euro 2025 was celebrated in many Swiss cities with fan zones and public viewings.
In the final of Euro 2025 in Basel, a penalty shootout was needed to decide the winners.

teile.einleitung: Dario Cologna is the most successful cross-country skier in Swiss history. He won four Olympic gold medals in cross-country skiing and the overall World Cup four times. He comes from the Val Müstair, a remote valley in the canton of the Grisons.
wichtigste: Dario Cologna was born in 1986 in the Val Müstair in the Grisons.
His sport is cross-country skiing.
He won four Olympic gold medals.
He celebrated his Olympic victories in 2010, twice in 2014 and in 2018.
He won the overall World Cup four times and the Tour de Ski four times.
In 2013 he became world champion in the skiathlon.
He ended his cross-country skiing career in 2022.

abschnitte.text: **Dario Cologna** was born on 11 March 1986 and grew up in the **Val Müstair**, the easternmost valley in Switzerland. Romansh is spoken there. As a teenager he concentrated fully on **cross-country skiing**. His younger brother Gianluca also became a cross-country skier.

In 2010 in **Vancouver** Cologna won his first Olympic gold over 15 kilometres in the free technique. In 2014 in **Sochi** he won gold twice, in the **skiathlon** and over 15 kilometres classic. He managed this even though he had had a serious ankle injury shortly before. In 2018 in Pyeongchang he won again over 15 kilometres free. In this way he won the same Olympic event three times in a row.

abschnitte.titel: World Cup and Tour de Ski
abschnitte.text: Cologna won the **overall World Cup** in cross-country skiing four times, in 2009, 2011, 2012 and 2015. He also won the **Tour de Ski**, a tough series of stages over New Year, four times. In 2013 in Val di Fiemme he became world champion in the skiathlon. In many races he beat the strong competition from Norway. That made him famous in the cross-country skiing world.

In **cross-country skiing** you move on narrow skis along snowy trails. There are two techniques: the **classic style** in tracks and the **skating technique**, which is like ice skating. Cross-country skiing is considered one of the most exhausting endurance sports in the world. In summer the professionals often train on roller skis.

Before Cologna, cross-country skiing was seen as rather a minor sport in Switzerland. Thanks to his successes the sport became much more popular, and many children took up cross-country skiing. He was also voted **Swiss Sportsman of the Year**. After retiring in 2022 he stayed connected with the sport. In the Val Müstair he is a great hero.

begriffe.erklaerung: A prepared track or course for cross-country skiers (German Loipe).
A race in which you first ski in the classic style and then in the skating technique.
A cross-country technique with sideways steps, as in ice skating.
A series of cross-country races on several days in a row.

gewusst: Together with Simon Ammann, Dario Cologna is the Swiss athlete with the most individual Olympic victories at the Winter Games.
A top cross-country skier can burn over 1000 kilocalories per hour in a hard race.
The Val Müstair lies so far east that it borders Italy and lies on the southern side of the Alps.

teile.einleitung: Steve Guerdat is a Swiss show jumper from the canton of Jura. In 2012 in London he became Olympic champion with his horse Nino des Buissonnets. He has been one of the best show jumpers in the world for many years.
wichtigste: Steve Guerdat was born on 10 June 1982 in Bassecourt in the canton of Jura.
His sport is show jumping.
In 2012 he became Olympic champion in London with Nino des Buissonnets.
In 2008 he won Olympic bronze with the Swiss team.
In 2024 in Paris he won Olympic silver with the horse Dynamix de Belheme.
He won the World Cup Final three times, in 2015, 2016 and 2019.

abschnitte.text: Steve Guerdat comes from **Bassecourt** in the canton of Jura. His father, Philippe Guerdat, was a show jumper himself and took part in the Olympic Games twice. So Steve grew up with horses. Even as a teenager he rode in competitions.

In **show jumping** a horse and its rider have to jump a course of obstacles. The obstacles can be over 1.60 metres high. If a pole falls down, you get **penalty points**. The time also counts, and rider and horse have to work together perfectly as a team.

At the 2012 Olympic Games in **London**, Guerdat won the individual gold medal. His horse was called Nino des Buissonnets. For Switzerland it was a great success in equestrian sport. In 2008 in Hong Kong, where the equestrian events of the Beijing Games were held, he had already won bronze with the team.

In 2024 in **Paris**, Guerdat won individual silver. This time he rode the horse Dynamix de Belheme. That meant he had won medals at three different Olympic Games. The competitions took place in front of the famous Palace of Versailles.

Guerdat won the show jumping **World Cup** Final three times: in 2015, 2016 and 2019. Each time he was on a different horse, namely Paille, Corbinian and Alamo. A show jumper works with their horses for years and has a close relationship with them. Guerdat is seen as a rider who is especially sensitive with horses.

begriffe.erklaerung: The route with all the obstacles, which have to be jumped in a certain order.
Points you get for mistakes, for example when a pole falls.
A deciding round when several riders have had no faults.
The closing competition of a whole season with the best riders in the world.

gewusst: In show jumping, women and men compete against each other in the same competition.
The Olympic equestrian events of 2008 took place not in Beijing but in Hong Kong.

teile.einleitung: Fabian Cancellara is a Swiss racing cyclist and one of the most successful bike racers in Switzerland. He was Olympic time trial champion twice and won many of the hardest one-day races in the world. Because of his strength and fighting spirit, he was called “Spartacus”.
wichtigste: Fabian Cancellara was born in 1981 in Wohlen near Bern.
His sport was road racing.
He became Olympic time trial champion in Beijing in 2008 and in Rio de Janeiro in 2016.
He was world champion in the individual time trial four times.
He won Paris-Roubaix three times and the Tour of Flanders three times.
At the Tour de France he often wore the yellow jersey.
He ended his professional career in 2016.

abschnitte.text: Fabian Cancellara was born on 18 March 1981 in **Wohlen near Bern**. His parents come from Italy, but he grew up in Switzerland. Even as a teenager he stood out for his speed. In 1998 and 1999 he became **junior world champion** in the time trial.

In a **time trial** each rider races alone against the clock. Cancellara was one of the best in the world at it for many years. He was world champion in this discipline in 2006, 2007, 2009 and 2010. At the Olympic Games in Beijing in 2008 and in Rio de Janeiro in 2016 he won gold each time.

Cancellara loved tough **classics**, famous one-day races. He won Paris-Roubaix, a race over bumpy cobbled roads, in 2006, 2010 and 2013. He won the Tour of Flanders in Belgium in 2010, 2013 and 2014. On top of that came victory in Milan-San Remo in 2008.

At the **Tour de France** Cancellara won several stages, mostly the time trials at the start. Because of this he was often allowed to wear the **yellow jersey** of the overall leader. Altogether he wore it for 29 days. No other rider who never won the Tour wore it for so long.

In 2016 Cancellara gave up professional racing; his last big victory was Olympic gold in Rio. After that he organised cycling events for amateur riders. Later he founded his own Swiss professional team, the Tudor Pro Cycling Team. Many young Swiss cyclists see him as a role model.

begriffe.erklaerung: A bike race in which each rider starts alone and the fastest time wins.
A famous, tough bike race that takes place on just one day.
The shirt worn at the Tour de France by the rider with the shortest overall time.
Someone who does their sport as their job.

gewusst: At the 2008 Olympic Games Cancellara also won a medal in the road race.
His nickname “Spartacus” comes from a famous fighter in ancient Rome.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss national curling teams represent Switzerland at world championships, European championships and the Olympic Games. Switzerland is one of the strongest curling nations in the world, especially in women’s curling. The sport is organised by the association Swiss Curling.
wichtigste: Curling is played on ice, with heavy granite stones and brooms.
The players sweep the ice in front of the stone with a broom.

abschnitte.text: In curling, two teams of four people play against each other. They slide heavy **curling stones** made of granite across the ice towards a target circle, the **house**. A stone weighs almost 20 kilograms. The team whose stones are closest to the centre at the end of a round scores points. Because you have to think a lot, curling is also called chess on ice.

In front of the gliding stone, the players sweep the ice with a **broom**. Sweeping makes the ice a little warmer, and the stone slides further and straighter. In this way the team can still influence the path of the stone. The person who decides the tactics is called the **skip**. They stand by the house and show where the stone should go.

Since curling became an Olympic sport again in 1998, Switzerland has won many medals. The men’s team led by skip **Patrick Hürlimann** won gold in Nagano in 1998. The women won silver in 2002 and 2006, among other medals. At the 2026 Olympic Games in Milan and Cortina, the Swiss women’s curling team again won **silver**. In mixed doubles, too, Switzerland won silver in 2018 with Jenny Perret and Martin Rios.

Especially successful is the women’s team from Aarau led by **Silvana Tirinzoni** and **Alina Pätz**. It became world champion in 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023; the 2020 World Championship was cancelled because of Covid. Before that, Swiss women such as Mirjam Ott and Binia Feltscher had already won world titles. The Swiss men have also won several world championship medals.

Curling originally comes from **Scotland**, where people played on frozen ponds in the 16th century. British guests brought the game to Swiss resorts such as St Moritz and Davos in the 19th century. Today there are many clubs and halls in Switzerland. The association **Swiss Curling** organises championships and supports young players. Curling is suitable for all age groups, including children and older people.

teile.einleitung: Vreni Schneider is a ski racer from Elm in the canton of Glarus. She won three Olympic gold medals and 55 World Cup races. In Switzerland she was voted Sportswoman of the Century.
wichtigste: Vreni Schneider was born on 26 November 1964 and comes from Elm in the canton of Glarus.
She won three Olympic gold medals.
In 1988 in Calgary she won the slalom and the giant slalom.
In 1994 in Lillehammer she again won gold in the slalom.
She celebrated 55 victories in the World Cup.
She won the overall World Cup three times.

abschnitte.text: Vreni Schneider comes from **Elm**, a mountain village in the canton of Glarus. She learnt to ski there as a little girl. The mountains around Elm were her first training ground. In the 1980s and 1990s she became one of the best ski racers in the world.

At the 1988 Olympic Games in **Calgary**, Vreni Schneider won gold in the slalom and the giant slalom. In 1994 in **Lillehammer** in Norway she won the slalom again. There she also won silver in the combined and bronze in the giant slalom. So altogether she won five Olympic medals, three of them gold.

Vreni Schneider won 55 races in the **World Cup**, mainly in slalom and giant slalom. In the 1988/89 season she won 14 races, which was a record for a long time. She won the overall World Cup in 1989, 1994 and 1995. She also became world champion several times.

Vreni Schneider is very popular in Switzerland. She was voted **Swiss Sportswoman of the Century**. Many people like her because she stayed modest and down to earth despite her successes. She ended her career in 1995.

After retiring, Vreni Schneider stayed in **Elm**. There she founded a ski school where children learn to ski. She still works for skiing and for her home region today. Elm is also known for the Martinsloch, a hole in the rock through which the sun shines onto the village twice a year.
